Fact.Name: Income sources supported
Fact.Description: Does Direct File support all of the income sources that you/you and your spouse have?

Fact.Name: Digital assets
Fact.Description: At any time during 2025, did you: (a) receive (as a reward, award, or payment for property or services) a digital asset (or a financial interest in a digital asset)?

Fact.Name: Digital assets
Fact.Description: At any time during 2025, did you sell, exchange, gift, or otherwise dispose of a digital asset (or a financial interest in a digital asset)?

Fact.Name: Not Digital Assets
Fact.Description: The TP did not receive receive or dispose of digital assets

Fact.Name: Every 2025 digital-asset disposition is either entered on Form 8949 or has nothing to report
Fact.Description:
SCREEN SPEC: the narrowing of /notDigitalAssets. The filer's attestation that the "yes" they gave to limb (b) of the Form 1040 digital-asset question is fully accounted for on this return even though this return carries no digital-asset Form 8949 row.
QUESTION TEXT, as it should be asked: "You told us you sold, exchanged, gifted or otherwise disposed of a digital asset in 2025, and you have not entered any digital-asset sale in your investment transactions. Is every one of those dispositions either already entered as an investment sale on this return, or one you have nothing to report for this year?"
HELP TEXT, paraphrasing the governing instruction with its cite: the 2025 Instructions for Form 1040 say that if you disposed of a digital asset you held as a capital asset "through a sale, trade, exchange, payment, or other transfer", you check "Yes" and "use Form 8949 to calculate your capital gain or loss and report that gain or loss on Schedule D" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040gi.pdf, page 16). But a "Yes" is required by several dispositions that produce NO Form 8949 row: a disposition BY GIFT (an inference, not a printed rule: the "check Yes" bullets at https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040gi.pdf, pages 15-16 do not name a gift; the nearest is "otherwise disposed of any other financial interest in a digital asset", and the Form 709 sentence sits in the reporting block at lines 874-880), where "you may be required to file Form 709" and nothing goes on this return (lines 874-880); and a disposal of a digital asset "that you held for sale to customers in a trade or business", which is reported "as you would report other income of the same type", i.e. on Schedule C rather than Form 8949 (lines 905-910). Answer YES if your 2025 dispositions were only of those kinds, or if you have already entered every reportable sale. Answer NO if you still have a sale, trade or exchange to enter.
ASKED WHEN: /disposedDigitalAssets is answered TRUE **and** the return carries no digital asset flagged Form 8949 row, i.e. scheduleD:/hasDigitalAssetForm8949Transactions is FALSE. Once the filer enters one digital-asset transaction this question stops being asked and its answer stops mattering, because /digitalAssetDispositionsAccountedFor is already TRUE on the transaction leg. It is NEVER asked of a filer who answered "no" or left the question blank.
UNANSWERED POSTURE: REFUSED. An unanswered attestation leaves /knockoutDigitalAssetYesWithNothingReported TRUE on the disposal limb and the return does not file. That is deliberate and is the data-completeness residue this unit keeps: a filer who says they disposed of a digital asset and enters neither a transaction nor this attestation has told us a reportable event happened and given us nothing to report, and filing that return would omit a capital gain. Nothing on the return is blank as a result; no printed cell reads this fact.
VALIDATION: Boolean, no Min or Max. The printed labels are the ordinary Yes and No.
WHAT THE ANSWER FEEDS: /digitalAssetDispositionsAccountedFor, and through it /knockoutDigitalAssetYesWithNothingReported, the flow:/flowIsKnockedOut member that replaced Not(/notDigitalAssets). It is a filing gate only: it moves no dollar, prints on no form and is not transmitted in the MeF return.

Fact.Name: The disposal half of the digital-asset answer is accounted for
Fact.Description:
TRUE when a "yes" to limb (b) of the Form 1040 digital-asset question has something behind it: either the return carries at least one Form 8949 transaction flagged as a digital asset (scheduleD:/hasDigitalAssetForm8949Transactions), or the filer answered TRUE to /writableNoUnenteredDigitalAssetDispositions, the attestation that the remaining dispositions are of the kinds that produce no Form 8949 row (a gift, which routes to Form 709, or dealer property, which routes to Schedule C).
COMPLETE SAFE BY CONSTRUCTION. The transaction leg is the IsComplete-guarded collection Bool, which is Complete FALSE on a return that never opened a Form 8949 section; the attestation leg is the All(IsComplete(x), x) fence, which is Complete FALSE while the writable is unanswered. The Any of two total Booleans is therefore total, so /knockoutDigitalAssetYesWithNothingReported can negate it without going Incomplete. The fence is used rather than a bare IsComplete because a bare IsComplete would file the return of a filer who answered NO, which is the opposite of what a NO means.
This fact says nothing about whether the 8949 rows are RIGHT or COMPLETE, only that the yes is not empty.

Fact.Name: Knockout when the digital-asset question is answered yes and nothing on the return backs it
Fact.Description:
The NARROWED successor of /notDigitalAssets as a member of flow:/flowIsKnockedOut .
WHAT USED TO REFUSE. flow.xml carried Not(/notDigitalAssets), which is Any(/receivedDigitalAssets, /disposedDigitalAssets): EVERY filer who answered yes to EITHER limb of the Form 1040 digital-asset question was refused, including the filer who then went on to enter the whole of it. Both halves the refusal was standing in for now ship and are consumed: the receipt half, /writableSchedule1Line8vDigitalAssetsOrdinaryIncome through /schedule1Line8vIncomeOrZero into Schedule 1 line 9, /otherIncome and /schedule1Line10AdditionalIncome, printing on Schedule 1 line 8v (IRS1040S1 f1_34) and Form 1040 line 8 (IRS1040 f1_72); and the disposal half, scheduleD:/form8949Transactions/*/isDigitalAsset through the Box G, H and I predicates (IRS8949 c1_1[3], [4], [5]) and the two nets onto Schedule D lines 7 and 15.
WHAT REFUSES NOW, and it is the data-completeness residue only. Two limbs, each fenced on its own answer:
RECEIPT LIMB. /receivedDigitalAssets is answered TRUE and /writableSchedule1Line8vDigitalAssetsOrdinaryIncome is UNANSWERED. The 8v intake carries a Min of $0, so a filer whose digital-asset receipts are all reported somewhere else answers it ZERO and files: the instructions route crypto paid as wages to Form 1040 line 1a and crypto received in a trade or business to Schedule C, and send only "ordinary income in connection with digital assets that isn't reported elsewhere on your return" to Schedule 1 line 8v (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040gi.pdf, page 16). ZERO IS AN ANSWER AND UNANSWERED IS NOT, which is why this limb tests IsComplete of the intake rather than its value. A second Boolean meaning "the 8v figure is zero" was REFUSED as a duplicate derivation of a quantity the intake already carries.
DISPOSAL LIMB. /disposedDigitalAssets is answered TRUE and /digitalAssetDispositionsAccountedFor is FALSE, that is the return carries no digital-asset Form 8949 row AND the filer has not attested that the remaining dispositions produce none. The attestation exists because a "yes" to limb (b) does NOT imply a Form 8949 row: a gift routes to Form 709 and off this return (lines 874-880) and dealer property routes to Schedule C (lines 905-910).
WHY THE RESIDUE IS THE CORRECT PERMANENT REFUSAL: a yes with nothing behind it is a filer telling us a reportable event happened and giving us nothing to report. Filing it omits the income, which is the under-report trap the contract names in terms; refusing it ends per return the moment the filer answers, never by a later dictionary edit.
COMPLETE SAFE BY CONSTRUCTION. Each limb opens with the All(IsComplete(x), x) fence on its own bare Boolean writable, so a return that has answered NEITHER question resolves this guard Complete FALSE rather than Incomplete, exactly as flow:/flowIsKnockedOut requires. The unanswered-question case is unchanged and still held where it always was, by /incomeSourcesIsComplete's IsComplete probe on /notDigitalAssets.
/notDigitalAssets IS NOT RETIRED AND ITS BODY IS UNCHANGED. It is not only a guard: it is bound to the Form 1040 "No" checkbox (dictionary/pdf/2025/IRS1040/en/configuration.yml, c1_10[1]) and it is the completeness probe inside /incomeSourcesIsComplete. It leaves flow.xml's Any and keeps both of those jobs.
NO COMMITTED RETURN MOVES. No scenario in scenarios/ answers either question yes, and the one committed fixture that does, asserts four income facts and no flow fact; it was refused before and is refused now, on the disposal limb. The freed and refused populations are witnessed only by this unit's fixtures.
DUAL-WIRED: this fact carries its own BlockSubmissionOnTrue beside its flow membership, on the /knockoutForeignAccountOrTrustAboveForm8938Threshold precedent. It cannot claim lint_dual_wiring's EXEMPT_INHERITED rule, which keys on a scope-sidecar citation reading "none - inherited IRS Direct File content": that exemption belongs to the predecessor /notDigitalAssets, whose sidecar row says exactly that, and this guard is newly authored with a real IRC 61 citation. The tag adds ONE entry to the generated submissionBlockingFacts and moves no value, because the guard is Complete FALSE on every committed return.

Fact.Name: Interest of signature authorization in a foreign financial account
Fact.Description: At any time during 2025, did you have a financial interest in or signature authority over a financial account located in a foreign country? Help: if you report a child's interest and dividends on Form 8814, answer yes also when that child had a foreign financial account; the parent then completes Schedule B Part III and files it with the return.

Fact.Name: Does not have interest of signature authorization in a foreign financial account
Fact.Description: Logical Negation of has foreign accounts

Fact.Name: Is the TP an owner, grantor, settler or trustor of a foreign trust?
Fact.Description: At any time during 2025, did you own a foreign trust? Help: if you report a child's interest and dividends on Form 8814, answer yes also when that child was the grantor of, or transferor to, a foreign trust.

Fact.Name: Did the TP have any transactions with a foreign trust?
Fact.Description: At any time during 2025, did you have a transaction with a foreign trust? Help: if you report a child's interest and dividends on Form 8814, answer yes also when that child received a distribution from a foreign trust.

Fact.Name: Is the TP an owner, grantor, settler or trustor of a foreign trust OR did the TP have any transactions with a foreign trust?
Fact.Description: Is the TP an owner, grantor, settler or trustor of a foreign trust OR did the TP have any transactions with a foreign trust?

Fact.Name: Is the TP NOT an owner, grantor, settler or trustor of a foreign trust AND did the TP NOT have any transactions with a foreign trust?
Fact.Description: Is the TP NOT an owner, grantor, settler or trustor of a foreign trust AND did the TP NOT have any transactions with a foreign trust?

The TP has interest in foreign accounts or foreign trusts
THIS FACT IS NOT ITSELF A flow:/flowIsKnockedOut MEMBER. It is the Schedule B Part III yes (line 7a or line 8); it feeds /doesNotHaveForeignAccountsOrTrusts and through it /incomeSourcesIsComplete, and its two writables still export the checkboxes. What changed is that it no longer refuses the return by itself; the refusal moved to /knockoutForeignAccountOrTrustAboveForm8938Threshold, directly below, which reads this fact and the return-level Form 8938 threshold answer together.

Fact.Name: Not foreign accounts nor foreign trusts
Fact.Description: The TP does not have interest in foreign accounts nor does the TP have interest in foreign trusts

Fact.Name: Knockout when Schedule B Part III answers yes and the return is above the Form 8938 threshold, or that threshold is unanswered
Fact.Description:
The narrowed successor of /hasForeignAccountsOrTrusts as a member of flow:/flowIsKnockedOut. It refuses the return only when the filer answered YES to Schedule B line 7a (a financial interest in or signature authority over a foreign financial account) or line 8 (foreign-trust grantor or foreign-trust transactions) AND the return-level Form 8938 threshold answer, read from the form8938 home module's pair form8938:/form8938ThresholdAnswered and form8938:/form8938AboveReportingThreshold, is ABOVE the threshold or UNANSWERED.
THE THREE OBLIGATIONS BEHIND A YES ARE SPLIT, per the contract's own re-derivation against the vendored Schedule B instructions, and two of the three stop refusing a federal return. (1) The FBAR, FinCEN Form 114, is filed with Treasury's Financial Crimes Enforcement Network and "Do not attach FinCEN Form 114 to your tax return" (i1040sb lines 260-268): a disclosure the filer owes elsewhere, which a refusal on this return is the wrong instrument for. Line 7a's second question and line 7b's country names are pure intakes and ship as /writableRequiredToFileFinCen114 and /writableScheduleBLine7bForeignCountries (with its second writing line), the Schedule B answers and NOT filers:/foreignCountryName, which is the mailing-address country. (2) Form 3520 is filed at its own address, "Don't attach Form 3520 to Form 1040 or Form 1040-SR" (lines 293-295), and Form 3520-A is the TRUST's filing (lines 296-299): the line 8 yes therefore refuses nothing on its own. (3) Form 8938 DOES attach to the return ("Attach Form 8938 to your annual return", i8938 lines 62-63), and only above the IRC 6038D reporting threshold, so it is the one leg that can still refuse.
WHAT IS FREED: the filer with a Schedule B Part III yes whose specified foreign financial assets are below the threshold that applies to them, or who has none at all (a foreign account can trip line 7a at any balance, and the lowest printed pair starts at $50,000). WHAT STILL REFUSES, two arms: (a) ABOVE the threshold, because a Form 8938 must accompany the return and this dictionary does not produce one, the build gap carried on the records overlay; (b) the threshold question UNANSWERED with a yes on 7a or 8, the asked-and-not- answered residue, which is the correct permanent refusal: nothing on Schedule B answers it and $0 is not a safe stand-in for an unknown asset total. Today the only screen that asks the threshold question is the Form 1099-R box 12 attestation, so a 7a-yes filer with no box 12 has no reachable answer until the form8938 aggregates are asked (INTAKE-GROUPS.md); that population refuses on arm (b), exactly as it refused before, and frees when the screen ships.
COMPLETE SAFE BY CONSTRUCTION: gated on IsComplete of /hasForeignAccountsOrTrusts, a real answered-ness predicate (that fact is an Any over two writables and is Incomplete until one is answered), so an unanswered Part III resolves FALSE here rather than Incomplete; the unanswered-Part-III case is already held by /incomeSourcesIsComplete. The threshold pair is read as Any(Not(answered), above), never the above fact alone, which is the trap the interest records contract names. This guard reads the form8938 pair DIRECTLY and never form1099Rs:/specifiedForeignFinancialAssetsAboveForm8938Threshold, whose box-12 gate makes it Complete FALSE, "below", on a return with no Form 1099-R.
NO COMMITTED RETURN MOVES: no fixture or scenario answers line 7a or line 8 yes, and schedule-b-neither-7a-nor-8-knockout-complete-safe-false and schedule-b-empty-return-knockout-complete-safe (the complete-safe floor). Consumer: flow:/flowIsKnockedOut (dictionary/ty2025/flow.xml), in the slot the Schedule B fact held. DUAL-WIRED: this fact carries its own BlockSubmissionOnTrue beside its flow membership, on the /knockoutForm8814ChildIncomeRequiresInclusion precedent, the most recent newly-authored knockout guard. This guard is newly authored content with a real IRC 6038D citation, so it cannot claim lint_dual_wiring's EXEMPT_INHERITED exemption (which keys on a scope-sidecar citation reading "none - inherited IRS Direct File content", true only of the predecessor /hasForeignAccountsOrTrusts); without the tag lint_dual_wiring fires membership-without-tag the moment the sidecar row lands. The tag adds ONE entry to the generated submissionBlockingFacts and moves no value: the guard is Complete FALSE on every committed return.
WHAT A FREED RETURN PRINTS TODAY, named rather than glossed (adversarial review MAJOR M1): a below-threshold 7a-yes return now files a Schedule B whose Part III line 7a question 2 (required to file FinCEN Form 114) and line 7b (the country names) are BLANK, because no screen asks /writableRequiredToFileFinCen114 or /writableScheduleBLine7bForeignCountries yet. That is a disclosure gap on a filed return, not a computation gap, and it is deliberately NOT made a refusal arm here: an arm on Not(IsComplete()) of those writables would re-refuse one hundred percent of the population this stage frees and make the narrowing vacuous.

Fact.Name: Made IRA contributions
Fact.Description: Whether the TP made contributions to an Individual Retirement Arrangement. Screen-completeness only — this answer does not refuse the return; see the block immediately above.

Fact.Name: Income sources complete
Fact.Description: The income sources sub-subsection is complete.

Fact.Name: Primary filer's household employee wages that no Form W-2 reported (Form 1040 line 1b)
Fact.Description:
The primary filer's attested total of wages he received as a household employee that were not reported on any Form W-2 — the figure Form 1040 line 1b asks for, verbatim: "Enter the total of your wages received as a household employee that was not reported on Form(s) W-2."
WHY THE POPULATION EXISTS AT ALL, and why this intake is the only door it has. The same instruction says an employer "isn't required to provide a Form W-2 to you if they paid you wages of less than $2,800 in 2025", so a household employee under that figure has NO Form W-2 to enter on line 1a. Before this intake existed both line-1b legs were a bare Derived Dollar 0 with no writable anywhere on their path, so those wages reached no line of the return at all: the return under-stated taxable income AND under-stated earned income, under-claiming the EITC and the CDCC for the same filer, in two opposite directions at once.
THE $2,800 IS NOT A CAP AND IS NOT A CONDITION ON THIS FACT. It is a Form W-2 ISSUANCE rule addressed to the employer; the line's own text has no limit attached, and a household employee paid MORE than $2,800 whose employer issued no Form W-2 enters the whole amount here. Pinned by tests/nodes/ty2025/income/line1b-household-employee-wages-above-2800-not-capped, which is the reason that case exists.
OPTIONAL (three-state): a filer who was never a household employee never answers it, and /primaryFilerUnreportedHouseholdWages resolves $0 through the IsComplete/Switch wrapper rather than through a Placeholder — an unanswered intake stays UNANSWERED here, and only the derived leg is complete-safe. Re-creating the old false zero on the writable itself is exactly the defect this fill closes.

Fact.Name: Secondary filer's household employee wages that no Form W-2 reported (Form 1040 line 1b)
Fact.Description: Secondary-filer twin of /writablePrimaryFilerUnreportedHouseholdWages. Separate because the two spouses' wage lines stay separate all the way up to the per-filer earned-income subtotals that the EITC and Form 2441 read; only the printed line 1b pools them.

Fact.Name: Primary filer's Household employee wages not reported on Form(s) W-2 (Form 1040 line 1b)
Fact.Description:
Primary filer's share of Form 1040 line 1b, printed "Household employee wages not reported on Form(s) W-2".
NO LONGER A STRUCTURAL ZERO. This fact was a bare Derived Dollar 0 with no writable anywhere on its path, so no return this dictionary could represent carried any line 1b amount. It now reads /writablePrimaryFilerUnreportedHouseholdWages through the IsComplete/Switch wrapper, so the intake's own completeness stops here: unanswered resolves a literal $0, which is unconditionally Complete, and /primaryFilerEmployerIncomeSubtotalBase stays Complete for every return that does not attest such wages. A bare Dependency on an unanswered writable would instead propagate Incomplete up through line 1z into AGI — a completeness regression far larger than the value fix.
THE ROUND IS THE PRINTED-LINE BOUNDARY, and it sits here rather than on the Add below for the same reason it sits on form8919:/primaryFilerForm8919Line6 and form4137's line 4 — the two nearest addends of the very same subtotal. Line 1b is a printed Form 1040 line and the page-23 rounding election ("You can round off cents to whole dollars on your return and schedules") reaches it; the filer's own entry is a whole-dollar figure. Rounding one attested amount per filer cannot introduce the sum-of-rounded-addends error line 1a guards against, because there is nothing here to aggregate. Round of a Complete value is Complete, and /employerIncomeSubtotal's own Round is then idempotent.

Fact.Name: Secondary filer's Household employee wages not reported on Form(s) W-2 (Form 1040 line 1b)
Fact.Description: Secondary-filer twin of /primaryFilerUnreportedHouseholdWages, reading /writableSecondaryFilerUnreportedHouseholdWages. Likewise no longer a structural zero and likewise complete-safe $0 on every return that does not attest such wages. See the primary twin for the completeness argument and for why the Round sits at this leg.

Fact.Name: Unreported household wages
Fact.Description:
Form 1040 line 1b, printed "Household employee wages not reported on Form(s) W-2" — the per-filer legs summed.
THE LINE COMPUTES. What it recorded was a silent wrong answer rather than a deferral: both per-filer legs were hard-coded $0 with no writable anywhere on their path, so no return this dictionary could represent carried any line 1b amount, and nothing refused the population either. Both legs now read per-filer writable intakes (/writablePrimaryFilerUnreportedHouseholdWages and its secondary twin) through the IsComplete/Switch wrapper.
THE DIRECTION THAT ROW NAMED, now closed on both limbs. Line 1b is taxable wages, so the zero UNDER-STATED income and therefore tax — the taxpayer-favorable, IRS-adverse direction. The population is real and specifically defined by the instruction: an employer "isn't required to provide a Form W-2 to you if they paid you wages of less than $2,800 in 2025", so for a filer under that figure this line is the ONLY route by which the wages reach the return. And the SECOND CONSUMER carried the opposite sign: the same legs reach /primaryFilerEmployerIncomeSubtotalBase and its secondary twin (both Export downstreamFacts), the per-filer wage subtotals earned-income consumers read, where the zero UNDER-STATED earned income and under-claimed EITC and CDCC for that same filer. Because the fill went in at the two per-filer legs, both limbs move together by construction; the earned-income movement is witnessed by tests/nodes/ty2025/income/line1b-household-employee-wages-reach-line-1-and-earned-income.
NO ROUND HERE: each leg already rounds at its own printed-line boundary (see /primaryFilerUnreportedHouseholdWages), and /employerIncomeSubtotal rounds the line-1z total once more. California TY2025 reads this fact through its stateSystems export (Schedule CA (540), Schedule CA (540NR)).

Fact.Name: Primary filer's unreported tip income (Form 1040 line 1c)
Fact.Description:
Primary filer's tip income not reported to the employer, and so not inside Form W-2 box 1 — Form 1040 line 1c. Reads form4137:/primaryFilerForm4137Line4 (Form 4137 line 2 less line 3), the figure that form's own line 4 routes to line 1c.
This fact feeds /primaryFilerEmployerIncomeSubtotalBase (exported) → /employerIncomeSubtotal → Form 1040 line 1z → AGI, and from there the EITC and CDCC earned income. It is complete-safe at $0: every Form 4137 line above it is complete-safe (an unanswered intake resolves $0 rather than Incomplete).

Fact.Name: Secondary filer's unreported tip income (Form 1040 line 1c)
Fact.Description: Secondary filer's twin of /primaryFilerUnreportedTipIncome, reading form4137:/secondaryFilerForm4137Line4. Form 4137 is filed per spouse, so the two legs are separate all the way up to /unreportedTipIncome. Complete-safe at $0 on every committed scenario.

Fact.Name: Unreported tip income
Fact.Description:
Tip income not reported on line 1a
Form 1040, (line 1c). California TY2025 reads this fact through its stateSystems export (Schedule CA (540), Schedule CA (540NR)).

Fact.Name: Primary filer's TAXABLE Medicaid waiver payments not reported in Form W-2 box 1 (Form 1040 line 1d)
Fact.Description:
The primary filer's attested total of TAXABLE Medicaid waiver payments that were not reported in box 1 of any Form W-2 — the figure Form 1040 line 1d asks for: "Enter your taxable Medicaid waiver payments that were not reported on" Form(s) W-2, box 1.
SPELLING NOTE FOR THE GREP: the derived legs this intake feeds carry the INHERITED misspelling /primaryFilerMedicareWaiverPayments ("Medicare" for "Medicaid"). Those paths are not renamed here — renaming a shipping fact is not this unit's business — so a search for either spelling must expect the other.
THE 1099-MISC / 1099-NEC ROUTE LANDS HERE, deliberately. The instruction directs a filer who does NOT have a separate trade or business of providing home care services to "enter on Form 1040, line 1d, your Medicaid waiver payments reported on Form 1099-MISC or Form 1099-NEC" — so those documents reach the return through this line and no other. This one intake therefore collects both the no-Form-W-2 case and the 1099-MISC/1099-NEC home-care case, because the printed line does not distinguish them. THE SOLE-PROPRIETOR FORK IS NOT MODELLED: a filer who IS "a sole proprietor in a business of providing home care services" is sent to the Schedule C instructions instead, and nothing in this graph asks that question or routes such a filer away from this line. The W-2 code II calculation bridge is built: those amounts are automatically added to this filer's per-filer total. A positive Code II amount still activates the submission refusal until IRSW2 generator support and guard release are built; the separate Schedule C sole-proprietor fork also remains open.
TAXABLE ONLY. Nontaxable §131 payments are collected separately at /writablePrimaryFilerSchedule1Line8sNontaxableMedicaidWaiverPayments, combined into this filer's line 1d/line 1z amount, and backed out on Schedule 1 line 8s. The per-spouse EIC Step-5 choice and subtrahend are built in eitc.xml and the external block 17 D4 record. This writable itself still collects taxable payments only.
OPTIONAL (three-state): unanswered stays UNANSWERED at this intake, and only the derived leg is complete-safe at $0 — no Placeholder, because a false zero is precisely the defect being closed.

Fact.Name: Secondary filer's TAXABLE Medicaid waiver payments not reported in Form W-2 box 1 (Form 1040 line 1d)
Fact.Description: Secondary-filer twin of /writablePrimaryFilerTaxableMedicaidWaiverPayments. Separate because the two spouses' amounts stay separate up to the per-filer earned-income subtotals — and because the instruction makes the spouses separable in their own right on this line: "If you and your spouse both received nontaxable Medicaid waiver payments during the year, you and your spouse can make different choices about including payments in earned income." The nontaxable amount now has its own input at /writableSecondaryFilerSchedule1Line8sNontaxableMedicaidWaiverPayments and its own EIC Step-5 choice in eitc.xml. It feeds the secondary filer's line 1d/line 1z leg and derived Schedule 1 line 8s back-out. The separate Schedule C sole-proprietor fork and the positive-Code-II schema/generator plus guard-release boundary remain open; the calculation bridge is built.

Fact.Name: Primary filer's nontaxable Medicaid waiver payments included in Form 1040 income (Schedule 1 line 8s)
Fact.Description:
The primary filer's positive-dollar nontaxable Medicaid waiver amount included in Form 1040 income and backed out on Schedule 1 line 8s. This per-filer amount is one of two sole sources of the signed return-level line 8s value. Form 1040 line 1d includes nontaxable amounts when elected for a credit or other tax benefit. The amount therefore enters the primary filer's line 1d and line 1z legs as well as the Schedule 1 back-out.
Enter only nontaxable Medicaid waiver payments from sources OTHER THAN a Form W-2 box 12, code II. Code II amounts are read from each W-2 and added automatically; including those amounts here would double-count them.
OPTIONAL: unanswered is complete-safe $0. A separately answered secondary-filer intake lets spouses report and elect independently.

Fact.Name: Secondary filer's nontaxable Medicaid waiver payments included in Form 1040 income (Schedule 1 line 8s)
Fact.Description: Secondary-filer twin of /writablePrimaryFilerSchedule1Line8sNontaxableMedicaidWaiverPayments. The separate amount preserves the instruction's permission for spouses to make different choices. Enter only nontaxable Medicaid waiver payments from sources OTHER THAN a Form W-2 box 12, code II; code II amounts are read from each W-2 and added automatically, so do not include them here.

Fact.Name: Primary filer's Form W-2 box 12 code II Medicaid waiver amounts, complete-safe total
Fact.Description: Unrounded sum of the primary filer's nontaxable Medicaid waiver amounts reported in Form W-2 box 12, code II. These source amounts are automatically combined with the additional non-Code-II amount asked at /writablePrimaryFilerSchedule1Line8sNontaxableMedicaidWaiverPayments, so a W-2 amount must not be entered a second time there. The source retains cents until the combined Form 1040 line 1d and Schedule 1 line 8s totals are rounded at their printed lines. A return with no completed W-2 collection resolves to $0.

Fact.Name: Secondary filer's Form W-2 box 12 code II Medicaid waiver amounts, complete-safe total
Fact.Description: Secondary-filer twin of /primaryFilerCodeIIMedicaidWaiverPayments, summing only the secondary filer's Forms W-2. It preserves the spouse-specific amount and cents until the combined printed line totals are rounded. A return with no completed W-2 collection resolves to $0.

Fact.Name: Primary filer's nontaxable Medicaid waiver payments, complete-safe
Fact.Description: The primary filer's additional non-Code-II amount entered for Schedule 1 line 8s, plus automatically read Code II W-2 amounts, complete-safe. It keeps the line 1d and line 1z paths complete-safe.

Fact.Name: Secondary filer's nontaxable Medicaid waiver payments, complete-safe
Fact.Description: The secondary filer's additional non-Code-II amount plus automatically read Code II W-2 amounts, complete-safe. The secondary-filer twin of /primaryFilerSchedule1Line8sNontaxableMedicaidWaiverPaymentsOrZero.

Fact.Name: Primary filer's Medicaid waiver payments not reported on Form(s) W-2 (Form 1040 line 1d)
Fact.Description: Primary filer's unrounded line-1d/line-1z addend: the taxable line-1d intake plus the additional non-Code-II amount and automatically read Code II W-2 amounts included in Form 1040 income. Cents are preserved here; Form 1040 line 1d rounds the combined filer amounts once, and line 1z rounds its combined total once. The fact's path keeps its inherited "Medicare" misspelling of "Medicaid"; the intakes are spelled correctly.

Fact.Name: Secondary filer's Medicaid waiver payments not reported on Form(s) W-2 (Form 1040 line 1d)
Fact.Description: Secondary-filer twin of /primaryFilerMedicareWaiverPayments: the unrounded line-1d/line-1z addend, including taxable intake, additional non-Code-II amount, and automatically read Code II W-2 amounts, preserving cents until the combined printed Form 1040 line is rounded once.

Fact.Name: Medicare Waiver Payments
Fact.Description:
Form 1040 line 1d, printed "Medicaid waiver payments not reported on Form(s) W-2 (see instructions)", adds the primary and secondary unrounded line 1d legs and rounds the combined printed amount once. Each leg includes its taxable line-1d intake, additional non-Code-II nontaxable amount, and automatically read Form W-2 box 12 code II amount.
The per-filer nontaxable amounts also derive the signed Schedule 1 line 8s back-out. The amount remains neutral to AGI because line 8s subtracts the included nontaxable amount, while each spouse's own EIC Step-5 choice determines whether their share stays in EIC earned income. The EITC pair and Step-5 behavior are built in block 17 D4.
The separate sole-proprietor route remains unmodelled: a filer in a home-care business is sent to Schedule C instructions, but this graph does not detect or route that case. California TY2025 reads this fact through its stateSystems export (Schedule CA (540), Schedule CA (540NR)).

Fact.Name: Taxable Dependent Care
Fact.Description: Taxable dependent care benefits from Form 2441 (line 1e). California TY2025 reads this fact through its stateSystems export (Schedule CA (540), Schedule CA (540NR)).

Primary filer's Employer-provided adoption benefits from Form 8839 (line 1f): this filer's share of form8839:/adoptionLine31TaxableBenefits.
WHY THIS READS A DISREGARDING-SECTION-137 MAGI BASE RATHER THAN adoptionLine31TaxableBenefits DIRECTLY. A direct wire is CIRCULAR: line 1f raises /totalIncome, /totalIncome raises /agi, /agi raises form8839:/adoptionMagi, which raises /adoptionExclusionMagi, the line 26/27/28 phaseout, line 30 and therefore line 31 itself. What the wire needs first is an adoption MAGI base that omits the line 1f adoption legs by construction, the way /totalIncomeUpperBoundForIraMagi is built for the section 219(g) MAGI. Sections 86(b)(2)(A) and 219(g)(3)(A)(ii) define their MAGIs "without regard to" section 137, so socialSecurity, iraDeduction, cdcc, scheduleE and /totalIncomeUpperBoundForIraMagi read a line 1z figure DISREGARDING SECTION 137 (/employerIncomeSubtotalDisregardingSection137, /totalIncomeDisregardingSection137); section 221(b)(2)(C)(ii) is handled by dropping the student loan add-back rather than re-pointing it; and the two per-filer earned-income bases (/primaryFilerEarnedIncomeBaseWithStatutoryEmployeeWages and its twin) read the EXCLUDING base. The authority for threading each consumer is set out on form8839:/adoptionLine31TaxableBenefits. The blocker is not the per-filer split alone; the split is real, because these legs are per-filer EARNED INCOME through /primaryFilerEmployerIncomeSubtotalBase, and its recipe is on the form8839 fact, but it is the cheap half of the work. scripts/find_dependency_cycle.py confirms the graph is acyclic (apart from two pre-existing Schedule H self-references).
THE SPLIT. Form 8839 has no filer axis — /form8839Children/*/employerAdoptionBenefits is per child, per return — and the only place the return says whose employer paid is Form W-2 box 12 code T, because a W-2 belongs to exactly one filer. So line 31 is APPORTIONED across the filers in proportion to their box 12 code T totals (formW2s:/primaryFilerAdoptionBenefitsBox12CodeT and its twin), and falls whole to the primary filer when no W-2 reports code T. That is the minimal correct shape the form8839 fact wrote down, built as recorded.
THE PAIR SUMS TO LINE 31 EXACTLY, by construction rather than by rounding luck: the SECONDARY leg takes the rounded proportional share and THIS leg is line 31 minus that share. A pair of independently rounded shares could miss line 31 by a dollar, and Form 1040 line 1f is a printed line that must equal Form 8839 line 31.
SIGNED, NOT FLOORED, and this is a deliberate reading of two printed texts against a third. Form 8839 line 31's Yes branch reads "Subtract line 23 from line 30. Enter the result as a negative number. Also, enter the result on line 1f of Form 1040, 1040-SR, or 1040-NR", and the Form 1040 instruction for line 1f says only "Enter the total of your employer-provided adoption benefits from Form 8839, line 31" with no floor. A negative line 1f therefore REDUCES wages, and that is the section 137(a)(2) special-needs mechanism working as intended: a special-needs adoption that became final in 2025 excludes the full per-child limit whether or not the employer paid that much, so the excess exclusion has to leave income somewhere and line 1f is where the form puts it. CONTRARY TEXT, disclosed: the shipping Description on form8839:/adoptionLine31TaxableBenefits says the Yes branch "must not reduce wages", and the i8839 Exclusion of Prior Year Benefits Worksheet line 6 does floor at -0- — but that worksheet is the FOREIGN-CHILD prior-year route and replaces line 31 only for that population, so it does not govern the main form. The printed main form wins.
COMPLETE-SAFE. form8839:/adoptionLine31TaxableBenefits is $0 on any return that never declared /form8839Children (both of its operands gate on IsComplete of that collection), so this leg is a Complete $0 on every return without a Form 8839 — which is every committed scenario. No IsComplete guard is added here for the same reason the module refuses one on complete-safe facts: the gate already exists, one layer up, on a real predicate.

Secondary filer's employer-provided adoption benefits from Form 8839 (line 1f). This leg is the secondary filer's SHARE of form8839:/adoptionLine31TaxableBenefits, apportioned by box 12 code T: Round(line 31 x secondary code T / total code T), and $0 when no W-2 on the return reports code T. The primary leg is then line 31 MINUS this one, so the pair sums to line 31 exactly and Form 1040 line 1f equals Form 8839 line 31 to the dollar. The full reading — why the W-2 is the only filer-bearing record of this money, why the amount is signed rather than floored, and what the three-stage cycle recipe did — is on /primaryFilerEmployerProvidedAdoptionBenefits.
WHY THE SECONDARY LEG IS THE ROUNDED ONE and the primary leg is the remainder: some leg has to absorb the rounding residue, and defaulting the whole amount to the PRIMARY filer when there is no code T at all is the recorded fallback, so making the primary leg the residual keeps one rule for both cases.
COMPLETE-SAFE: the Switch's catch-all is a literal $0, and both weights are complete-safe CollectionSums over complete-safe per-W-2 amounts, so this fact is Complete on every return.

NO LONGER A STRUCTURAL ZERO. BYTE-IDENTICAL ON THE COMMITTED CORPUS, and as with the tip legs the property that matters is COMPLETENESS. This feeds /primaryFilerEmployerIncomeSubtotalBase (exported) → /employerIncomeSubtotal → Form 1040 line 1z → AGI → the EITC and CDCC earned income. The old body was unconditionally Complete at $0 and the replacement is Complete at $0 too, because every Form 8919 line is complete-safe.

Fact.Name: Secondary filer's wages from Form 8919 (Form 1040 line 1g)
Fact.Description: Secondary filer's twin of /primaryFilerWagesFrom8919, reading form8919:/secondaryFilerForm8919Line6. Form 8919 is filed per spouse, so the two legs stay separate up to /wagesFrom8919. Likewise complete-safe $0 on every committed scenario.

Fact.Name: Wages From 8919
Fact.Description: Wages from Form 8919 (line 1g). California TY2025 reads this fact through its stateSystems export (Schedule CA (540), Schedule CA (540NR)).

Fact.Name: Primary filer's elective deferrals subject to the IRC 402(g) limit
Fact.Description: The primary filer's total, over every Form W-2 attributed to that filer, of the box 12 amounts that are elective deferrals under IRC 402(g)(3) or designated Roth contributions IRC 402A(a)(1) treats as such: codes D, E, F, S, AA and BB. The TY2025 Form 1040 instructions measure the line 1h test over "all plans", so the test is per FILER and across employers, never per W-2. Codes G and EE (457(b)) and code H (501(c)(18)(D)) are excluded upstream in formW2s:/formW2s/*/electiveDeferralsSubjectTo402gLimit, which states the statutory reason for each. NAMED GAP: a deferral made to a plan of an employer that issued no Form W-2 in this dictionary, or a deferral reported on a prior-year USERRA make-up line, is invisible here, so the total can only ever be too LOW. COMPLETE SAFE: the CollectionSum sits inside an IsComplete Switch on the formW2s:/formW2s collection defaulting to $0, so a return that never opened the Form W-2 section resolves Complete $0 rather than Placeholder. That matters beyond this fact: the sum feeds the line 1h excess, which is an addend of /primaryFilerOtherEarnedIncome and so of /otherEarnedIncome, the PDF-bound Form 1040 line 1h — an unguarded sum took that printed line Placeholder on every return with no Forms W-2.

Fact.Name: Primary filer's designated Roth contributions inside the 402(g) total
Fact.Description: The primary filer's box 12 code AA and code BB total. IRC 402(g)(1)(A) subjects designated Roth contributions to the limit but withholds the gross-income inclusion for so much of the excess as does not exceed them, because those amounts are already in box 1 of the Form W-2. Subtracted from the excess in /primaryFilerExcessElectiveDeferralsOnLine1h. COMPLETE SAFE: the CollectionSum sits inside an IsComplete Switch on the formW2s:/formW2s collection defaulting to $0, so a return that never opened the Form W-2 section resolves Complete $0 rather than Placeholder. That matters beyond this fact: the sum feeds the line 1h excess, which is an addend of /primaryFilerOtherEarnedIncome and so of /otherEarnedIncome, the PDF-bound Form 1040 line 1h — an unguarded sum took that printed line Placeholder on every return with no Forms W-2.

Fact.Name: Primary filer's 402(g) elective deferrals outside a SIMPLE plan
Fact.Description: The primary filer's total of the 402(g) codes other than code S. Zero here beside a positive /primaryFilerElectiveDeferrals402g is this dictionary's reading of the TY2025 Form 1040 instructions' "if you have only SIMPLE plans". COMPLETE SAFE: the CollectionSum sits inside an IsComplete Switch on the formW2s:/formW2s collection defaulting to $0, so a return that never opened the Form W-2 section resolves Complete $0 rather than Placeholder. That matters beyond this fact: the sum feeds the line 1h excess, which is an addend of /primaryFilerOtherEarnedIncome and so of /otherEarnedIncome, the PDF-bound Form 1040 line 1h — an unguarded sum took that printed line Placeholder on every return with no Forms W-2.

Fact.Name: Primary filer defers only under SIMPLE plans
Fact.Description: True when the primary filer has at least one dollar of 402(g) elective deferrals and every one of them is a box 12 code S SIMPLE contribution. Selects the $16,500 base limit and the SIMPLE catch-up figures instead of the $23,500 base limit and the general catch-up figures. False (so the higher limit applies) whenever the filer has no deferrals at all, which keeps a filer with nothing to test off the lower limit.

Fact.Name: Primary filer's base IRC 402(g) elective-deferral limit
Fact.Description: The applicable dollar amount under IRC 402(g)(1)(B) as indexed for 2025, $23,500 — or $16,500 where /primaryFilerHasOnlySimpleElectiveDeferrals402g is true. NOT MODELLED, and both directions are named: the $26,500 limit for a section 403(b) plan where the filer qualifies for the Pub. 571 15-year rule (this fact gives $23,500 instead, which OVER-includes income), and the $17,600 limit available to participants in certain SIMPLE plans (this fact gives $16,500 instead, which also OVER-includes). Neither condition is on the Form W-2 and neither has an intake question in this dictionary.

Fact.Name: Primary filer's IRC 414(v) catch-up allowance
Fact.Description: The amount by which the primary filer's base 402(g) limit is raised before the line 1h excess is measured. The TY2025 Form 1040 instructions exclude catch-up contributions from the $23,500 test and state that the additional deferral is not subject to the overall limit on elective deferrals, and the employer reports the catch-up inside the SAME box 12 code as the ordinary deferral, so the only way to honour the exclusion against a box 12 total is to raise the limit by the allowance. $7,500 at age 50 or older; $11,250 for a filer aged 60 to 63 at the end of 2025; $3,500 and $5,250 respectively where the filer defers only under SIMPLE plans. Age is the ordinary end-of-year age filers:/filers/*/age computes, which is the anniversary rule IRC 414(v)'s "before the close of the taxable year" test takes. UNANSWERED DATE OF BIRTH gives $0, so the base limit stands and the return over-includes rather than under-includes. That is the adverse-safe direction, and it is the whole of the claim made here: NO guard in this dictionary was found that refuses a return whose date of birth is unanswered, so the state is reachable and is defaulted rather than refused. NOT MODELLED: the $3,850 catch-up available to certain SIMPLE participants, which the Form W-2 cannot distinguish.

Fact.Name: Primary filer's IRC 402(g) elective-deferral limit as tested on line 1h
Fact.Description: The primary filer's base 402(g) limit raised by the IRC 414(v) catch-up allowance. Pub. 560 prints the same arithmetic for the general case: $23,500 base plus the $7,500 age 50 catch-up is the $31,000 above which a catch-up-eligible participant's deferrals are excess.

Fact.Name: Primary filer's excess elective deferrals
Fact.Description: The primary filer's 402(g) elective deferrals over that filer's limit, floored at zero. This is the "excess deferral" of IRC 402(g)(2) BEFORE the designated Roth carve-out; the amount that reaches Form 1040 line 1h is /primaryFilerExcessElectiveDeferralsOnLine1h.

Fact.Name: Primary filer's excess elective deferrals included on Form 1040 line 1h
Fact.Description: The primary filer's excess elective deferrals less that filer's designated Roth contributions, floored at zero — the amount the TY2025 Form 1040 instructions put in the line 1h total. THE INCLUSION IS UNCONDITIONAL: neither the instructions nor IRC 402(g) makes it depend on whether the plan returned the excess by April 15, 2026. IRC 402(g)(2)(C) excludes the corrective DISTRIBUTION from gross income (taxing only the income on it, in the year distributed), and Pub. 560 states both branches in the same terms — taken out by April 15 the excess "isn't reported again ... for 2026", left in the plan it is "though taxable in 2025" taxed a second time on eventual distribution. So there is no April 15 intake question here and no adverse default to set. THE PRIOR-YEAR CORRECTIVE-DISTRIBUTION LEG IS NOW BUILT: current-year Code 8 box 2a from a non-IRA Form 1099-R flows through /primaryFilerCorrectiveDistributionsOfExcessDeferralsOnLine1h. Code P is a prior-year distribution and contributes zero to TY2025 line 1h.

Fact.Name: Primary filer's strike or lockout benefits (Form 1040 line 1h)
Fact.Description:
The primary filer's strike or lockout benefits received in 2025, other than a bona fide gift.
QUESTION TEXT: "Did you receive any strike or lockout benefits in 2025 from a union? If so, how much (other than a bona fide gift)? Include the fair market value of any non-cash benefits, such as goods or property, as well as cash."
HELP TEXT, paraphrasing the governing instruction: the 2025 Instructions for Form 1040 list "Strike or lockout benefits (other than bona fide gifts)" as one of the amounts that "must be included in the total on line 1h" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040gi.pdf, page 24). Publication 525 states the measure: benefits paid by a union as strike or lockout benefits, "including both cash and the FMV of other property, are usually included in your income as compensation," excludable only "when the facts clearly show that the union intended them as gifts to you" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/p525.pdf, page 36). No information return reports this payment, so the amount — cash plus the fair market value of any non-cash benefit — is the filer's own figure. Enter $0, or leave this blank, if you received none.
ASKED WHEN: every primary filer, unconditionally — there is no upstream fact that could gate the question (no document this dictionary models carries a strike-or-lockout box), matching the sibling Armed Forces excess-reimbursement writable's own ungated shape.
VALIDATION: Dollar, Min $0. No maximum.
UNANSWERED POSTURE: blank on the return; NOTHING IS REFUSED. /primaryFilerStrikeOrLockoutBenefitsOrZero is this writable's complete-safe wrapper, $0 when unanswered — the ordinary posture for every other Form 1040 line 1h leg this module already ships (the disability-pension and IRC 402(g) excess-deferral legs, and the Armed-Forces excess-reimbursement leg). UNANSWERED MEANS "none received", which is the favourable AND correct default for a benefit most filers never receive.
WHAT THE ANSWER FEEDS: /primaryFilerStrikeOrLockoutBenefitsOrZero, an addend of /primaryFilerOtherEarnedIncome (a term of /otherEarnedIncome, printed Form 1040 line 1h) and so, through it, of every subtotal that reads that per-filer base — line 1z, total income and AGI.

Fact.Name: Primary filer's strike or lockout benefits, complete safe
Fact.Description: The complete-safe wrapper of /writablePrimaryFilerStrikeOrLockoutBenefits: the filer's answer when it was answered, and $0 otherwise. Read by /primaryFilerOtherEarnedIncome. The intake is a bare Writable, so a raw Dependency on it would make line 1h, line 1z, AGI and every figure built from them Incomplete on every return that did not answer this one optional question; this wrapper is the same complete-safe Switch idiom /form1040Line1hArmedForcesMovingExpenseExcessReimbursementOrZero already uses on the same printed line. $0 on every scenario in scenarios/, none of which answers the intake, so line 1h, line 1z and AGI are byte identical there.

Fact.Name: Secondary filer's strike or lockout benefits (Form 1040 line 1h)
Fact.Description: The secondary-filer twin of /writablePrimaryFilerStrikeOrLockoutBenefits — see it for the question text (including the fair-market-value-of-non-cash-benefits instruction), help text, validation and unanswered posture, which are identical. WHAT THE ANSWER FEEDS: /secondaryFilerStrikeOrLockoutBenefitsOrZero, an addend of /secondaryFilerOtherEarnedIncome.

Fact.Description: The complete-safe wrapper of /writableSecondaryFilerStrikeOrLockoutBenefits — the secondary-filer twin of /primaryFilerStrikeOrLockoutBenefitsOrZero. Read by /secondaryFilerOtherEarnedIncome. $0 on every scenario in scenarios/, none of which answers the intake.

Fact.Name: Primary filer's Form 1099-R corrective distributions of prior-year excess deferrals on Form 1040 line 1h
Fact.Description: Sum of this filer's current-year Code 8, non-IRA Form 1099-R box 2a amounts, retaining cents across forms. Code P is a prior-year distribution code and contributes zero to TY2025 line 1h. IRA distributions are reported on lines 4a and 4b, not here. A Code 8 item with an unresolved IRA classification or an unanswered taxable amount is refused by form1099Rs:/knockoutForForm1099RCorrectiveDistributionInputs.

Fact.Name: Secondary filer's Form 1099-R corrective distributions of prior-year excess deferrals on Form 1040 line 1h
Fact.Description: The MFJ secondary-filer twin of /primaryFilerCorrectiveDistributionsOfExcessDeferralsOnLine1h, retaining cents across forms. Outside MFJ or while filing status is unanswered, this leg is complete-safe zero.

Fact.Name: Form 1040 line 1h — corrective distributions of excess deferrals
Fact.Description: The TY2025 total of eligible Code 8 box 2a amounts from non-IRA Form 1099-Rs, for both filers on a joint return. Code P distributions are prior-year and contribute zero. The per-filer amounts are integrated into the respective other-earned-income bases, so the total line 1h and earned-income path carry each distribution once.

Fact.Name: Primary filer's section 1402(c)(2)(C) wages were also reported on a Form W-2
Fact.Description: SCREEN: "Were those foreign-government or international-organization wages also reported in box 1 of a Form W-2?" HELP TEXT: Line 1a takes Form W-2 box 1. If no Form W-2 was issued, the same wages are other earned income on line 1h. Enter only wages on which no U.S. social security or Medicare tax was withheld. A wholly owned instrumentality counts only in certain cases: section 3121(b)(12) requires service similar to U.S. Government service abroad and a Secretary of State equivalent-exemption certification. A Federal employee transferred to an international organization under 5 U.S.C. 3582 who keeps a reemployment right stays in ordinary FICA employment under section 3121(y) and belongs on neither this screen nor Schedule SE. ASKED WHEN: the primary's entered foreign-government wages are positive, whether the services were performed in the United States, a listed possession, or elsewhere. UNANSWERED POSTURE: Incomplete on line 1h for positive wages. VALIDATION: Boolean.

Fact.Name: Primary filer's Form W-2 for those wages withheld social security or Medicare tax
Fact.Description: SCREEN: "Did that Form W-2 withhold social security tax (box 4) or Medicare tax (box 6)?" HELP TEXT: foreign-government and international-organization wages belong on Schedule SE only when FICA was not withheld. A FICA-withheld Form W-2 entered here would pay SE tax on top of FICA, because Schedule SE line 8a offsets only the OASDI cap. ASKED WHEN: those wages were also on a Form W-2 and services were not explicitly performed outside the Schedule SE geography. UNANSWERED POSTURE: Incomplete on line 1h on that active route. An answered Yes triggers the existing domestic FICA-conflict guard; wages explicitly outside the Schedule SE geography do not require this answer for line 1h.

Fact.Name: Primary filer's section 1402(c)(2)(C) wages on Form 1040 line 1h
Fact.Description: The primary filer's gross foreign-government employee wages not reported on Form W-2, included on Form 1040 line 1h before any separately computed income exclusion. This reads the entered wage amount, not Schedule SE's location-filtered amount: services performed outside the United States and listed possessions can be exempt from SE tax without being excluded from gross income. Missing or zero entered wages carry $0; positive entered wages require the W-2 reporting answer. Wages already on a W-2 remain on line 1a and are never added here. The existing FICA question remains required on that W-2 route unless services were explicitly performed outside the Schedule SE geography; the existing domestic FICA-conflict knockout is unchanged. A missing location does not erase no-W-2 wages from income; Schedule SE still resolves its own location question separately.

Fact.Name: Secondary filer's section 1402(c)(2)(C) wages were also reported on a Form W-2
Fact.Description: The MFJ secondary-filer twin of /writablePrimaryFilerForeignGovernmentWagesReportedOnFormW2.

Fact.Name: Secondary filer's Form W-2 for those wages withheld social security or Medicare tax
Fact.Description: The MFJ secondary-filer twin of /writablePrimaryFilerForeignGovernmentWagesHadFicaWithheld.

Fact.Name: Secondary filer's section 1402(c)(2)(C) wages on Form 1040 line 1h
Fact.Description: The MFJ secondary-filer twin of /primaryFilerForeignGovernmentWagesOnLine1h.

Fact.Name: Knockout: section 1402(c)(2)(C) wages entered on Schedule SE were also on a FICA-withheld Form W-2
Fact.Description: True when a filer included foreign-government employee wages on Schedule SE and attested that those same wages were reported on a Form W-2 that withheld social security or Medicare tax. That double entry would pay SE tax on top of FICA. Complete-safe false until every operand of the contradiction is answered Yes. DUAL-WIRED: BlockSubmissionOnTrue plus membership in flow:/flowIsKnockedOut.

Fact.Name: Other earned income
Fact.Description: Other earned income (line 1h). Carries the code-3 disability-pensions-before-minimum-retirement-age wages (re-activating the inherited hook — the upstream shipped the dependency commented out), and the second addend below, /primaryFilerExcessElectiveDeferralsOnLine1h — the IRC 402(g) elective deferrals this filer's Forms W-2 report in box 12 codes D, E, F, S, AA and BB, over that filer's 402(g)(1)(B) limit as raised by the IRC 414(v) catch-up allowance, less the designated Roth share IRC 402(g)(1)(A) carves out — and the third, /primaryFilerStrikeOrLockoutBenefitsOrZero, the filer's self-attested strike or lockout benefits, and /primaryFilerCorrectiveDistributionsOfExcessDeferralsOnLine1h, the current-year Code 8, non-IRA Form 1099-R box 2a amounts, and /primaryFilerForeignGovernmentWagesOnLine1h, the no-W-2 section 1402(c)(2)(C) wages, and form1099Misc:/primaryFilerForm1099MiscH2aCompensation, the H-2A agricultural worker compensation an employer reported in Form 1099-MISC box 3.

Fact.Name: Other earned income
Fact.Description: Other earned income (line 1h). The secondary-filer twin of /primaryFilerOtherEarnedIncome, including the MFJ secondary-filer Code 8 corrective- distribution leg and the secondary filer's Form 1099-MISC box 3 H-2A compensation.

Fact.Name: Other earned income
Fact.Description: Other earned income (line 1h). California TY2025 reads this fact through its stateSystems export (Schedule CA (540), Schedule CA (540NR)).

Fact.Name: ESPP disqualifying disposition ordinary income already in Form W-2 box 1
Fact.Description:
SCREEN. How much of the employee stock purchase plan ordinary income from this return's disqualifying dispositions did your employer already include in Form W-2 box 1? Enter $0 if none of it was.
WHY THE QUESTION HAS TO BE ASKED AT ALL. A disqualifying disposition turns the exercise spread, the fair market value of the stock when the option was exercised less the option price, into compensation for services in the year of the disposition. Many employers put that amount in Form W-2 box 1, and the wages line then already carries it; many do not, because section 421(b) expressly relieves them of withholding on it. Nothing this return already knows tells the two apart, so the amount that still has to be reported on Form 1040 line 1h is the ordinary income less whatever box 1 already carried.
ASKED WHEN: whenever scheduleD:/esppDisqualifyingOrdinaryIncomeTotal is more than $0. That is a gate the return can see for itself, unlike the sibling line 1h intakes on this module whose obligation is an application screen-flow one: the total is positive only on a return that classified at least one Form 8949 row as an ESPP disqualifying disposition and supplied that row's exercise value and purchase price. Until the question is answered on such a return, Form 1040 line 1h, line 1z and every figure built from them stay Incomplete rather than silently under-reporting the wages, which is the same posture /stateLocalIncomeTaxRefundCalculationRoute takes on this module: a positive amount does not resolve until the route it belongs to is known. Case income/s498-espp-ordinary-income-gate-unanswered-blocks-line-1h measures that.
VALIDATION: Dollar, Min $0. The consuming body floors a negative answer and caps an answer larger than the ordinary income itself, so neither can turn the line 1h leg into a negative wage; cases income/s498-espp-negative-already-in-box1-floored and income/s498-espp-already-in-box1-over-total-capped measure both ends.
A DOLLAR RATHER THAN A YES OR NO, on purpose. One return can hold several disqualifying dispositions with different payroll treatments, and only an amount expresses the mixed case without a per-transaction question in the Schedule D module, which is where the classification itself lives. Case income/s498-espp-ordinary-income-partly-in-w2-box1 is that return.

Fact.Name: ESPP disqualifying disposition ordinary income on Form 1040 line 1h
Fact.Description:
The employee stock purchase plan disqualifying-disposition ordinary income this return still has to report as wages: scheduleD:/esppDisqualifyingOrdinaryIncomeTotal less the part the employer already put in Form W-2 box 1.
WHY LINE 1h AND NOT LINE 1a. Publication 525 reports the amount as wages beside the capital gain on the same sale, and its Example 11 splits one $1,000 gain into $300 of wages and $700 of capital gain. Line 1a is the Form W-2 box 1 total, so an amount that is NOT on a Form W-2 cannot be entered there; line 1h is the line this module already routes no-W-2 wages to, and /primaryFilerForeignGovernmentWagesOnLine1h states the same reasoning for the section 1402(c)(2)(C) wages. The printed line 1h instruction lists the items that MUST be included there and does not name stock options, so the placement itself is this dictionary's interpretation rather than a printed instruction, and it is tagged accordingly.
THE OTHER HALF OF THE SAME AMOUNT IS ON SCHEDULE D, ONCE. The same ordinary income is the Form 8949 column (g) basis correction through scheduleD:/form8949Transactions/*/esppBasisCorrectionAdjustment, which is what makes the capital gain $700 rather than $1,000. That is not a double count: the basis correction removes the compensation element from the CAPITAL gain, and this fact puts it on the WAGES line, which is exactly the split Publication 525 prints.
COMPLETE-SAFE ON EVERY RETURN THAT HAS NO DISQUALIFYING DISPOSITION. The first case resolves $0 whenever the Schedule D total is not more than $0, which is every return that never answered the classification, so line 1h, line 1z and AGI are untouched there. The Switch has no catch-all on purpose: an unanswered gate beside a POSITIVE ordinary income runs off the end and this fact is Incomplete, which is the intended refusal to resolve. A True catch-all would hand a placeholder total to line 1z and AGI instead.
THE SAME NAMED GAP THE ARMED FORCES MOVING EXPENSE LEG HAS. This is a return-level figure, not a per-filer one: the Schedule D transaction collection carries no filer. It therefore enters /otherEarnedIncome, /employerIncomeSubtotal and /employerIncomeSubtotalDisregardingSection137 and NOT the two per-filer bases, so it is absent from /employerIncomeSubtotalWithoutCommunityPropertyAllocation, from the Form 2441 earned-income figures and from the IRA compensation cap. On an MFJ return whose ESPP income belongs to one spouse those figures are understated by this amount.

The summed value of line 1a to 1d and 1f to 1h, using only the primary filer's income, excluding any taxable CDCC benefits: /primaryFilerEmployerIncomeSubtotalBaseExcludingAdoptionBenefits (lines 1a-1d, 1g-1h, less the statutory-employee box 1 routed to Schedule C) plus /primaryFilerEmployerProvidedAdoptionBenefits (line 1f), split apart so that a MAGI "without regard to section 137" can be built BY CONSTRUCTION for this base's own downstream consumers rather than by subtracting the line 1f leg back out (see /primaryFilerEmployerProvidedAdoptionBenefits for why a direct wire would be circular).
STATUTORY EMPLOYEE ROUTING. The excluding-adoption-benefits base SUBTRACTS formW2s:/primaryFilerStatutoryEmployeeWagesRoutedToScheduleC, the primary filer's own box 1 wages from a W-2 whose box 13 "Statutory employee" box is checked and which names the Schedule C those wages are entered on. The printed instruction routes that box 1 to Schedule C line 1, and Schedule C line 31 reaches Schedule 1 line 3, so leaving it in this base as well would put it into /totalIncome twice; formW2s:/wages takes the same subtraction for Form 1040 line 1a, since line 1a and line 1z are two chains over the same box 1 amounts that may never be moved separately.
THE SUBTRAHEND IS FILER SCOPED ON PURPOSE. This base is not only a line 1z addend, it IS the primary filer's own earned income figure for Form 2441 line 4, for the IRA compensation cap and for the CDCC gates, so subtracting the RETURN level total here would charge this filer with a routed W-2 belonging to the spouse. formW2s mints the two filer scoped sums for exactly this seam.
WHAT THIS MOVES DOWNSTREAM, stated rather than left to be found. Every earned income figure computed from this base loses the statutory wages with it, and every printed worksheet that wants them back reads its OWN add back line rather than an unreduced 1z: EIC Worksheet B Part 3 line 3 ("Enter the amount from Schedule C, line 1, that you are filing as a statutory employee", https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040gi.pdf, page 47) through eitc:/eitcEarnedIncomeBase; the Schedule 8812 line 18a worksheet line 2a ("Enter any statutory employee income reported on line 1 of Schedule C", https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040s8.pdf, page 8) through /statutoryEmployeeWagesInEarnedIncome (with the worksheet's line 2b half on scheduleSE:/selfEmploymentEarnedIncomeSubjectToUsTax); and Form 2441's earned income item 3 ("If you are filing Schedule C (Form 1040) as a statutory employee, the amount shown on line 1 of the schedule", https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i2441.pdf, page 4) through /primaryFilerEarnedIncomeBaseWithStatutoryEmployeeWages and its twin, cdcc.xml's gates and its 5000 exclusion base wages, iraDeduction:/primaryFilerIraCompensation and its twin, and standardDeduction:/minimumStandardDeduction. /flowKnockoutStatutoryEmployee (formW2s.xml) is narrowed to the data-completeness residue: a checked box 13 whose routing was never answered. A routed statutory employee return is FILABLE, so everything this base feeds is reachable.
BYTE IDENTICAL ON THE COMMITTED CORPUS: the subtrahend is complete safe $0 and no committed scenario checks box 13, so this base, line 1z, total income, AGI and every earned income figure below them resolve to exactly what they resolved to before that subtrahend existed.

Fact.Name: The primary filer's line 1z base WITHOUT the line 1f adoption leg
Fact.Description:
Everything /primaryFilerEmployerIncomeSubtotalBase is except Form 1040 line 1f: lines 1a to 1d and 1g to 1h for the primary filer, less the statutory-employee box 1 routed to a Schedule C. BYTE-IDENTICAL to the base on every return that reports no employer-provided adoption benefits, because the leg it omits is $0 there.
WHY IT EXISTS, and it is the whole reason the Form 1040 line 1f wire could finally land. Sections 86(b)(2)(A) and 219(g)(3)(A)(ii) each define their modified AGI "without regard to" section 137, and the i8839 line 25 MAGI worksheet builds its own base the same way — its line 1 is "the amount you would enter on line 1z of Form 1040 if you could exclude the total amount on Form 8839, line 23". A base that CONTAINS the line 1f leg and then subtracts it back out has the right value and the WRONG SHAPE: the amount subtracted is downstream of the phaseout that produces it, so the dependency edge survives the cancellation and the engine still overflows. This fact is that base built by construction; nothing in its cone reads Form 8839.
NOT A PRINTED LINE. Form 1040 prints no 1z-without-1f, and this fact is never exported to a PDF field or to MeF. It is an intermediate that exists so /employerIncomeSubtotal (which DOES print) and the three section-137-disregarding MAGIs can be two different quantities without two different derivations of the same wages.

The summed value of line 1a to 1d and 1f to 1h, using only the secondary filer's income, but excluding any taxable CDCC benefits: /secondaryFilerEmployerIncomeSubtotalBaseExcludingAdoptionBenefits plus /secondaryFilerEmployerProvidedAdoptionBenefits (line 1f), the secondary twin of the same split on /primaryFilerEmployerIncomeSubtotalBase — see there for why the section 137 leg leaves by construction rather than by subtraction.
STATUTORY EMPLOYEE ROUTING: the secondary filer twin of the subtraction on /primaryFilerEmployerIncomeSubtotalBase, which carries the full statement of why the box 1 leaves this base, why the subtrahend is filer scoped, and which downstream earned income figures move with it. Subtracts formW2s:/secondaryFilerStatutoryEmployeeWagesRoutedToScheduleC; complete safe $0 and $0 on every committed return.

Fact.Name: The secondary filer's line 1z base WITHOUT the line 1f adoption leg
Fact.Description: The secondary filer mirror of /primaryFilerEmployerIncomeSubtotalBaseExcludingAdoptionBenefits, which carries the full statement of why sections 86(b)(2)(A) and 219(g)(3)(A)(ii) and the i8839 line 25 worksheet all need a line 1z built WITHOUT the section 137 leg rather than one that subtracts it back out. Byte-identical to /secondaryFilerEmployerIncomeSubtotalBase on every return that reports no employer-provided adoption benefits.

Fact.Name: Primary filer's EARNED INCOME wage base, with routed statutory employee wages added back
Fact.Description:
The primary filer's own wage-side earned income for every per-filer earned-income surface: /primaryFilerEmployerIncomeSubtotalBase PLUS formW2s:/primaryFilerStatutoryEmployeeWagesRoutedToScheduleC, the add-back half of the statutory employee routing.
THE QUANTITY IS FORM 2441's EARNED INCOME ITEMS 1 AND 3 FOR THIS FILER, and item 3 is the whole reason this fact exists: "If you are filing Schedule C (Form 1040) as a statutory employee, the amount shown on line 1 of the schedule" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i2441.pdf, page 4). Item 1 is "the amount shown on Form 1040, 1040-SR, or 1040-NR, line 1z" (same file lines 259-260), which the base is, and item 3 is a SEPARATE additive item beside it rather than a correction to it: the instruction prints them as two numbered members of one list. Note WHICH Schedule C figure the item names: LINE 1, the wages, not line 31, the net profit. The net profit reaches these same consumers through their self-employment term, which is already gated off a statutory business by scheduleC:/scheduleCs/*/primaryFilerNetProfit, so reading line 1 here and line 31 there is the only pairing that neither drops nor doubles the amount.
PER FILER, ON THE INSTRUCTION'S OWN WORDS: "If filing jointly, figure your and your spouse's earned income separately. Enter your earned income on line 4 and your spouse's earned income on line 5" (same file lines 252-255). formW2s mints the two filer scoped routed sums for exactly this seam; a return level add-back here would charge this filer with a routed W-2 belonging to the spouse, which is the mirror of the mis-attribution the round 7 subtraction avoided.
IT ALSO SERVES TWO NON-2441 CONSUMERS AND BOTH ARE EARNED INCOME BY STATUTE, not by analogy. The section 129(b)(1) earned income limitation on the dependent care exclusion (cdcc:/cdccPrimaryFilerBaseWagesAreLessThanMaxExclusion) and the section 21(d)(1) earned income limitation the cdcc eligibility gates screen for both ask what this individual EARNED, and a statutory employee's box 1 is compensation for services either way.
COMPLETE SAFE. Both terms are complete safe, the routed sum is complete safe $0, and no committed scenario checks box 13, so this fact equals the base on every committed return and nothing downstream of it moves. Cents preserved and NOT rounded, matching the base: the consumers that round do so at their own printed lines.
WHAT IT IS NOT. Not a line 1z figure and not an AGI figure. /employerIncomeSubtotal and the AGI chain keep the RAW base, because the wages really are gone from line 1z, and adding them back there would reverse the round 7 subtraction and double count in /totalIncome.
A THIRD TERM covers item 3's OTHER ARM. The paragraphs above read item 3 through the routed W-2, because that is the Schedule C line 1 the graph could see. scheduleC:/scheduleCs/*/isStatutoryEmployeeIncome has a second arm - the bare ATTESTATION, a Schedule C whose line 1 checkbox the filer answered with no box-13 W-2 on the return pointing at it - and item 3 does not distinguish them: it asks for "the amount shown on line 1 of the schedule" of any Schedule C "you are filing as a statutory employee". On that arm line 1 is the gross receipts the filer entered, and NOTHING subtracted them from the base, so the third term is purely additive rather than a restoration. scheduleC:/primaryFilerAttestationStatutoryEmployeeScheduleCLine1 is that amount, filer scoped by the same partition (scheduleC:/scheduleCs/*/belongsToPrimaryFiler) that /primaryFilerScheduleCNetProfit uses.
THE THREE TERMS CANNOT OVERLAP. The routed term sums W-2 box 1s over W-2s whose box 13 is checked; the attestation term sums Schedule C line 1s over businesses that NO such W-2 names (its per item gate carries Not(../hasLinkedStatutoryEmployeeW2)); and the base has had the routed box 1s removed and never carried a Schedule C receipt at all. The line 31 side is unchanged and still reaches these consumers through their self employment term, which scheduleC:/scheduleCs/*/primaryFilerNetProfit zeroes on BOTH arms of the checkbox - so reading line 1 here and a gated line 31 there remains the only pairing that neither drops nor doubles, now over the whole statutory population rather than half of it.

Fact.Name: Secondary filer's EARNED INCOME wage base, with routed statutory employee wages added back
Fact.Description:
The secondary filer twin of /primaryFilerEarnedIncomeBaseWithStatutoryEmployeeWages, which carries the full reading of why Form 2441's earned income item 3 is an ADDITIVE item, why the add-back is filer scoped and why the line 1z and AGI chain deliberately does not take it. Sums /secondaryFilerEmployerIncomeSubtotalBase and formW2s:/secondaryFilerStatutoryEmployeeWagesRoutedToScheduleC, cents preserved, complete safe, equal to the base on every committed return.
A THIRD TERM, scheduleC:/secondaryFilerAttestationStatutoryEmployeeScheduleCLine1, covers item 3's other arm - the Schedule C line 1 of her ATTESTATION-only statutory businesses, which no box-13 W-2 names and whose receipts nothing ever subtracted from her base. The primary twin carries the reading and the three-way disjointness argument.

Fact.Name: Line 1z BEFORE the Form 8958 community-property allocation — the EARNED INCOME figure
Fact.Description:
THE EARNED INCOME OF THIS FILER, which is not the same quantity as Form 1040 line 1z and is not the same quantity as line 1z without the allocation. Two arms:
(a) On a community-property allocation return — Round(primary base + taxable dependent care). The SECONDARY filer's base is deliberately excluded, and that exclusion is the whole point of this arm. Nothing else in this dictionary lets a spouse's W-2 into the collection on a non-joint return; formW2s:/formW2s/*/secondaryFilerUsedWithoutMFJ is what first admits one. On exactly that population the secondary base becomes non-zero for the first time, so a household total here would report the SPOUSE'S wages as this filer's earned income. IRC 32(c)(2)(B)(i) is about "the earned income of an individual", and Publication 555 says "Your earned income includes the entire amount you" earned — neither licenses ADDING the spouse's whole wages, and the direction of that error is taxpayer-favourable (the ACTC takes 15% of earned income over $2,500), which is exactly the kind that ships quietly.
(b) On every other return — Round(primary base + secondary base + taxable dependent care + the Form 1040 line 1h excess Armed Forces moving expense reimbursement), equal to /employerIncomeSubtotal because the allocation addend is $0 there. On arm (a) the line 1h excess is not added: it is a return-level figure with no filer attribution.
WHY THE ARM IS KEYED ON THE GATE RATHER THAN ON Not(isFilingStatusMFJ). Either is defensible and the more general MFJ test would also be correct on the law. The gate is chosen because it is complete safe FALSE — so an unanswered filing status cannot make this fact Incomplete — and because it fires on exactly the population this unit created, leaving every other return's value untouched. The population the MFJ test would additionally reach is a non-joint, non-community return carrying a spouse's W-2, and that return is still REFUSED by formW2s:/formW2s/secondaryFilerUsedWithoutMFJ, so the extra generality would compute a number nobody can file.
WHY IT EXISTS. IRC 32(c)(2)(B)(i) says the earned income of an individual "shall be computed without regard to any commu-" / "nity property laws" (26 U.S.C. 32, https://uscode.house.gov/view.xhtml?req=granuleid:USC-2024-title26-section32&num=0&edition=2024, LEFT column of a two column extraction), and Publication 555 says the same thing in the filer's words: "Your earned income includes the entire amount you" earned "even if part of it is treated as belonging to your" spouse. Its CAUTION in the very next sentence draws the line this fact sits on — that rule "doesn't apply when determining your ad-" justed gross income, which "includes that part of both your and your spouse's" wages. So Form 1040 line 1z and the AGI chain below it CARRY the allocation, and the EARNED INCOME facts read this one instead.
THE FOUR READERS ARE EACH DECIDED, not left to fall out, and all four therefore get the FILER-scoped figure on an allocation return. eitc:/eitcEarnedIncomeBase — IRC 32(c)(2)(B)(i) by name. /earnedIncomeWithAllCombatPay, whose consumers are the ctcOdc additional child tax credit legs — IRC 24(d)(1)(B)(i) takes "payer’s earned income (within the mean-" / "ing of section 32) which is taken into ac-" count, so §32's rule comes with it. /earnedIncomeWithAllCombatPayIncludingExcludedTerritory, an EITC fact. standardDeduction:/minimumStandardDeduction, the IRC 63(c)(5)(B) floor "(B) the sum of $250 and such individual's earned income." — and this one is THIS REPO'S READING, stated as such: §63 prints no community-property rule of its own, and the choice is to keep "earned income" one quantity across the dictionary rather than to have the phrase mean two different things two facts apart.
EVERY OTHER READER OF /employerIncomeSubtotal KEEPS THE ALLOCATION, and they are the AGI chain: /totalIncome (Form 1040 line 9), /totalIncomeUpperBoundForIraMagi, scheduleE:/section8582Magi and socialSecurity:/socialSecurityBenefitsWkshtLine3.

Fact.Name: Statutory employee Schedule C line 1, as an EARNED INCOME add-back (arm matched, both arms of the checkbox)
Fact.Description:
The routed statutory employee wages that every printed earned-income worksheet adds back beside /employerIncomeSubtotalWithoutCommunityPropertyAllocation, ARM MATCHED to that fact's own two arms.
WHY IT IS A SWITCH RATHER THAN A SINGLE DEPENDENCY, and this is the whole content of the fact. The figure it accompanies has two arms: on a community property allocation return it is the PRIMARY filer's base alone, and on every other return it is the household sum. An add-back that always read the RETURN LEVEL formW2s:/statutoryEmployeeWagesRoutedToScheduleC would add a spouse's routed W-2 to a figure that deliberately excludes that spouse's wages, so on exactly the population the arm exists for it would report the spouse's statutory wages as this filer's earned income. That is the taxpayer favourable direction and it is the error this Switch prevents. The printed worksheets agree with the arms rather than with the return level total: the Schedule 8812 line 18a worksheet says "Disregard community property laws when figuring the amounts to enter on this worksheet" and, separately, "If married filing jointly, include your spouse's amounts with yours when completing this worksheet" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040s8.pdf, page 8), and a community property allocation return is by construction NOT a joint return, so on that arm the worksheet wants this filer's own amount and nothing else.
