NOT A REPLACEMENT FOR THE PER FILER PAIR ABOVE, and the two may never be summed into one figure. /primaryFilerEarnedIncomeBaseWithStatutoryEmployeeWages and its twin serve the consumers that read a per filer BASE (Form 2441, the cdcc gates, the section 129 screen, the section 219 ceiling); this fact serves the four consumers that read the RETURN LEVEL /employerIncomeSubtotalWithoutCommunityPropertyAllocation. The two reader sets are disjoint and were measured by grep; see the seam banner above the pair.
THE FOUR CONSUMERS, each with its own printed add-back line, which is why the add-back is an addend at each of them rather than a rebody of the figure they share: /earnedIncomeWithAllCombatPay (Schedule 8812 line 18a) - Earned Income Worksheet line 2a, "Enter any statutory employee income reported on line 1 of Schedule C" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040s8.pdf, page 8), whose paired line 2b then says "Do not include on this line any statutory employee income" of the Schedule C line 31 it collects (same file lines 379-381). /earnedIncomeWithAllCombatPayIncludingExcludedTerritory (the section 32 twin, read by eitc:/hasEarnedIncome) and eitc:/eitcEarnedIncomeBase - EIC Worksheet B Part 3 line 3, "Enter the amount from Schedule C, line 1, that you are filing as a statutory employee" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040gi.pdf, page 47), against Part 2's "Don't include on these lines any statutory employee income" (same file line 3093). standardDeduction:/minimumStandardDeduction - IRC 63(c)(5)(B), "the sum of $250 and such individual's earned income", which prints no statutory employee rule of its own; this repo's settled reading, already stated on /employerIncomeSubtotalWithoutCommunityPropertyAllocation for the community property question, is to keep "earned income" ONE quantity across the dictionary rather than let the phrase mean two different things two facts apart.
COMPLETE SAFE $0 on every committed return: both arms resolve to a complete safe routed sum and no committed scenario checks box 13, so all four consumers are byte identical.
BOTH ARMS OF THE CHECKBOX are covered, and this is the fact's second population, not a second quantity. Worksheet line 2a is "any statutory employee income reported on LINE 1 of Schedule C". The ROUTED arm - the businesses a box-13 W-2 names, whose line 1 the graph supplies from formW2s - is one source of it. The other arm of scheduleC:/scheduleCs/*/isStatutoryEmployeeIncome is the bare ATTESTATION: the filer checked the Schedule C line 1 box and no W-2 on the return points at that business, so its line 1 is simply the gross receipts he entered. Nothing subtracted those receipts from Form 1040 line 1a (there was no link to subtract through), so they are NOT in the companion base and 2a is where they enter earned income. Each arm now adds scheduleC:/primaryFilerAttestationStatutoryEmployeeScheduleCLine1 (and, on the household arm, the secondary twin) beside the routed sum it already had.
THE TWO TERMS ARE DISJOINT BY CONSTRUCTION: the scheduleC per item gate carries Not(../hasLinkedStatutoryEmployeeW2), so a routed business contributes to the formW2s term and never to the scheduleC one. Line 2a is therefore each statutory business's line 1 exactly once, whichever arm explains it — with ONE qualified state: a ROUTED business that ALSO carries typed receipts contributes only its W-2 box 1 at 2a (which is what the printed line asks: "statutory employee INCOME reported on line 1", not "line 1"); its non-statutory receipts-less-expenses residue leaves earned income entirely. That double-entry state is legally moot — the Schedule C instructions require TWO Schedules C (i1040sc 365-367, quoted on hasLinkedStatutoryEmployeeW2) — and is deliberately not modelled or witnessed.
THE COMPANION 2b EXCLUSION MOVED WITH IT, and it had to. scheduleC:/scheduleCs/*/statutoryEmployeeNetProfit is gated on the whole checkbox again, so 2a and 2b cover one population. The value that moves is Schedule 8812 line 18a on tests/nodes/ty2025/income/statutory-attestation-only-schedule-c-keeps-pre-existing-18a: 60,000 -> 70,000, which is the printed worksheet's foot (1a 20,000 + 2a 50,000 + 2b 0). The committed corpus is byte identical - 1,538 statutoryEmployee occurrences in scenarios/, 0 true, re-measured this session, and the Schedule C line 1 checkbox is unanswered in all of them.

Fact.Name: employer income subtotal
Fact.Description:
Is used as earned income for calculating the EITC and CDCC.
Form 1040, Line 1z

Fact.Name: Form 1040 line 1z DISREGARDING SECTION 137 — the i8839 worksheet's own line 1z
Fact.Description:
Line 1z as it would read if the WHOLE of Form 8839 line 23 could be excluded: the two per-filer bases WITHOUT their line 1f legs, plus the line 1e taxable dependent care, the Form 8958 community-property wage allocation and the line 1h excess Armed Forces moving expense reimbursement, rounded once exactly as /employerIncomeSubtotal is. It is NOT a printed line and is never exported to MeF or a PDF field.
THE PRINTED SENTENCE THIS IS. The i8839 Modified Adjusted Gross Income Worksheet for line 25 begins "Enter the amount you would enter on line 1z of Form 1040, 1040-SR, or 1040-NR if you could exclude the total amount on Form 8839, line 23" and then adds line 23 back at its own line 2. This fact is that worksheet line 1 verbatim; /totalIncomeDisregardingSection137 adds line 2 and line 3.
AND IT IS THE SAME QUANTITY TWO STATUTES DEMAND. Section 86(b)(2)(A) computes the social security modified AGI "without regard to ... section 137", and section 219(g)(3)(A)(ii) does the same for the IRA deduction phaseout. Both therefore want the FULL benefit in income rather than the section 137 remainder — and the full benefit is phaseout-independent, which is exactly why reading this fact instead of /employerIncomeSubtotal leaves the dependency graph acyclic where the naive wire made it cyclic over five distinct return arcs. Section 221 goes the other way (221(b)(2)(C)(ii) applies the MAGI "after application of sections 86, 135, 137, 219, and 469"), so the student loan MAGI keeps reading the real line 1z; that asymmetry is not an oversight and is the reason there are two facts here rather than one.
WHY IT DOES NOT SUBTRACT THE LINE 1f LEGS FROM /employerIncomeSubtotal, which would be the obvious one-line body: the amount subtracted is itself downstream of the phaseout this figure feeds, so the subtraction cancels the VALUE and keeps the EDGE and the engine still overflows its stack. The per-filer bases are split so this figure can be built by construction.
BYTE-IDENTICAL CONSEQUENCE ON THE COMMITTED CORPUS: no committed scenario answers a Form 8839 employer-benefit intake or a box 12 code T, so line 23 is $0, both line 1f legs are $0, and this fact equals /employerIncomeSubtotal on every committed return.

Fact.Name: This estate or trust K-1's box 2a ordinary dividends, complete safe
Fact.Description: THIS Schedule K-1 (Form 1041)'s box 2a ordinary dividends, defaulting to $0 when the box is unanswered. The printed form routes the box in one line of its own page 2 table, and the beneficiary reports it on Form 1040 line 3b. Complete safe alias of scheduleE:/form1041K1s/*/writableBox2aOrdinaryDividends, built in this module rather than in scheduleE because the consuming total lives here and this unit owns this module. The form prints "2a. Ordinary dividends Form 1040 or 1040-SR, line 3b". Summed over the collection by /estateTrustK1OrdinaryDividends.

Fact.Name: Estate or trust K-1 ordinary dividends (box 2a) (aggregate to Form 1040 line 3b)
Fact.Description:
CollectionSum(/form1041K1s/*/estateTrustK1Box2aOrdinaryDividends), the Schedule K-1 (Form 1041) leg of Form 1040 line 3b and the sibling of the partnership and S corporation leg scheduleE:/k1PortfolioOrdinaryDividends. Without this leg, a beneficiary's line 3b would read $0 against real dividends, an UNDERSTATEMENT of income and so the adverse direction. Through /ordinaryDividends it reaches the Schedule B over $1,500 dividends test, Form 8960 line 2 (NIIT) and the EITC investment income test exactly like a 1099-DIV dividend and like the partnership leg beside it.
THE GATE IS THE COLLECTION, NOT scheduleE:/claimsEstateTrustK1, the same deliberate divergence this unit made on interest:/estateTrustK1InterestIncome and for the same reason: Schedule E line 42, which gates on the Part III claim flag, is a reconciliation figure nothing computes tax from, while this line IS taxed, so dropping a recorded box because the filer never answered /writableHasEstateTrustK1 would understate income. Recorded for the lead rather than left to inference.
COMPLETE SAFE: the CollectionSum sits inside an IsComplete Switch on the /form1041K1s collection defaulting to $0, and each item's term defaults to $0, so a return that never opened the estate or trust K-1 section resolves Complete $0. Every committed scenario is byte identical: none answers the box. UNROUNDED, because the consuming line already Rounds once.

Fact.Name: This estate or trust K-1's box 2b qualified dividends, complete safe
Fact.Description: THIS Schedule K-1 (Form 1041)'s box 2b qualified dividends, defaulting to $0 when the box is unanswered. The printed form routes the box in one line of its own page 2 table, and the beneficiary reports it on Form 1040 line 3a. Complete safe alias of scheduleE:/form1041K1s/*/writableBox2bQualifiedDividends, built in this module rather than in scheduleE because the consuming total lives here and this unit owns this module. The form prints "2b. Qualified dividends Form 1040 or 1040-SR, line 3a". Box 2b is a SUBSET of box 2a, not a further addend, exactly as Form 1099-DIV box 1b is a subset of box 1a. Summed over the collection by /estateTrustK1QualifiedDividends.

Fact.Name: Estate or trust K-1 qualified dividends (box 2b) (aggregate to Form 1040 line 3a)
Fact.Description:
CollectionSum(/form1041K1s/*/estateTrustK1Box2bQualifiedDividends), the Schedule K-1 (Form 1041) leg of Form 1040 line 3a and the sibling of scheduleE:/k1PortfolioQualifiedDividends. Added to /qualifiedDividends, so the beneficiary's qualified share reaches the QDCGT preferential rate worksheet. It MOVES WITH the box 2a leg on /ordinaryDividends in the same edit, because box 2b is a subset of box 2a and landing one alone would state a return reporting more qualified dividends than ordinary dividends.
THE GATE IS THE COLLECTION, NOT scheduleE:/claimsEstateTrustK1, the same deliberate divergence this unit made on interest:/estateTrustK1InterestIncome and for the same reason: Schedule E line 42, which gates on the Part III claim flag, is a reconciliation figure nothing computes tax from, while this line IS taxed, so dropping a recorded box because the filer never answered /writableHasEstateTrustK1 would understate income. Recorded for the lead rather than left to inference.
COMPLETE SAFE: the CollectionSum sits inside an IsComplete Switch on the /form1041K1s collection defaulting to $0, and each item's term defaults to $0, so a return that never opened the estate or trust K-1 section resolves Complete $0. Every committed scenario is byte identical: none answers the box. UNROUNDED, because the consuming line already Rounds once.

Fact.Name: Qualified Dividends
Fact.Description: Qualified dividend income to report on line 3a of Form 1040. Sum of Form 1099-DIV Box 1b plus the Schedule K-1 box 6b / box 5b qualified dividends (scheduleE:/k1PortfolioQualifiedDividends, complete-safe 0 for every non-K-1 return), per the partner instructions ("Report any qualified dividends on Form 1040 or 1040-SR, line 3a."). Feeds the QDCGT preferential-rate worksheet unchanged. A THIRD LEG, /estateTrustK1QualifiedDividends, is the Schedule K-1 (Form 1041) box 2b total, whose routing is printed on the form itself ("2b. Qualified dividends Form 1040 or 1040-SR, line 3a"). It moves in the same edit as the box 2a leg on line 3b, because box 2b is a subset of box 2a. Complete safe $0 on every return with no Form 1041 K-1, so every committed scenario is byte identical. BELOW THAT SUM, dividendReports:/dividendNomineeQualifiedDividendsTotal is subtracted: the qualified part of every Form 1099-DIV nominee share, because Pub. 550 excludes "Qualified dividends you received as a nominee." from line 3a. The result is floored at $0 and capped at line 3b (/ordinaryDividends): qualified dividends are also included in the ordinary dividend total on line 3b, so where a nominee share leaves line 3b but its qualified part is unanswered, at least the part of it that cannot be nonqualified comes off line 3a too. Complete-safe $0 on every return that answers the nominee qualified-part question for no payer. California TY2025 reads this fact through its stateSystems export (Schedule CA (540), Schedule CA (540NR)).

Fact.Name: Ordinary dividends
Fact.Description: Ordinary dividend income to report on line 3b of Form 1040. Sum of Form 1099-DIV Box 1a plus the Schedule K-1 box 6a / box 5a ordinary dividends (scheduleE:/k1PortfolioOrdinaryDividends, complete-safe 0 for every non-K-1 return), per the partner instructions ("Report ordinary dividends on Form 1040 or 1040-SR, line 3b."). The K-1 term therefore reaches the Schedule B over-$1,500 dividends test, Form 8960 line 2 (NIIT) and the EITC investment-income test exactly like 1099-DIV dividends. A third leg, /estateTrustK1OrdinaryDividends — the Schedule K-1 (Form 1041) box 2a total, printed on the form as "2a. Ordinary dividends Form 1040 or 1040-SR, line 3b" — reaches those same three consumers. Complete-safe $0 on every return with no Form 1041 K-1, so every committed scenario is byte identical. Below that sum, dividendReports:/dividendNomineeDistributionTotal is subtracted — the total the filer received as a nominee, in the filer's name but actually belonging to someone else, per Schedule B's "report the whole figure, subtract the nominee amount below the subtotal" mechanic (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040sb.pdf, page 1), mirrored here because line 3b has no Schedule B counterpart line of its own to carry the subtraction. The subtraction is floored at $0 — a nominee distribution can never drive this line, and therefore AGI, Form 8960 line 2, the EITC investment-income test and Form 4952 line 4a, negative — the same floor interest:/interestIncome already carries for its own below-the-line subtractions. interest:/requiresScheduleB's $1,500 dividend test reads this exact fact by Dependency, so the trigger and the printed line can never disagree. Complete-safe $0 on every return that answers the nominee question for no payer, so every committed scenario is byte identical. A further addend sits OUTSIDE that floored sum: form8621:/form8621OrdinaryDividends, the part of a section 1291 distribution that is not an excess distribution and is therefore an ordinary dividend under section 301(c). It is not a qualified dividend — a PFIC is not a qualified foreign corporation — so it reaches line 3b and not line 3a, and it is complete-safe $0 on every return with no Form 8621. The Round wraps the whole sum, this leg included, so line 3b is rounded once from the cents-bearing total.

Fact.Name: Fully-taxable traditional IRA distribution (Form 1040 line 4b)
Fact.Description: The total amount of a fully-taxable traditional IRA distribution (Form 1099-R box 1, with the IRA/SEP/SIMPLE box checked) for which no nondeductible-contribution basis exists, so the entire distribution is taxable. Per the Form 1040 instructions a fully-taxable IRA distribution is entered on line 4b (/taxableIraDistributions) with NO entry on line 4a. Complete-safe: 0 / unanswered ⇒ no IRA income ⇒ /taxableIraDistributions and /totalIncome unchanged. Scope: fully taxable only; partial taxability (basis / Form 8606), the 10% early-distribution penalty (Form 5329), and rollover / QCD / HFD exclusions are deferred. On a joint return this amount is the PRIMARY filer's own distribution unless /writableIraDistributionAmountBelongsToSecondaryFiler says it is the secondary filer's; the two per-filer shares are form8606:/fullyTaxableIraDistributionAttributedToFiler and its secondary twin.

Fact.Name: The fully-taxable IRA distribution belongs to the secondary filer
Fact.Description: On a joint return, whether the amount answered at /writableIraDistributionAmount is the SECONDARY filer's own fully-taxable traditional IRA distribution rather than the primary filer's. Complete-safe: unanswered attributes the amount to the primary filer. Feeds form8606:/fullyTaxableIraDistributionAttributedToFiler and its secondary twin, which let the two Form-8606-versus-scalar knockouts test each filer's own claim against that same filer's own share of this amount, instead of one filer's claim against an amount that may belong to the other.

Fact.Name: Federal income tax withheld on a fully-taxable IRA distribution (Form 1099-R box 4)
Fact.Description: Federal income tax withheld (Form 1099-R box 4) on the fully-taxable traditional IRA distribution reported via /writableIraDistributionAmount. Reported on Form 1040 line 25b. Complete-safe consumer (/iraDistributionWithholding): 0 / unanswered ⇒ no line-25b withholding from this intake ⇒ line 25b unchanged. Scope: the scalar intake only (the Form 8606 intake has no withholding companion yet).

Fact.Name: IRA distribution federal withholding (Form 1040 line 25b term)
Fact.Description: Complete-safe federal income tax withheld (Form 1099-R box 4) on the scalar IRA distribution: the answered /writableIraDistributionWithholding when present, else 0. Consumed by taxCalculations /form1099Withholding (Form 1040 line 25b). Complete-safe: 0 when the withholding intake is unanswered.

Fact.Name: Gross IRA distributions from the Form 1099-R collection (Form 1040 line 4a input)
Fact.Description: The sum of box 1 (gross distribution) across every Form 1099-R with the IRA/SEP/SIMPLE box checked. This is the total the "More than one distribution" rule asks for on line 4a; whether line 4a actually carries it is /iraDistributions' decision, because a SINGLE fully-taxable distribution is entered on line 4b with no line-4a entry at all. NON-NEGATIVE (box 1 carries a Min $0 limit per item) and whole dollars (each form1099Rs:/form1099Rs/*/grossDistribution is already rounded; the Round here is the module idiom, not a second rounding step). Complete-safe 0 when no IRA-flagged 1099-R is present, which is every return in the corpus at this commit.

Fact.Name: Taxable IRA distributions from the Form 1099-R collection (Form 1040 line 4b input)
Fact.Description:
The sum of box 2a (taxable amount) across every Form 1099-R with the IRA/SEP/SIMPLE box checked — the "figure the taxable amount of each distribution and enter the total of the taxable amounts on line 4b" half of the same instruction. Box 2a is taken as reported: the shapes where box 2a is NOT the taxable amount each carry their own refusal (box 2b checked, a rollover, or box 2a below box 1 — see form1099Rs:/form1099Rs/*/isUnsupportedIraDistribution, and the two line-4c carve-outs named below, which are the shapes where box 2a IS the taxable amount despite differing from box 1). NON-NEGATIVE, whole dollars, complete-safe 0.
THIS SUM NO LONGER EQUALS /iraDistributionsFromForm1099Rs ON EVERY FILABLE RETURN, and the correction is recorded rather than quietly dropped: the equality was previously a property of this fact. TWO shapes now differ, one per printed branch of the Form 1040 instructions' Exception 1, and both are elections the filer has made on line 4c box 1. (i) form1099Rs:/form1099Rs/*/isFullDirectRolloverElection — a fully rolled-over DIRECT rollover, box 1 the gross and box 2a $0, which is Exception 1's first branch verbatim ("If the total distribution was rolled over, enter -0- on line 4b"). (ii) form1099Rs:/form1099Rs/*/isPartialDirectRolloverElection — a PARTLY rolled-over direct rollover, box 2a above $0 and below box 1, which is the second branch ("If the total distribution wasn't rolled over, enter the part not rolled over on line 4b"). Inside Exception 1's own scope the rolled-over part is never taxable and the Form 8606 basis population is refused alongside an IRA-flagged 1099-R, so box 2a IS the part not rolled over. This CollectionSum produces both with no term added, because box 2a is already the figure each branch asks for. No body change was needed here for either; only this paragraph. BREADTH-FIRST SIBLING of the contracted /iraDistributionsFromForm1099Rs: the contract named only the gross half, and line 4b cannot be derived from a gross total alone.
A THIRD SHAPE, the QCD half of the line-4c residue, DID NEED A BODY CHANGE. Exception 3's qualified charitable distribution is INVISIBLE on the Form 1099-R - the custodian reports box 2a equal to box 1 because it does not know the money went to charity - so unlike the two rollover branches there is no reported figure this sum could pick up. The dependency therefore moved from the raw box 2a to form1099Rs:/form1099Rs/*/line4bTaxableAmount, which is box 2a less form1099Rs:/form1099Rs/*/line4cQcdExclusion and is identical to box 2a on every form with no supported QCD election - which is every form in every committed scenario, the line-4c election writable being answered on none of the 56 that carry Form 1099-R items. The SHAPE of this fact is deliberately unchanged: one CollectionSum under one Round, the round-once-at-the-total discipline, never a sum of per-item rounded addends. Netting the exclusion into box 2a itself was rejected - see that fact's own Description for the fifteen consumers that read box 2a as the reported figure, several of them knockout inputs.

Fact.Name: The scalar IRA intake is answered with a positive amount
Fact.Description: Whether /writableIraDistributionAmount is both answered and greater than zero — the same "an answered 0 behaves like an unanswered intake" test /taxableIraDistributions already applies inline for its own arm selection, named here because a second consumer now needs it. Complete false when the intake is unanswered.

Fact.Name: Knockout: the Form 8915-F qualified amount is larger than the ordinary distribution route it comes out of
Fact.Description:
Blocks submission when the Form 8915-F current-year qualified amount that has to LEAVE the ordinary Form 1040 line 4b or line 5b route is larger than what that route is carrying.
WHAT THE CONTRADICTION IS. Form 8915-F line 7 tells the filer to report the excess of lines 2 through 4 column (a) over the line 6 qualified amount "as IRA and/or pension and annuity distributions, as applicable, in accordance with the instructions for your tax return". The Part I intakes here are independent return-root writables: a filer can answer line 2 column (a) 30,000 and column (b) 22,000 without entering any Form 1099-R at all. When that happens the graph has two irreconcilable statements — a distribution Part I says was received, and an ordinary route that is not carrying it — and the line 7 excess has nowhere to be reported from. Neither number can be trusted, so the return is refused rather than filed with a line 5b that silently drops the excess.
WHY A REFUSAL AND NOT A FLOOR ALONE. The floor on each of the two totals stops a negative line from printing; it does not make the return right. A floored return understates line 4b or line 5b by exactly the line 7 excess, in the taxpayer's favour and invisibly. This repo refuses a return it cannot compute rather than file a number it cannot defend.
THE NARROW SHAPE, stated so it is not widened by accident. It fires on the ARITHMETIC contradiction only — removal greater than route — and NOT on the presence of a qualified disaster distribution. A return whose Part I claim reconciles with its Forms 1099-R computes and files: without this guard such a return would file with the qualified amount counted twice, and the only alternative on offer was to flag the Form 1099-R and be refused by form1099Rs:/flowKnockoutRetirementQualifiedDisasterDistribution. That sibling knockout is UNCHANGED by this unit and still refuses every flagged return; narrowing or withdrawing it is not done here.
BOTH SIDES IN ONE FACT because the two routes fail the same way and a filer meets them as one question.

Fact.Name: Knockout: an IRA-flagged Form 1099-R beside a duplicate scalar intake
Fact.Description:
THE DOUBLE-COUNT REFUSAL. This dictionary has a legacy scalar route (/writableIraDistributionAmount) and a Form 1099-R collection route to Form 1040 line 4b. Those are alternative intake shapes, so using both blocks submission rather than silently counting or dropping dollars.
Form 8606 is not a duplicate route. A partly taxable traditional-IRA distribution is reported on Form 1099-R and its basis calculation is reported on Form 8606; the two forms must be joined to compute one line-4b amount. The collection therefore may coexist with a claimed Form 8606, and /iraDistributions plus /taxableIraDistributions select the Form 8606 worksheet result for that document-backed population.
WHY NOT SILENTLY PREFER ONE ROUTE. Arm selection alone would compute a number for a return whose intakes contradict each other, and the direction of that error is UNDER-statement of income when the two intakes are genuinely different IRAs — a World-#1 exposure. The refusal is the taxpayer-safe direction and is visible.
Complete false on every return with no IRA-flagged Form 1099-R.

Fact.Name: IRA distributions
Fact.Description:
IRA distributions to report on line 4a of Form 1040. For a FULLY-TAXABLE traditional IRA distribution (scope) the Form 1040 instructions direct that NO entry be made on line 4a (the full amount goes on line 4b, /taxableIraDistributions) — so that case resolves 0, unchanged. In the PARTIAL-taxability case (Form 8606 Part I claimed) line 4a carries the GROSS distributions (form8606:/form8606GrossDistributions); complete-safe 0 when neither intake is in use.
THE COLLECTION ROUTE. An IRA-flagged Form 1099-R can reach a filable return, and when one is present this line comes from the collection instead of from Form 8606. Two printed rules decide whether line 4a carries a figure at all: a SINGLE fully-taxable distribution goes on line 4b with NO line-4a entry, but with MORE THAN ONE distribution the gross total is entered on line 4a even though each one is fully taxable. Both are honoured here.
THE SECOND DISJUNCT (gross above taxable) IS REACHABLE, and it serves BOTH printed branches of Exception 1. The line-4c election successor unit admits a fully rolled-over DIRECT rollover the filer elected on line 4c box 1 (form1099Rs:/form1099Rs/*/isFullDirectRolloverElection): box 1 carries the gross, box 2a is $0, and this disjunct puts the gross on line 4a while /taxableIraDistributions puts -0- on line 4b. Its partial-rollover successor admits the other branch (form1099Rs:/form1099Rs/*/isPartialDirectRolloverElection): box 2a sits above $0 and below box 1, the same disjunct puts the gross on line 4a, and line 4b carries box 2a, which inside Exception 1's scope is the part not rolled over. Both are exactly Exception 1's printed pairs. The disjunct was written as a kept-for-later hedge and turned out to be the whole of the arm both units needed, so no body change was owed in this module for either; the paragraph is corrected because the first unit falsified its "unreachable" claim and the second falsified its "one shape" successor.
A THIRD EXCEPTION USES THE SAME DISJUNCT: Exception 3's qualified charitable distribution, which opens "enter the total distribution on line 4a". A QCD is reported with box 2a EQUAL to box 1, so the gross and taxable collection totals can be equal, in which case the disjunct does not fire; they differ when /taxableIraDistributionsFromForm1099Rs sums box 2a NET of the exclusion. So line 4a carries the gross for a QCD, exactly as printed, and again with no body change here - only this paragraph. Line 4a is unchanged for every return with no supported QCD election.
WHY THIS IS ARM SELECTION AND NOT A THIRD SUMMAND — the double-count the /iraDistributionsFromForm1099Rs contract measured. A partly-taxable IRA distribution is reported BOTH on an IRA-flagged Form 1099-R AND on Form 8606, so ADDING the collection total beside the two Form 8606 grosses would count that distribution's box 1 twice. Two independent barriers stop it. (1) This Switch never evaluates both routes: with an IRA-flagged 1099-R present the Form 8606 terms are not read at all. (2) The two populations are made DISJOINT by refusal — /knockoutIraDistributionDoubleIntake blocks submission when an IRA-flagged 1099-R co-exists with a claimed Form 8606 or a positive /writableIraDistributionAmount, and form1099Rs:/form1099Rs/*/isUnsupportedIraDistribution refuses any IRA item whose box 2a differs from its box 1, which is the only shape Form 8606 exists to describe.
BYTE-IDENTITY IS STRUCTURAL, not measured-and-hoped: form1099Rs:/hasIraDistribution1099R is Complete false on every return with no IRA-flagged 1099-R, so the second Case is taken with the Form 8606 body verbatim on every return with no IRA-flagged 1099-R.
A TERM RIDES OUTSIDE THE ROUTE SWITCH: form8606:/form8606RothGrossDistributionsAllFilers, the two filers' gross ROTH IRA distributions - Part III line 19 plus the qualified distributions that have no Part III, which i8606 sends straight to this line. It is added rather than made a fourth arm for the same reason /form8606Line25cOrZero is added to /taxableIraDistributions: Part III is not gated on form8606:/claimsForm8606, so a Roth-only filer selects no arm at all. Before it, a nonqualified Roth distribution reached line 4b through /form8606Line25cOrZero with NOTHING on line 4a beside it, and a qualified one appeared on the return nowhere. The term is complete-safe and $0 across the committed corpus.
A PRE-EXISTING GAP THIS UNIT FOUND AND DID NOT CLOSE, recorded so it is not rediscovered: this fact carries NO Export of any kind, so Form 1040 line 4a computes and nothing reads it — not the MeF surface, not downstream facts. Its sibling /pensionsAndAnnuities, the line-5a gross that pairs with it, carries Export downstreamFacts and mef. Adding the mef export is a separate surface change with its own snapshot suite, so the asymmetry is named here rather than silently repaired. California TY2025 reads this fact through its stateSystems export (Schedule CA (540), Schedule CA (540NR)). CONTRIBUTIONS RETURNED BY THE DUE DATE. On a return with no IRA-flagged Form 1099-R, line 4a also carries the 2025 traditional and Roth contributions returned by the due date under section 408(d)(4): the Form 8606 instructions say "you must include the amount of the distribution of the returned contributions you made in 2025 and any related earnings on your 2025 Form 1040 ... line 4a" and the earnings on line 4b (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i8606.pdf, page 7). The returned contributions are not taxable; the earnings are not intaken (TAX-INTERPRETATIONS IN-306), so line 4b is unchanged. With an IRA-flagged Form 1099-R the trustee reports the distribution and the collection route carries it, so the amount is not added twice (obligations IRA-030, IRA-017 (b), reconciliation finding).

Fact.Name: Form 1040 line 4b, the chosen ordinary traditional-IRA route, BEFORE the Form 8915-F qualified removal
Fact.Description:
The Part III twin of /ordinaryPensionDistributionsBeforeForm8915FRemoval. The three mutually exclusive traditional-IRA routes — the scalar intake, the Form 8606 Part I/II taxable amount for either filer, and the Form 1099-R collection — exactly as /taxableIraDistributions chooses between them inline, extracted so the Form 8915-F line 20 removal has a named minuend and can be compared with what the route is carrying.
NOTHING MOVED IN THE EXTRACTION. The body is the Switch verbatim, arm order and all; every committed return resolves the same figure, and the only reader is /taxableIraDistributions.
THE REMOVAL APPLIES TO THE CHOSEN ARM, WHICHEVER IT IS, and that is deliberate rather than convenient. Form 8915-F line 7 tells the filer to report the non-qualified excess "as IRA and/or pension and annuity distributions, as applicable, in accordance with the instructions for your tax return", so whichever of the three routes is carrying the traditional-IRA distribution is the route that must carry the excess only. On the Form 8606 arm the removal is $0 by construction: a qualified amount reported on Form 8606 lands on Form 8915-F line 18, and line 20 — the removal — is the part NOT reported there.

Fact.Name: Taxable IRA distributions
Fact.Description:
Taxable IRA distributions to report on line 4b of Form 1040. A fully-taxable traditional IRA distribution (/writableIraDistributionAmount) is reported here; complete-safe (0 when unanswered, identical to the prior stub value). The PARTIALLY-taxable case is now modeled — when the Form 8606 Part I intake is claimed, the pro-rata taxable amount (form8606:/form8606TaxableAmount, line 15c) reports here. The two intakes are mutually exclusive (form8606:/knockoutForm8606WithFullyTaxableIntake blocks a positive overlap). The scalar case fires only on an answered POSITIVE amount (a bare IsComplete precedence would let an answered-0 scalar intake shadow the 8606 case and silently drop the pro-rata taxable amount below the KO's >0 trigger — an answered 0 behaves like an unanswered intake for 4b routing, so the 8606 case computes); the positive-overlap state stays deterministic (scalar precedence) and KO'd. Flows into /totalIncome.
A THIRD route, the Form 1099-R collection (/taxableIraDistributionsFromForm1099Rs — the box-2a total NET of each item's QCD exclusion, per-item line4bTaxableAmount). It sits LAST among the three live cases, so the and Form 8606 arm selections above are untouched and every return without an IRA-flagged 1099-R still reaches the same case with the same value; the final Dollar 0 else-branch is likewise unchanged, and form1099Rs:/hasIraDistribution1099R is Complete false on every return with no IRA-flagged 1099-R. The three routes are mutually exclusive on any FILABLE return: /knockoutIraDistributionDoubleIntake blocks submission when an IRA-flagged 1099-R co-exists with a positive scalar amount or a claimed Form 8606.
TWO further quantities ride OUTSIDE the route Switch, and neither is one of the three mutually exclusive traditional-IRA routes. The FIRST is form8606:/form8606Line25cOrZero, the taxable part of a Roth IRA distribution (Form 8606 Part III lines 25a/25c), which the form sends to this same line 4b. It is added rather than made a fourth arm because Part III is not one of the three mutually exclusive traditional-IRA routes: form8606's Part III chain hangs off /writableForm8606RothIraDistributions and is not gated on /claimsForm8606, so a Roth-only filer selects no arm at all, and a filer who claims Part I or Part II can hold a Part III amount beside it. The term is complete-safe ($0 when Part III is unanswered), which is every committed scenario, so this line is byte-identical across the corpus.
The SECOND is form8915F:/form8915FLine26AmountSubjectToTaxOrZero, Form 8915-F line 26 ("Amount subject to tax ... Include this amount in the total on line 4b"), the Part III IRA qualified disaster distribution instalment. THE DOUBLE COUNT IS PREVENTED BY AN EXCLUSION TERM, not by a knockout: form1099Rs:/flowKnockoutRetirementQualifiedDisasterDistribution only refuses a Form 1099-R whose SELF-REPORTED ../qualifiedDisasterDistribution is Complete AND true, so a return that answers that box No, or leaves it blank, can still carry a current-year qualified disaster distribution through the 1099-R collection while the Part I writables (independent return-root intakes) claim the same distribution. The chosen ordinary route is /ordinaryIraDistributionsBeforeForm8915FRemoval less form8915F:/form8915FCurrentQualifiedIraTaxableRemoval. The instalment term below is complete-safe and $0 across the committed corpus. BOTH NEW TERMS ARE MIRRORED into /totalIncomeUpperBoundForIraMagi, which must keep DOMINATING this line for the section 219(g) proof to stay sound; the reasoning and the two obligations that mirror could not discharge are recorded there.

Fact.Name: Pensions And Annuities
Fact.Description:
Pensions and annuities to report on line 5a of Form 1040.
THE FOURTH ADDEND handles a rollover case that would otherwise be mishandled. A taxed DIRECT rollover whose box 2a equals box 1 became a fully taxable pension, so its gross reached line 5b and no line 5a, and the the pre-existing routing would have inherited the residual this Description names below. It is NOT that class. The residual below rests on the Fully taxable pensions and annuities rule ("If your pension or annuity is fully taxable, enter the total pension or annuity payments (from Form(s) 1099-R, box 1) on line 5b; don't make an entry on line 5a"; https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040gi.pdf, page 28). For a ROLLOVER the on-point paragraph overrides it and is unconditional: "Use lines 5a and 5b to report a rollover, including a direct rollover, from one qualified employer's plan to another or to an IRA" and "Enter on line 5a the distribution from Form 1099-R, box 1"; lines 1906-1925 of the same file, RIGHT column, the operative sentence at 1918-1919. form1099Rs:/fullyTaxablePensionRolloverGross is that box 1, for the fully taxable members only - the partly taxable ones already reach this line through /partlyTaxablePensions and summing both would double-count. It is $0 on every return that carries no taxed direct rollover, so this line is unmoved for every other return.
THE THIRD ADDEND handles the retired-public-safety-officer premium exclusion. A fully taxable pension normally contributes nothing here - box 1 and box 2a are equal, so the instruction lets line 5a stay blank and line 5b carry the figure alone. The retired-public-safety-officer premium exclusion breaks that equality WITHOUT touching box 2a, and the instruction says what then happens in the same breath as the exclusion itself: "Report your total distributions on line 5a and the taxable amount on line 5b." form1099Rs:/fullyTaxablePensionsWithPsoExclusionGross is that gross, and it is $0 on every return carrying no such form, so line 5a is unmoved for every other return. A PARTLY taxable form with an exclusion needs no term - the /partlyTaxablePensions addend already carries its gross - and the two collections are disjoint by construction (one filters on isFullyTaxable, the other on isPartlyTaxablePension), so no form is counted twice.
A NAMED RESIDUAL RIDES WITH THAT ADDEND, AND IT IS OLDER THAN THE ADDEND. This line can resolve BELOW /taxablePensionsAndAnnuities, which is incoherent on the printed form - line 5b is the taxable part of line 5a - and it reaches past the screen because this fact carries Export mef="true". THE CLASS IS PRE-EXISTING, by construction rather than by accident: this line is rollovers plus PARTLY-taxable gross, while line 5b is FULLY-taxable gross plus partly-taxable TAXABLE amounts, so a return carrying one ordinary fully taxable pension and nothing else already reports 5a = $0 against a positive 5b today. The instruction's own answer is broader than either fact - "Report your total distributions on line 5a" - and the pre-fill dictionary instead implements the Form 1040 convention that a wholly taxable pension may leave 5a blank.
WHAT THE PSO EXCLUSION DOES TO IT, stated rather than left for a reader to derive: it EXTENDS the class into a new population; it neither creates nor cures it. On a return mixing an electing fully-taxable form with a non-electing one, only the electing form's gross joins this line, 5a 40,000 against 5b 48,800. DIRECTION: the understatement is on the DISCLOSURE line only. Line 5b, AGI and the tax are untouched, because nothing downstream reads this fact as income - /totalIncome takes line 5b. The exposure is a mis-stated 5a on the printed form and in the MeF image, never a wrong tax.
NOT REDESIGNED HERE, deliberately. Making 5a the true "total distributions" means adding every fully taxable pension's gross to this line for every filer, which moves a printed line on a large share of committed returns and is a Form-1040 presentation decision in its own right - not something to fold into a section 402(l) exclusion fill. This is a named residual.
THE NAMED RESIDUAL ABOVE ALSO GAINS THE OPPOSITE DIRECTION, from Form 4972's Part II election (form1099r-form4972-part2-ordinary-income-to-line5b), and the direction is the point: every member named above UNDERSTATES this line, and this one OVERSTATES it. Form 4972's printed instructions, page 2 RIGHT column of a three-column extraction, item 2 (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f4972.pdf, page 2): a Part-II-only election reports "only the ordinary income portion of the distribution" on lines 5a AND 5b, that portion being "the amount from box 2a of Form 1099-R, minus the amount from box 3 of that form." Line 5b now carries exactly that. LINE 5a DOES NOT: a Part-II-only form with a positive box 3 has box 1 different from its effective taxable amount, so form1099Rs:../isPartlyTaxablePension admits it and the /partlyTaxablePensions addend puts BOX 1 here, which pins the overstatement rather than hiding it. THE EXPOSURE IS THE DISCLOSURE LINE ONLY, as for every other member of this class: nothing downstream reads this fact as income (/totalIncome takes line 5b), so line 5b, AGI and the tax are untouched. NOT FIXED HERE, deliberately: netting the capital gain part out of this line means a new per-form term and a new collection for a population of one election, and the same Form-1040 presentation decision the paragraph above declines to fold into a fill. A Part-II-only form with box 3 at $0 or blank is FULLY taxable and contributes nothing here, so the overstatement is exactly the box 3 amount and never more. California TY2025 reads this fact through its stateSystems export (Schedule CA (540), Schedule CA (540NR)).

Fact.Name: Form 1040 line 5b, the ordinary Form 1099-R route, BEFORE the Form 8915-F qualified removal
Fact.Description:
The Form 1099-R pension route exactly as /taxablePensionsAndAnnuities carries it inline — the fully taxable and partly taxable totals plus the Form 8958 community allocation, less the section 402(l) retired-public-safety-officer premium exclusion — extracted to a fact of its own so that the Form 8915-F qualified-amount removal has a named minuend and so that the removal can be COMPARED with what this route is actually carrying.
NOTHING MOVED IN THE EXTRACTION. The body is the Switch verbatim; every committed return resolves the same figure it did before, and the only reader is /taxablePensionsAndAnnuities.
WHY IT HAD TO BECOME A FACT. income:/knockoutForm8915FQualifiedAmountExceedsOrdinaryRoute has to ask whether the Form 8915-F line 10 removal is larger than the ordinary route it comes out of, and a knockout cannot reach inside another fact's Switch to find out.

Fact.Name: Taxable Pensions And Annuities
Fact.Description:
Taxable pensions and annuities to report on line 5b of Form 1040.
THE SUBTRAHEND is the retired-public-safety-officer premium exclusion, which IRC 402(l) takes out of gross income and which the instruction spends one sentence on - "If you make this election, reduce the otherwise taxable amount of your pension or annuity by the amount excluded." It cannot be netted into box 2a upstream, because "the amount shown in box 2a of Form 1099-R doesn't reflect the exclusion" is the printed rule and fourteen facts in form1099Rs read ../taxableAmount as the REPORTED figure. So it arrives here as its own term, the shape the line 4b side already uses for the QCD and HFD exclusions.
IT CANNOT DRIVE THIS LINE NEGATIVE. Every per-form term inside form1099Rs:/psoPremiumExclusion is bounded by that form's own form1099RFrontier:/form1099Rs/*/effectiveTaxableAmount, which is exactly the amount that form contributes to one of the two addends above, so each term is already inside the minuend; the per-filer $3,000 caps only lower the total further.
THE INCLUDIBILITY CEILING ON form1099Rs:/form1099Rs/*/psoExcludableAmount IS THE EFFECTIVE TAXABLE AMOUNT, NOT BOX 2a AS REPORTED: for an indirect rollover, reported box 2a is the PRE-rollover figure, so a ceiling keyed to it would admit an oversized subtrahend against the post-rollover addend (a $20,000 box 2a rolled over down to $2,000 would admit a $3,000 subtrahend against a $2,000 addend, and this Subtract carries no floor).
A display value for line 5b for the MeF XML and PDF
non taxable pension and annuities, used for calulating part of line 13b on Schedule R

Fact.Name: Taxable Pensions And Annuities literal code
Fact.Description: Indicates when there is a rollover.

Fact.Name: Form 1040 line 7b, "Schedule D not required" (Exception 1)
Fact.Description:
Form 1040 line 7b, LEFT checkbox: "Check if: Schedule D not required". DERIVED from the Form 1040 line 7a "Exception 1" conditions. It was a hard-wired False before this fact existed, on the premise that capital gain/loss was always zero in scope. Two things falsify that premise: this dictionary COMPUTES Schedule D (scheduleD.xml carries 23 of the 24 printed lines and /capitalGainOrLossForForm1040 routes the result), and /capitalGainsOrLosses already sends the Form 1099-DIV box 2a total straight to line 7a when /claimsCapitalGainsOrLosses is false. The box was the only part of that route still saying no.
THE PRINTED CONDITIONS, each one a leg of the All below. 2025 Instructions for Form 1040, Line 7a: "Exception 1. You don't have to file Form 8949 or Schedule D if you aren't deferring any capital gain by investing in a qualified opportunity fund and both of the following apply. 1. You have no capital losses, and your only capital gains are capital gain distributions from Form(s) 1099-DIV, box 2a (or substitute statements); and 2. None of the Form(s) 1099-DIV (or substitute statements) have an amount in box 2b (unrecaptured section 1250 gain), box 2c (section 1202 gain), or box 2d (collectibles (28%) gain)." Line 7b then says only: "If Exception 1 applies, check the 'Schedule D not required' box on line 7b."
LEG 1 — NOT scheduleD:/claimsCapitalGainsOrLosses. This is condition 1 as this dictionary holds it, and it is the SAME gate the dollar route uses, so line 7a and line 7b move together and can never disagree. /netCapitalGainOrLoss is identically $0 when the gate is false, so a filer on this path has no capital gain and no capital loss of any kind other than box 2a: every Schedule D input, the carryover and the Form 4684/4797/6252/6781/8824 legs included, sits behind that one gate.
LEG 2 — NOT scheduleD:/hasForm8949Transactions. Belt to leg 1's braces: /form8949Transactions is a top-level writable collection and nothing in the dictionary forces it empty when the Schedule D gate is answered no. A return that itemises a Form 8949 row while answering "no capital gains" is contradictory, and on a contradictory return the box stays UNCHECKED — never checked on the strength of an answer the other intake denies. This is the leg the round-5 records cross-reference asked for; it is expressed through the shipping any-row flag rather than through the six /hasForm8949Box{A..L}Transactions classifiers because that flag is their disjunction and one quantity gets one fact.
LEG 3 — dividendReports:/capitalGainDistributions greater than $0. The printed instruction is "enter your total capital gain distributions ... on line 7a AND check the box", so the box reports a filled line 7a, not an empty one. This leg is also what keeps every return with no capital activity at all byte-identical: without it a wage-only return would print a checked "Schedule D not required" box. The predecessor Description's own word for this was "nonzero", so the leg is inherited, not invented. NOTE THE ROUNDING BOUNDARY, pinned by the fixture pair sdnr-boundary-box2a-rounds-to-zero / sdnr-boundary-box2a-rounds-to-one-dollar: this leg tests the same Round(box 2a total + Form 8814 line 10) that /capitalGainsOrLosses prints on line 7a, so box 2a totalling $0.49 prints $0 on line 7a and leaves the box unchecked while $0.50 prints $1 and checks it. The box and the printed dollar cross the threshold together, which is the coupling that matters.
LEG 3 ALSO COUNTS FORM 8814 LINE 10. The child's capital gain distributions an IRC 1(g)(7) election puts on the parent's return (form8814:/form8814TotalLine10CapitalGainDistributions) reach line 7a by the same two routes as box 2a and are Form 1099-DIV box 2a distributions in the child's hands, and the Form 8814 Line 10 instruction says in as many words "Check the box on line 7b, 'Schedule D not required', if applicable". So leg 3 is now (box 2a + Form 8814 line 10) greater than $0, and the box, the printed line 7a and the line 7b "includes child's capital gain" box (/line7aIncludesChildCapitalGain) move together. ONE MORE GAP, OF THE SAME KIND AS (a): condition 2 is tested on the PARENT'S Forms 1099-DIV only; the child's intake carries no box 2b/2c/2d split (the gap named on form8814:/form8814Children/*/line10CapitalGainDistributionsIncluded), so a child whose distributions include unrecaptured 1250, 1202 or collectibles gain has the box checked when it should be unchecked — a display error in the same conservative direction as (a), and the dollar route has the same blind spot. THE CHILD-SUBCATEGORY GAP ABOVE IS CLOSED. LEG 7 reads Not(form8814:/form8814AnyChildHasSubcategoryCapitalGainDistributions). One elected child with an included box 2b, 2c or 2d amount leaves this checkbox unchecked, even when another child has ordinary capital gain distributions only. The exported flag is complete-safe FALSE for an unopened child collection; an included child's unanswered subcategory question remains Incomplete here, preserving that existing source's posture. This closes the checkbox obligation only; the separately named Schedule D rate-category consumers and the dollar-route residue below are unaffected.
LEGS 4-6 — none of box 2b, 2c or 2d present, condition 2, tested on the module aggregates /unrecapturedSection1250GainFromDividends, /section1202ExclusionFromDividends and /collectiblesGainFromDividends. Each aggregates a non-negative per-1099-DIV writable, UNROUNDED, so "greater than zero" is "some Form 1099-DIV has an amount in that box", cents included (a $0.30 box 2b is an amount in box 2b) and ONE such form disqualifies the whole return (fixture sdnr-multi-1099div-one-carries-box2d pins the any-not-every reading over a two-item collection).
THREE GAPS THIS FILL DOES NOT CLOSE AND DOES NOT HIDE. (a) BOX 2C IS PROXIED. Condition 2 names box 2c, the section 1202 GAIN; this dictionary holds only the section 1202 EXCLUSION the filer claims against it, so a filer with box 2c who claims no exclusion is not caught. The proxy errs by checking a box that should stay unchecked, which is a display error, not a dollar error — and the dollar route it accompanies has the same blind spot already. (b) THE QUALIFIED-OPPORTUNITY-FUND LEG IS NOT MODELLED. Exception 1 opens with "if you aren't deferring any capital gain by investing in a qualified opportunity fund"; the only QOF fact this dictionary holds is scheduleD:/writableDisposedOfQualifiedOpportunityFundInvestment, which asks about a DISPOSAL and not about a deferral, so it is not a proxy and is deliberately not used. A box-2a distribution is itself a deferrable gain, so the leg is not fully subsumed by legs 1 and 2. No intake exists to build it from. (c) THE 2B/2C/2D RESIDUE ON THE DOLLAR ROUTE. When one of those boxes IS present and the Schedule D gate is answered no, this fact correctly leaves the box unchecked, while /capitalGainsOrLosses still routes box 2a directly onto line 7a with no Schedule D attached — an inconsistent print. That is a pre-existing hole in the routing, not one this fact opens, and it belongs to /capitalGainsOrLosses.
VALUE MOVE (this rebody is a correction, brief invariant on byte-identity): three committed unit scenarios have box 2a above zero with the Schedule D gate unanswered, and their line 7b moves False to True. Every one of them is exactly the filer Exception 1 describes, and a checked box is the CORRECT print for them. No committed spine TSV carries this path, so no committed expectation file changes.
CITE SPELLING, the convention this repo already documents in dividendReports.xml: XML forbids a double hyphen inside a comment, so the authority comment below writes the two vendored file names with single hyphens. The exact on-disk spellings are https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f1040.pdf and https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040gi.pdf.
THE UNBELTED-BYPASS CLASS, named once rather than chased with legs (the D2 landing review's L1): amounts that enter the capital-gain chain OUTSIDE the two gates this fact reads - carryovers, the collapsed nets, the 1a/8a rows, K-1 lines 5/12, form4797's section 1231 LTCG portion and form4684's casualty gain (both added at /longTermGainOrLossAfterCarryover) - can leave the box CHECKED on a return that nonetheless files Schedule D by another rule. Dollar-inert (the gate zeroes value only at /netCapitalGainOrLoss); the box is display, and a wrongly-checked box on a Schedule-D-filing return is the conservative misprint.

Fact.Name: Capital Gains or Losses
Fact.Description: Capital gain or (loss) for line 7 of the 1040, from Schedule D line 16 (with the line-21 loss limitation applied). Adds the "Schedule D not required" path for 1099-DIV box 2a capital gain distributions. When Schedule D IS filed (/claimsCapitalGainsOrLosses), box 2a is already inside /capitalGainOrLossForForm1040 (folded into Schedule D line 13 → line 15 → line 16), so nothing is added here — no double count. When Schedule D is NOT required (the taxpayer answered no to other capital transactions but has box-2a distributions), /capitalGainOrLossForForm1040 is 0 and the box-2a total is routed directly onto Form 1040 line 7 (the Form 1040 line-7 "if not required, check here" path). The direct line 7a amount is Round(box 2a total + Form 8814 line 10): the box 2a total arrives unrounded and the line is rounded once ("include cents when adding the amounts and round off only the total", https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040gi.pdf, page 23).

Fact.Name: State and local income tax refund calculation route options
Fact.Description: No prior-year tax benefit, the ordinary immediately-preceding-year worksheet, or the Publication 525 recovery calculation required by an exception in the instructions.

Fact.Name: State and local income tax refund calculation route
Fact.Description: The route established from the imported current refund and prior-year return records. A positive refund cannot resolve until one of the three source-grounded routes is known.

Fact.Name: Personal Form 1099-G box 2 refunds received
Fact.Description: The state and local income tax refunds, credits, or offsets reported in box 2 of the filer's Forms 1099-G that count toward the Schedule 1 line 1 recovery: every personal refund for 2024 (box 8 not checked), plus every personal refund for another year when the recovery is figured under Publication 525 or has no prior-year tax benefit. A refund with box 8 checked is not included. $0 when no Form 1099-G is listed. Incomplete while a listed document's box 8 or refund year is unknown, and while a refund for a year other than 2024 is present on the 2024 worksheet route or before the route is chosen, because that refund is figured under Publication 525.

Fact.Name: Personal Form 1099-G box 2 refunds for another year, on the Publication 525 or no-benefit route
Fact.Description: The personal box 2 refunds of the filer's Forms 1099-G that are for a tax year other than 2024. $0 when there are none. When there are some, the amount counts only on the Publication 525 route and the no-tax-benefit route; on the 2024 worksheet route, or before the route is chosen, it is Incomplete, because the 2024 worksheet does not measure a refund for another year.

Fact.Name: State and local income tax refund, credit, or offset received
Fact.Description: The raw current-year recovery reported on Form 1099-G or a similar government statement, including a refund applied to estimated tax. This is not yet the taxable amount. Use this amount only for a refund shown on a statement that is not a Form 1099-G; a Form 1099-G is entered once, as an item of unemployment:/form1099Gs, and its box 2 is not entered here again.

Fact.Name: Complete-safe state and local income tax refund received
Fact.Description: The raw recovery when a source record exists, otherwise zero because no refund document or government statement was supplied. A supplied positive recovery still requires an explicit tax-benefit calculation route below. When the return lists its Forms 1099-G (unemployment:/form1099Gs), this adds their personal box 2 refunds (/form1099GPersonalBox2RefundTotal) to any refund shown on another statement.

Fact.Name: Other state and local income-tax refunds, complete safe
Fact.Description: The refund shown on a statement other than a Form 1099-G when answered, otherwise Complete $0, so it can be added beside the Form 1099-G box 2 refunds.

Fact.Name: Prior-year Schedule A line 5d state and local taxes
Fact.Description: The state and local tax amount shown on the prior-year Schedule A line 5d, imported from the prior-year return record.

Fact.Name: Prior-year Schedule A line 5e allowed state and local tax deduction
Fact.Description: The prior-year state and local tax deduction after its federal limit, imported from the prior-year return record.

Fact.Name: Prior-year total itemized deductions
Fact.Description: The total itemized deductions from prior-year Schedule A line 17, imported from the prior-year return record. On a 2024 Form 1040-NR the same amount is Schedule A (Form 1040-NR) line 8, which is the line Publication 525 Worksheet 2 names for that filer; enter that amount here.

Fact.Name: Prior-year filing status options
Fact.Description: The filing-status choices needed to reconstruct the 2024 State and Local Income Tax Refund Worksheet lines 5 through 7.

Fact.Name: Prior-year filing status
Fact.Description: SCREEN. Which filing status did you use on your prior federal return? This is needed only when the prior-year state-refund worksheet reaches lines 5 through 7. The filing status for this return is not a substitute because it can differ from the prior-year status. form6251:/form8801PriorYearFilingStatusWasMarriedFilingSeparately also reads it when the Form 8801 question about the prior-year status is unanswered.

Fact.Name: Prior-year return form and dual-status box options
Fact.Description: The three 2024 return shapes the State and Local Income Tax Refund Worksheet has to tell apart before it can import a 2024 standard deduction: a Form 1040-NR, a Form 1040 or 1040-SR with the dual-status standard deduction box checked, and a Form 1040 or 1040-SR without that box checked. The first two carry a zero 2024 standard deduction.

Fact.Name: The 2024 return, and its dual-status standard deduction box
Fact.Description: SCREEN. Which one describes your 2024 federal return? Choose the Form 1040-NR option only if the 2024 return itself was a Form 1040-NR, the nonresident alien return. Choose the checked-box option if the 2024 return was a Form 1040 or 1040-SR on which the box labeled "Spouse itemizes on a separate return or you were a dual-status alien" was checked; a dual-status alien who was a resident at the end of 2024 files that return and checks that box. Choose the last option if the 2024 return was a Form 1040 or 1040-SR with that box left unchecked, which is where a dual-status alien belongs who filed a joint return with a spouse who was a U.S. citizen or resident alien at the end of 2024 and elected to be taxed on their combined worldwide income, because that election says not to check the box. This is asked only when the state and local income tax refund worksheet reaches lines 5 through 7, and it is about 2024 alone: a filer who is a resident for 2025 may still have filed Form 1040-NR for 2024, and the 2025 filing status is not a substitute. Either of the first two answers makes the prior-year standard deduction in that worksheet zero and leaves the whole 2024 itemized deduction available to be recovered: a nonresident alien filing Form 1040-NR could not claim the standard deduction, and the 2024 standard deduction is zero for anyone who checked that box, even if born before January 2, 1960, or blind. That box is a single box shared with the married filing separately spouse-itemized rule, so a filer whose 2024 spouse itemized on a separate return may truthfully choose the checked-box option; it reaches the same zero as the separate spouse-itemized answer, and the two answers are not cross-checked against each other. A 2024 Form 1040-NR filer's refund is calculated under Publication 525 rather than the printed worksheet, whose line 5 is written for a 2024 Form 1040 or 1040-SR. A Form 1040-NR answer is followed by one more question, whether the filer was a student or business apprentice eligible for the U.S.-India income tax treaty's standard deduction, because that treaty lets such a filer claim the standard deduction on Form 1040-NR; a yes keeps the 2024 standard deduction in the worksheet.

Fact.Name: The 2024 Form 1040-NR filer could claim the standard deduction under the U.S.-India treaty
Fact.Description: SCREEN. Asked only when the 2024 return was a Form 1040-NR. Answer yes if, in 2024, you were a student or business apprentice eligible for the benefits of Article 21(2) of the United States-India Income Tax Treaty. Such a filer can claim the standard deduction on Form 1040-NR if they do not itemize, so the 2024 standard deduction they could have claimed is compared with the 2024 itemized deductions exactly as it is for a Form 1040 filer; answer yes even if you itemized in 2024. A yes uses the 2024 standard deduction for the 2024 filing status (single, married filing separately or qualifying surviving spouse, the statuses a Form 1040-NR can carry) plus your own age and blindness additions; no spouse boxes are counted. A married filer whose spouse filed a return and itemized in 2024 could not take the standard deduction, and the married filing separately spouse-itemized answer still makes it zero. A no, or no answer, makes the 2024 standard deduction zero, the rule for every other nonresident alien.

Fact.Name: Primary filer was 65 or older at the end of 2024
Fact.Description: The primary filer was born before January 2, 1960, the TY2024 worksheet's age test for the additional standard deduction.

Fact.Name: Primary filer was blind on the 2024 return
Fact.Description: SCREEN. Was the primary filer blind for purposes of the additional standard deduction claimed on the 2024 federal return? This is the prior-year Form 1040 blindness box; the 2025 answer can differ.

Fact.Name: Secondary filer was 65 or older on the 2024 return
Fact.Description: SCREEN. If you filed jointly in 2024, or married filing separately and your spouse had no income, was not filing a return, and could not be claimed as a dependent, was your spouse born before January 2, 1960? Answer from the 2024 return. The prior-year spouse may not be a filer on this 2025 return.

Fact.Name: Secondary filer was blind on the 2024 return
Fact.Description: SCREEN. If you filed jointly in 2024, or married filing separately and your spouse had no income, was not filing a return, and could not be claimed as a dependent, was your spouse blind for purposes of the additional standard deduction on that return? Answer from the 2024 return.

Fact.Name: Prior-year MFS spouse itemized deductions
Fact.Description: SCREEN. If the 2024 filing status was married filing separately, did your spouse itemize deductions on their separate 2024 return? The 2024 standard deduction is zero when either spouse itemizes.

Fact.Name: Prior-year MFS spouse qualifies for age and blindness boxes
Fact.Description: SCREEN. If the 2024 filing status was married filing separately, did your spouse have no income, not file a return, and not qualify as someone's dependent? The spouse age and blindness boxes on that separate return may be checked only when all three are true.

Fact.Name: TY2024 basic standard deduction
Fact.Description: The TY2024 filing-status base, before the per-box age and blindness additions.

Fact.Name: TY2024 additional standard deduction per age or blindness box
Fact.Description: The 2024 amount for each checked age or blindness box. Single and head-of- household returns use $1,950; married filing jointly, married filing separately, and qualifying surviving spouse returns use $1,550.

Fact.Name: Primary filer's TY2024 age addition
Primary filer's TY2024 blindness addition
Secondary filer's TY2024 age addition
Secondary filer's TY2024 blindness addition
Prior-year standard deduction available for the refund worksheet
Fact.Description:
The prior-year standard deduction including age and blindness additions. This is zero when the filer was required to itemize because an MFS spouse itemized, exactly implementing the worksheet instruction to skip lines 5 through 7 and carry line 4.
The prior-year lump-sum writable is replaced with the TY2024 filing- status base plus the separate age and blindness boxes from the 2024 return. The current return's filing status is not used as a proxy. The inputs are required when this worksheet reaches lines 5-7; unanswered prior-year facts leave this amount Incomplete. The MFS spouse- itemized case resolves zero under IRC 63(c)(6)(A). It is also zero when the 2024 return was a Form 1040-NR, because a nonresident alien filing that return could not claim the standard deduction, and equally zero when the 2024 return was a Form 1040 or 1040-SR carrying a checked "Spouse itemizes on a separate return or you were a dual-status alien" box, which is the 2024 instructions' own exception; the whole 2024 itemized deduction is then available to be recovered. The one Form 1040-NR exception is a student or business apprentice eligible for the U.S.-India treaty's standard deduction: that filer keeps the 2024 standard deduction for a single, married filing separately or qualifying surviving spouse status plus their own age and blindness additions, unless married filing separately with a spouse who itemized. Any other 2024 filing status, which a Form 1040-NR cannot carry, or an unanswered treaty question, gets the zero every other Form 1040-NR filer gets. The 2024 return shape is required here: when it is missing this amount stays Incomplete rather than assuming an unchecked box on a 2024 Form 1040 and granting a standard deduction the filer may never have had.

Fact.Name: Publication 525 taxable state and local income tax refund amount
Fact.Description: The exact Schedule 1 line 1 allocation produced from the prior-year return recomputation when any Form 1040 instruction exception requires Publication 525. This source record is bounded below by zero and capped at the raw income-tax recovery below.

Fact.Name: State and Local Income Tax Refund Worksheet line 1
Fact.Description: The smaller of the current recovery and prior-year Schedule A line 5d.

Fact.Name: State and Local Income Tax Refund Worksheet line 2
Fact.Description: Prior-year Schedule A line 5d less line 5e, floored at zero.

Fact.Name: State and Local Income Tax Refund Worksheet line 3
Fact.Description: The recovery remaining after the state-and-local-tax deduction limit interaction.

Fact.Name: State and Local Income Tax Refund Worksheet line 8
Fact.Description: The prior-year itemized deductions that exceeded the standard deduction the filer could have claimed, or all itemized deductions when the prior-year standard deduction was unavailable.

Fact.Name: Taxable refund from the ordinary Schedule 1 line 1 worksheet
Fact.Description: The smaller of worksheet line 3 and line 8: the recovery bounded by both the SALT-limit interaction and the prior-year deduction that actually reduced taxable income.

Fact.Name: Taxable refunds, credits, or offsets of state and local income taxes
Fact.Description: Schedule 1 line 1. No supplied recovery is complete-safe zero. A positive recovery resolves only through the no-tax-benefit route, the ordinary prior-year worksheet, or the exact Publication 525 result for exception cases; there is no silent positive-refund fallback. While the refund received is Incomplete (a listed Form 1099-G whose box 8 or refund year is unknown, or a personal refund for a year other than 2024 on the 2024 worksheet route) this result is Incomplete. Box 8 trade-or-business refunds are not part of this line.

Fact.Name: Has Other Income
Fact.Description:
Whether Schedule 1 Part I discloses ANY reportable entry. This is what decides whether Schedule 1 must be attached (feeds /requiresSchedule1, which is the printed form's own `includeWhen`) — NOT whether the Part I net is positive.
PREVIOUSLY the body was `GreaterThan(/otherIncome, $0)`, which tests the SIGN of a sum rather than the EXISTENCE of an entry. /otherIncome sums Schedule 1 lines 1, 7 and 9 (see /otherIncome's own Description), and line 9 itself (/schedule1TotalOtherIncome) can be NEGATIVE or exactly ZERO while a reportable Part I entry still exists: Schedule 1 lines 8a (the NOL deduction, /schedule1Line8aNetOperatingLossDeduction), 8d (the Form 2555 foreign earned income exclusion, form2555:/schedule1Line8dForeignEarnedIncomeExclusion) and 8s (the Medicaid waiver payment back-out, /schedule1Line8sNontaxableMedicaidWaiverBackOutOrZero) are the schedule's own PREPRINTED-PARENTHESES fields, entered "as a negative number" per the Form 1040 instructions (see /schedule1Line8aNetOperatingLossDeduction's own Description, which quotes the instruction), and are the ONLY THREE addends of /schedule1TotalOtherIncome capable of being negative — every other addend is a complete-safe OrZero wrapper around a Dollar intake with a Min-0 Limit, or a CollectionSum/LesserOf of nonnegative amounts (each enumerated on /schedule1TotalOtherIncome's own Description). Line 1 (taxable state/local refunds) and line 7 (unemployment compensation, tested independently by unemployment:/receivedUnemploymentCompensation as its own /requiresSchedule1 disjunct) are both complete-safe zero-or-positive too. So the ONLY way for /otherIncome to be negative or exactly zero while a Part I entry exists is for one of these three signed addends to be nonzero — dominating the sum (Schedule 1 nets to a LOSS, taxpayer-adverse: the loss never reaches Form 1040 line 8 and total income is overstated) or exactly offset by a nonnegative addend elsewhere (case (b), offsetting entries netting to $0: a disclosure/completeness defect, since neither entry prints). A bare `NotEqual(/otherIncome, $0)` would fix case (a) but not case (b) — NotEqual(0, 0) is false — so existence is tested as: /otherIncome itself nonzero, OR any one of the three signed addends itself nonzero.
THE SOURCE. Schedule 1 line 9, "Total other income. Add lines 8a through 8z," and line 10, "Combine lines 1 through 7 and 9" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f1040s1.pdf, page 1), condition the schedule's content on having entries to total — the Part I line list carries no minimum-total or sign language, and the schedule's own heading, "Additional Income and Adjustments to Income" (source line 2), states its purpose as reporting the entries themselves. A negative or exactly-offsetting Part I total is not "no additional income" — for the NOL and Medicaid-waiver cases specifically it is additional income AND an additional required disclosure that happens to sum low.
UNCHANGED: an unanswered Part I — every one of the three signed addends complete-safe $0, every other addend complete-safe $0 — still resolves /otherIncome Complete $0 and every disjunct below Complete false, so this fact is Complete false exactly as before. No committed scenario answers any of the three signed addends together with an offsetting entry, so no committed scenario's printed values move; the two returns that DO move (nol-line-8a-deduction-negative-entry, and the third disjunct's own schedule1-line8s-medicaid-waiver-negative) were node-test fixtures pinning the defect itself, not committed scenarios, and are updated by this unit — see the unit report.
THE EXISTENCE TEST SPANS THE WHOLE OF PART I, not just /otherIncome: a Schedule C/E/F loss flowing into Part I with no other income has the same effect. The fix above reaches only /otherIncome and its three signed line-8 addends, and /otherIncome is Schedule 1 lines 1, 7 and 9 ONLY (see its own Description). The FIVE remaining Part I legs that the printed line 10 combines — line 2a alimony received (alimony:/taxableAlimonyReceived), line 3 business income or (loss) (scheduleC:/scheduleCNetProfitSubjectToUsTax, with the Form 8958 line 5 half scheduleC:/communityPropertyScheduleCAllocationAdjustmentUnrounded that the same printed line carries), line 4 other gains or (losses) (form4797:/form4797OrdinaryIncome), line 5 rental real estate, royalties, partnerships and S corporations (scheduleE:/scheduleETotalIncome) and line 6 farm income or (loss) (scheduleF:/scheduleFNetProfitOrLoss) — reach Form 1040 line 9 as DIRECT addends of /totalIncome rather than through /otherIncome, so they were not merely netted away: they were never tested here at all. A return whose ONLY Schedule 1 Part I entry is one of those five printed Form 1040 line 8 from /schedule1Line10AdditionalIncome while /requiresSchedule1 never turned true. The two ordinary shapes are alimony received under a pre-2019 instrument, and a Schedule C, E or F LOSS — a PROFIT already reaches /requiresSchedule1 through /hasAdjustmentsToIncome, because the deductible part of self-employment tax is a Part II adjustment, while a loss produces no such adjustment. Each of the six is now its own NotEqual disjunct, reading the SAME identities /schedule1Line10AdditionalIncome and /totalIncome read, so the existence test now spans the whole of Part I. THE SOURCE for the five line identities: https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f1040s1.pdf, page 1 (2a "Alimony received"), 19 (3 "Business income or (loss). Attach Schedule C"), 20 (4 "Other gains or (losses)"), 21 (5 "Rental real estate, royalties, partnerships, S corporations, trusts, etc."), 22 (6 "Farm income or (loss). Attach Schedule F") and 56-57 (10 "Combine lines 1 through 7 and 9. This is your additional income. Enter here and on Form 1040, 1040-SR, or 1040-NR, line 8").
COMPLETE-SAFE. No consumer's completeness moves: the only reader, /requiresSchedule1, was already Incomplete wherever this fact is not Complete true. Witnesses, one per new leg, each with every other leg $0: node tests with only alimony, only a Schedule C loss, only a Form 8958 community-property half, only a Form 4797 ordinary loss, only a Schedule E royalty loss and only a Schedule F loss each require Schedule 1.
STILL NOT TESTED, disclosed rather than fixed: an INNER net inside one leg. A Schedule E whose rental profit and partnership loss cancel to exactly $0 on line 5, or a Schedule C pair of businesses that cancel on line 3, still leaves that leg $0 and this fact blind to the entries behind it. Reaching those needs a per-entry existence test inside each schedule's own module, not a further term here.

Fact.Name: Has Adjustments to Income
Fact.Description: Does the taxpayer have adjustments to income reported in Schedule 1 Part 2?

Fact.Name: Schedule 1 source claims
Fact.Description: Source-presence disjunction for Schedule 1 attachment. This intermediate preserves the existing source census while allowing the public attachment fact to make an explicit, complete-safe false when one optional source claim is still unanswered.

Fact.Name: Schedule 1 source claims, complete-safe
Fact.Description: The Schedule 1 source-presence disjunction, or false when an optional source claim is unanswered. The attachment decision must not remain Placeholder merely because a filer has not opened an unrelated optional interview.

Fact.Name: Requires Schedule 1
Fact.Description:
Does the taxpayer need to file Schedule 1?
The attachment gate includes every Schedule 1 Part I source that has a complete-safe claim or presence fact: line 1 refunds, line 2a taxable alimony, line 3 Schedule C, line 4 Form 4684 or Form 4797, line 5 Schedule E, line 6 Schedule F, line 7 unemployment, and line 9 other income. An ordinary return with none of those sources resolves a complete-safe false, so the IRS1040S1 includeWhen gate is explicit rather than relying on an Incomplete value as a falsy proxy. This unit widens the source census for lines 2a through 6; a Form 4797 like-kind carry-in answered without a section-1245 disposition remains a named residual because no separate claim gate exists for that Form 8824 input.

Fact.Name: Gambling winnings not reported on a Form W-2G (Schedule 1 line 8b portion)
Fact.Description: OPTIONAL: gambling winnings NOT reported to the taxpayer on a Form W-2G (casual winnings under the payer reporting thresholds). Same Schedule 1 line 8b as the W-2G total — the two sum on the line. Carried GROSS: gambling losses are a Schedule A itemized deduction, never netted here.

Fact.Name: Jury duty pay (Schedule 1 line 8h)
Fact.Description: OPTIONAL: jury duty pay received. NOTE (disclosed limitation): jury duty pay GIVEN TO AN EMPLOYER is a Schedule 1 line 24a adjustment (i1040gi line 8h points there) — line 24a is not modeled by this unit, so a taxpayer who surrendered pay to an employer would overstate AGI.

Fact.Name: Prizes and awards (Schedule 1 line 8i)
Fact.Description:
OPTIONAL: prizes and awards. INTERPRETATION: scoped here to non-gambling, non-trade-or-business prizes — the i1040gi Line 8i text itself only cross-references line 8m; gambling prizes belong on 8b and business prizes on Schedule C, so this reading routes each category to its own line rather than double-counting. Tagged provisional.
ALSO EXCLUDES a prize or award already reported on a Form 1099-MISC the filer entered and characterised as a prize on that document's screen (form1099Misc:/form1099Miscs/*/ writableBox3Characterisation) — that amount is counted automatically through form1099Misc:/form1099MiscPrizesAndAwards, an addend of /prizesAwardsIncome below. Enter a prize here only when it did NOT come with a Form 1099-MISC, or the 1099-MISC has not been entered yet.

Fact.Name: Non-W-2G gambling winnings (complete-safe, Schedule 1 line 8b portion)
Fact.Description: /writableOtherGamblingIncome when answered, else 0.

Fact.Name: Jury duty pay (complete-safe, Schedule 1 line 8h)
Fact.Description: /writableJuryDutyPay when answered, else 0 (see /otherGamblingIncome). California TY2025 reads this fact through its stateSystems export (Schedule CA (540), Schedule CA (540NR)).

Fact.Name: Prizes and awards (complete-safe, Schedule 1 line 8i)
Fact.Description: /writablePrizesAwards when answered, else 0 (see /otherGamblingIncome), PLUS form1099Misc:/form1099MiscPrizesAndAwards — the box 3 amount of every Form 1099-MISC the filer characterised as a prize or award. The two legs cannot double-count: the manual writable is scoped (see its own Description) to exclude a prize already reported on a 1099-MISC, and the 1099-MISC leg excludes itself from the OTHER Schedule 1 line, 8z (form1099Misc:/form1099MiscOtherIncome), by the same writableBox3Characterisation answer. California TY2025 reads this fact through its stateSystems export (Schedule CA (540), Schedule CA (540NR)).

Fact.Name: The wages earned while an inmate are NOT part of the Form W-2 box 1 wages or self-employment income already entered on this return
Fact.Description:
