OPTIONAL (three-state) router for the ONE inmate-compensation amount this dictionary collects, eitc:/writableInmatePenalInstitutionCompensation. TRUE means the filer followed the printed CAUTION — the amount is not inside any wage or self-employment figure entered here, so it needs its Schedule 1 line 8u placement and needs NO EIC exclusion (it was never in the earned-income base). FALSE, and unanswered, mean the amount arrived through the ordinary wage/self-employment intake and is already inside Form 1040 line 1z, so it needs the EIC exclusion and must NOT be placed again.
UNANSWERED IS THE PRESERVING ARM, deliberately. Every return authored before this fact existed leaves it unanswered, resolves FALSE through /incarceratedWagesOutsideReportedIncome, and computes byte-identical to its pre-L8U self: line 8u contributes $0 and the EIC exclusion is subtracted exactly as it was. The new arm is reachable only by answering TRUE.
ASKED AGAINST DOCUMENTS, NOT AGAINST THE OUTPUT. The question names the box 1 wages and the self-employment income the filer has ALREADY entered, rather than asking the filer to predict which line the software will print. That is the same discipline applied to the EITC writable's Name; the difference is that the answer now reaches the graph instead of only the screen.

Fact.Name: Inmate wages sit outside the reported wage/self-employment income (complete-safe)
Fact.Description:
/writableIncarceratedWagesOutsideReportedIncome when answered, else FALSE — the complete-safe alias pattern of form8889:/hasTopLevelHsaPledgedAsSecurity, and it is load bearing rather than decorative. This boolean is read inside the When of a Switch on BOTH sides of the seam: here by /schedule1Line8uIncarceratedWages, which feeds /schedule1TotalOtherIncome -> /otherIncome -> /totalIncome, and in eitc by /inmatePenalInstitutionCompensationInEarnedIncome, which feeds /eitcEarnedIncomeBase. A bare Dependency on the unanswered writable would propagate ITS completeness into both cones, turning /totalIncome and /eitcEarnedIncomeBase from Complete to Placeholder on every return that never answers it — the same contagion eitc:/inmatePenalInstitutionCompensation's own IsComplete guard exists to stop, and a real regression rather than a value change. The False literal is unconditionally Complete, so both cones stay Complete exactly as before.
Pinned by tests/nodes/ty2025/income/l8u-router-and-amount-unanswered-stay-complete, which leaves both the router and the amount unanswered and asserts Complete on the whole chain.

Fact.Name: Wages earned while incarcerated (Schedule 1 line 8u)
Fact.Description:
Schedule 1 line 8u, "Wages earned while incarcerated. Enter the amount that you received for services performed while an inmate in a penal institution." A PLACEMENT line, not a back-out line — which is exactly why the Form 1040 line 1a CAUTION can say "Do not report these wages on line 1a" — so this leg ADDS to Schedule 1 line 9 and thence to Form 1040 line 8. Contrast Schedule 1 line 8s, the Medicaid-waiver line, whose own heading says the amount is INCLUDED on line 1a or 1d and which the EIC Step 5 worksheet therefore subtracts; 8u has no such heading and the worksheet prints no inmate line, because 8u has already routed the amount out of line 1z.
THE OPERAND IS THE EITC MODULE'S ATTESTED AMOUNT, READ THROUGH ITS EXISTING COMPLETE-SAFE, ALREADY-ROUNDED WRAPPER eitc:/inmatePenalInstitutionCompensation, and that is the whole of the de-duplication. There is no second dollar intake for line 8u: the figure the filer typed once for the EIC question is the figure that lands here, and /incarceratedWagesOutsideReportedIncome decides which of the two consumers gets it. The arithmetic invariant the seam guarantees, asserted in both arms of the boundary pair tests/nodes/ty2025/income/l8u-incarcerated-wages-routed-to-line-8u and l8u-incarcerated-wages-included-in-reported-wages:
/schedule1Line8uIncarceratedWages + eitc:/inmatePenalInstitutionCompensationInEarnedIncome == eitc:/inmatePenalInstitutionCompensation
The attested dollars are placed exactly once — never zero times, never twice.
NO ROUND OF ITS OWN, unlike the six sibling legs on this same Add. Those Round because they read RAW writables; this one reads an operand that eitc already Rounded at this very printed line under the page 23 whole-dollar election, whose textual hook IS Schedule 1 line 8u. A second Round would be identity at best and, if the operand ever stopped being whole, would silently move that boundary.
direction: the $0 tail of the Switch fires when the router is FALSE or unanswered, and it is the PRE-EXISTING behaviour rather than a gap leg — on that arm the amount is inside Form 1040 line 1z already, so a $0 here is the CORRECT figure, not a placeholder, and adding it would OVER-state total income by double-counting. The direction of the residual error is recorded below and it belongs to the router, not to this default.
THE RESIDUAL, NAMED RATHER THAN CLAIMED AWAY. This unit does not eliminate the double-count hazard; it MOVES it from "the filer answered two amount questions" (which nothing in the data could detect) to "the filer answered one router question wrongly" (which the filer can check against documents already entered). Two populations are still imperfectly served and neither is silently wrong:
(1) THE FORM W-2 HALF, and it is a HANDOFF, not a gap this module can close. The filer who holds a Form W-2 whose box 1 ALREADY includes the inmate wages cannot both enter that W-2 (so its box 2 withholding reaches Form 1040 line 25a) and keep the wages off line 1a: box 1 flows to formW2s:/primaryFilerWages whole. That filer must answer the router FALSE, which is CORRECT for them under this design — their return computes the same right numbers it computed before L8U, with the amount on line 1a instead of line 8u. The placement is off the printed instruction; the arithmetic is not. Closing it needs a per-W-2 incarcerated-wages carve-out of box 1 in dictionary/ty2025/formW2s.xml that preserves box 2, which is not built.
(2) THE SCHEDULE C VARIANT. A filer who received Form 1099 inmate compensation and ALSO reported it as Schedule C gross receipts has it inside scheduleSE:/selfEmploymentEarnedIncome; answering the router TRUE would place it on line 8u a second time and strip the EIC exclusion it does need. The router's own question names self-employment income for exactly this reason. Direction if answered wrongly: total income OVER-stated and the EIC base OVER-stated — taxpayer-unfavourable on income, taxpayer-favourable on the credit, and visible on the printed return rather than buried. California TY2025 reads this fact through its stateSystems export (Schedule CA (540), Schedule CA (540NR)).

Fact.Name: Income for officer or crew service on a vessel engaged in fishing (Pub. 505 fishing item)
Fact.Description:
OPTIONAL: the filer's income for services as an officer or crew member of a vessel WHILE THE VESSEL IS ENGAGED IN FISHING. The second bullet of Pub. 505's gross income from fishing list.
A CARVE-OUT OF INCOME ALREADY REPORTED, never an addition to it — see the block comment above. Crew pay arrives as W-2 wages or as Schedule C business income and is already in /totalIncome through those paths; this fact records how much of it is FISHING income, for the estimated-tax two-thirds numerator alone.
AT SEA, NOT ASHORE, and the distinction is the printed one: this bullet says "while the vessel is engaged in fishing", and SHORE service is expressly an item of the SEPARATE "services normally performed in connection with fishing" bullet (/writableOtherFishingServicesIncome). A filer with both answers both; putting shore pay here would not change the sum, but it would make the two facts unable to say what they record. Min 0: the bullet names income for services, and no printed form gives it a loss shape. interpretation:provisional.

Fact.Name: Exxon Valdez taxable interest and punitive damage awards (Pub. 505 fishing item)
Fact.Description:
OPTIONAL: certain taxable interest and punitive damage awards received in connection with the Exxon Valdez litigation. The fourth bullet of Pub. 505's gross income from fishing list, and the one that is least obviously fishing income until the list is read.
A CARVE-OUT, like its siblings: such interest is already reported as taxable interest and such damages as other income, so both are already inside /totalIncome. This records the portion that counts as FISHING income for the two-thirds numerator.
"CERTAIN" IS THE PUBLICATION'S OWN WORD AND IT IS NOT NARROWED HERE. Pub. 505 says "Certain taxable interest and punitive damage awards received in connection with the Exxon Valdez litigation" and defines no test for which are which; no other vendored source in this repo does either. So the attestation carries the printed phrase and the filer's determination, and this fact does NOT invent a qualifying rule — inventing one is the fabrication invariant #3 forbids. Min 0. interpretation:provisional.

Fact.Name: Income for services normally performed in connection with fishing (Pub. 505 fishing item)
Fact.Description:
OPTIONAL: income for services NORMALLY PERFORMED IN CONNECTION WITH fishing — the fifth and last bullet of Pub. 505's gross income from fishing list.
ITS SCOPE IS PRINTED, and the fill did not have to guess: "Services normally performed in connection with fishing include: Shore service as an officer or crew member of a vessel engaged in fishing; and Services that are necessary for the immediate preservation of the catch, such as cleaning, icing, and packing the catch." So this covers SHORE service and catch-preservation work — cleaning, icing, packing — and it is the complement of /writableFishingVesselCrewServiceIncome, which is service AT SEA while the vessel is engaged in fishing.
WHERE THAT DEFINITION LIVES IS A TRAP WORTH KNOWING: it is in the MIDDLE column of the three-column extraction at lines 1518-1524, about eighty-five lines BEFORE the bullet it defines at line 1619. A successor reading the left column alone finds the bullet with no definition and could reasonably conclude none is printed. One is.
A CARVE-OUT of income already reported as wages or business income, not an addition to it — see the block comment above. Min 0. interpretation:provisional.

Fact.Name: Pub. 505's three fishing-services items, combined (exported, unwired)
Fact.Description:
The sum of the three Pub. 505 fishing items that no form line isolates — officer/crew service at sea, Exxon Valdez interest and punitive damages, and services normally performed in connection with fishing — each complete-safe $0 when unanswered, so this resolves Complete 0 on every return that answers none of them (which is every committed scenario).
THREE OF THE FIVE FISHING BULLETS, NOT ALL FIVE, and the missing two are named so this total is not mistaken for the fishing numerator. Bullet 1 is Schedule C LINE 7, which this dictionary does not model (it models line 1 gross receipts, and cost of goods sold is folded inside the collapsed /scheduleCs/*/writableTotalExpenses where nothing can extract it). Bullet 3 is the K-1 share, which ships as the three scheduleE aggregates (/k1GrossFarmingFishingIncome, /k1FarmingFishingIncomeSCorp, /estateTrustGrossFarmingFishingIncome) — those boxes are COMBINED farming-and-fishing figures, so they serve both of Pub. 505's lists and are deliberately not repeated here.
WHAT CONSUMES IT: estimatedPayments:/grossFarmingFishingIncomeCurrentYear, whose two-thirds test reads it. NOTHING MAY ADD IT TO AN INCOME TOTAL — every dollar in it is already inside /totalIncome through wages, interest or business income, and this is a classification of that money, not more of it. interpretation:provisional.

Fact.Name: Net operating loss deduction from an earlier year (Schedule 1 line 8a)
Fact.Description:
OPTIONAL: the deduction for a net operating loss from an earlier year, which the filer computes on Form 172 and enters on Schedule 1 line 8a. SUPERSEDED FOR A POSITIVE AMOUNT: the carry-in inventory (form172 /form172NolCarryIns: the year each loss began and the amount still available, plus the taxable-income base when a post-2017 loss is present) is how an NOL deduction reaches line 8a, because the IRC 172(a)(2) 80 percent limit needs the loss vintage and that base. A positive answer here with no inventory item leaves Schedule 1 line 8a Incomplete until the inventory is answered; the application should ask the inventory instead of this question. An answered $0 still means no deduction. ANSWERED AS A POSITIVE AMOUNT — the negation the printed line requires happens once, downstream, on /schedule1Line8aNetOperatingLossDeduction. Answering this negative and letting that fact negate it again would ADD the loss to income.
THE CARRYFORWARD QUESTION, RECORDED RATHER THAN MODELLED. An NOL is cross-year by nature, so the naming convention had to be chosen deliberately: this path is NOT given a `previousYear…`/`…FromPreviousYear` shape, and the reason is that the figure entered on line 8a is a CURRENT-YEAR quantity, not a prior-year balance. The instruction says "Enter any deduction for an NOL from an earlier year" — the loss originated earlier, but the DEDUCTION is the amount Form 172 allows for this year out of a pool that may span several earlier years and that any allowable-amount limitation reduces. NOT MODELLED, and named so a successor unit can find the gap: the NOL carryforward pool itself, its pre-2018/post-2017 vintage split, and the section 172(a)(2) 80%-of-taxable-income limitation on the deductible amount that the vintage split feeds — Form 172 Part I and Part II themselves are now built (dictionary/ty2025/form172.xml), the amount this year's loss (net of any Part II carryback used and any section 461(l) excess business loss folded in) carries to NEXT year. What is still missing is the CONSUME side: a successor year's line 8a reading that emitted figure instead of taking it as a bare attestation, the vintage split, and the 80%-of-taxable-income cap. A filer whose Form 172 result is wrong gets a wrong line 8a here; this dictionary neither derives nor checks it.
The `Limit type="Min"` of 0 below is a VALIDATION bound (it is what the validator and limit_test read), not a resolution-time floor: whatever is answered resolves at face value. It is here because a negative answer would be a sign error rather than a representable NOL deduction, and it matches the three sibling line-8 writables above.

Fact.Name: PDF should include Form 172
Fact.Description:
Whether the tax return PDF should include Form 172, Net Operating Losses (NOLs). True in any of three cases. (1) A USE year on the older intake: /writableNetOperatingLossDeduction answered and greater than $0, meaning the filer is deducting a prior year's NOL on Schedule 1 line 8a. (1b) A USE year on the carry-in inventory: form172 /form172AllowedNolDeduction resolved and greater than $0, the deduction line 8a takes from the inventory. (2) A LOSS year: Form 172 Part I fully resolved and /form172Line24NetOperatingLoss less than $0, meaning this year's own computation produced a fresh NOL, even though there is nothing to deduct yet.
THE USE-YEAR ATTACHMENT IS PRINTED. The Form 172 instructions say, of a carryforward year: "If you carry forward your NOL to a tax year after the NOL year, list your NOL deduction as a negative figure on Schedule 1 (Form 1040) ... Attach a Form 172 for each NOL to your Form 1040 or Form 1041 if it applies." So the attachment is owed in every year the deduction is claimed, not only the year the loss arose.
THE LOSS-YEAR ARM HAS NO COMPARABLE PRINTED SENTENCE: every "attach" instruction in the vendored i172 is use-year, addressed to Form 1045 or Form 1040-X, forms this product does not file. Attaching Form 172 whenever this year's own Part I computation shows a loss is this dictionary's completeness choice, so a filer or preparer can see the loss that was just computed, and not a departure from a printed instruction.
WHY EACH ARM IS GATED THE WAY IT IS: the use-year arm gates on greater-than-zero because the instruction attaches "for each NOL" and an answered $0 is a filer stating they have none. The loss-year arm gates on IsComplete(line 24) before the sign comparison, because line 24 rests on bare Part I writables that carry no complete-safe wrapper, and a bare LessThan over an incomplete line 24 would make this fact Incomplete on every return that has not finished Part I. Each arm's own IsComplete guard comes first and the comparison sits inside it, so an unanswered arm resolves FALSE rather than making the whole fact Incomplete — the completeness-contagion trap this module has been bitten by more than once.
SCOPE: this says the form belongs in the PDF. It does NOT compute the deduction Schedule 1 line 8a takes in a use year — that quantity is still attested at /writableNetOperatingLossDeduction, a different, unrelated year's figure from this year's own Part I computation.
EXPORTED RATHER THAN CONSUMED, and unlike its three siblings it has to be. /pdfIncludeForm8862, /pdfIncludeScheduleEic and /pdfIncludeSchedule8812 are inherited from the frozen ty2024-l0 vendoring, which lint_wiring exempts. Form 172 did not exist for TY2024, so this fact has no L0 twin and carries its own Export. Its consumer is the PDF assembler, which is SERVICE-owned (invariant #7).

Fact.Name: Schedule 1 line 8a - the NOL deduction entered as a NEGATIVE number (it SUBTRACTS from other income)
Fact.Description:
THIS FACT IS NEGATIVE WHENEVER THE DEDUCTION IS POSITIVE. It is the Schedule 1 line 8a ENTRY, not the deduction amount: = 0 minus /writableNetOperatingLossDeduction when that intake is answered, else $0. Do not sum it anywhere as a deduction figure - it is the negated one, and a reader who treats it as positive inverts AGI. The positive figure is /writableNetOperatingLossDeduction.
THE NEGATION IS THE PRINTED INSTRUCTION, VERBATIM, NOT A MODELLING CHOICE. Schedule 1 line 8a is a preprinted-parentheses field - "a Net operating loss. . . 8a ( )" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f1040s1.pdf, page 1) - and the Form 1040 instructions spell out both halves: "Enter the amount in the preprinted parentheses (as a negative number). The amount of your deduction will be subtracted from the other amounts of income listed on lines 8b through 8z" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040gi.pdf, page 91, a three-column extraction whose left column carries this passage). Schedule 1 line 9 then says "Add lines 8a through 8z" (line 55), so the negated entry is what line 9 adds. Consumer: /schedule1TotalOtherIncome directly below. This is the same shape as line 8d, whose fact form2555:/schedule1Line8dForeignEarnedIncomeExclusion arrives already negated for exactly the same printed reason.
COMPLETE-SAFE: $0 when the intake is unanswered, so an unanswered NOL cannot poison total income and every committed scenario stays byte-identical. The $0 direction OVER-states income and over-taxes, which is the conservative direction.
TWO SOURCES FOR THIS ONE ENTRY, AND WHICH ONE WINS. form172:/form172NolCarryIns is a newer, itemized carry-in inventory that REPLACES this fact's direct /writableNetOperatingLossDeduction intake once it is genuinely built — form172.xml's own Description of /form172AllowedNolDeduction states the wiring rule: the inventory replaces the old intake, and a return that answered the old intake without building the inventory must not be silently read as having no loss. An inventory the filer has ANSWERED but left EMPTY (a real "no carry-in losses" attestation, distinct from never having touched the screen) is not "built" in that sense, so it does not shadow an old intake that carries a figure: the first Switch case requires the inventory to hold at least one item, not merely to be complete. A non-empty inventory still replaces the old intake outright, per the same rule, whatever the old intake carries.
A POSITIVE OLDER FIGURE WITHOUT THE INVENTORY NO LONGER REACHES LINE 8a. IRC 172(a)(2) deducts losses from tax years that began before 2018 in full and later losses only up to 80 percent of the excess of taxable income figured without the NOL, section 199A and section 250 deductions over the earlier losses. The older intake carries neither the vintage nor that base, so the limit cannot be applied to it, and taking it at face value let a post-2017 loss through uncapped. So with no inventory item, an older figure above $0 leaves this fact Incomplete until the filer answers the carry-in inventory (the loss year and the amount of each loss, and the taxable-income base when a post-2017 loss is present). An answered $0 and an unanswered older intake both still give $0.
DISCLOSED CONSEQUENCE 1 - THIS ADDEND MAKES A HAZARD REACHABLE THAT WAS PREVIOUSLY UNREACHABLE, and the note on /schedule1TotalOtherIncome below has been corrected to say so. /hasOtherIncome tests the line-9 chain with GreaterThan 0, so a return whose only Schedule 1 Part I entry is an 8a NOL deduction has /otherIncome NEGATIVE, /hasOtherIncome false, and /requiresSchedule1 not true - while Schedule 1 genuinely carries an entry. The TAX MATH is unaffected (the deduction reaches /totalIncome and AGI correctly); what is wrong is the schedule-required flag. Unlike the line 8d arm, nothing refuses this population: there is no NOL knockout. NOT FIXED HERE ON PURPOSE: the narrowing this needs is assigned by the note below to the unit that retires form2555:/knockoutFilesForm2555, and a NotEqual-0 test would not even be a complete fix (a return with +5,000 of gambling and a 5,000 NOL totals zero on line 9 and still reads as no-Schedule-1).
DISCLOSED CONSEQUENCE 2 - THE AMT SIDE IS NOT BUILT AND THE GAP IS NOW ARMED. Form 6251 line 2e is "Net operating loss deduction from Schedule 1 (Form 1040), line 8a. Enter as a positive amount" - the AMT computation ADDS this deduction back before subtracting its own line 2f ATNOLD. Neither 2e nor 2f exists. So for a filer who answers this intake, AMTI is understated by the deduction until Form 6251 line 2e lands. That was inert while no NOL could be entered at all; it is live now.
TYPE/SIGN/ROUNDING: Dollar, integer cents, SIGNED and normally NEGATIVE. No rounding is added here - the intake is a whole-dollar entry and negation is exact. California TY2025 reads this fact through its stateSystems export (Schedule CA (540), Schedule CA (540NR)).

Fact.Name: Unemployment-adjacent line 8z income kinds
Fact.Description: Income categories supported by this Schedule 1 line 8z calculation.

Fact.Name: Unemployment-adjacent Schedule 1 line 8z entries
Fact.Description: Per-payment records for private unemployment funds, unemployment-like payments to state employees outside the state unemployment compensation law, and union unemployment funds. These payments are reported on Schedule 1 line 8z under the distinct rules shown by the selected payment type.

Fact.Name: Filer who received this unemployment-adjacent payment
Fact.Description: SCREEN. Whose income is this? The default is the primary filer; choose the secondary filer when that filer received the payment. This records attribution for later community-property routing.

Fact.Name: Unemployment-adjacent payment type
Fact.Description: SCREEN. Which kind of unemployment-adjacent payment did you receive? Choose a private nonunion fund, a state employee payment outside the state unemployment law, union regular-dues benefits, or a special union fund whose contributions were deductible or nondeductible.

Fact.Name: Unemployment-adjacent payment amount
Fact.Description: SCREEN. Enter the total payment received from this private fund, state program, or union fund.

Fact.Name: Unemployment-fund contributions
Fact.Description: SCREEN. For a private fund or a special union fund with nondeductible contributions, enter the total amount you paid into that fund. Enter $0 if you made no contributions. This is not asked for payment types whose full amount is included.

Fact.Name: Taxable unemployment-adjacent payment
Fact.Description: The taxable amount reported with the unemployment-adjacent line 8z total. Private-fund and nondeductible special-union-fund payments are reduced by contributions, with a zero floor. Noncovered state-employee payments, regular-dues benefits, and deductible special-union-fund benefits are fully included.

Fact.Name: Unemployment-adjacent payment record is complete
Fact.Description: A payment type and amount are required. Contributions are also required for a private unemployment fund or a special union fund with nondeductible contributions.

Fact.Name: At least one unemployment-adjacent payment record is incomplete
Fact.Description: True when a listed payment is missing a required classification, amount, or contribution figure. An unanswered collection is complete-safe false.

Fact.Name: Taxable unemployment-adjacent income for Schedule 1 line 8z
Fact.Description: The sum of the taxable per-payment amounts above. An unanswered collection contributes complete-safe zero; an incomplete listed payment remains Incomplete.

Fact.Name: Schedule 1 line 8z entries
Fact.Description: Per-entry write-ins for Schedule 1 line 8z, "Other income. List type and amount:" — the generic route for taxable income this return has no more specific line for. Each entry is a type string plus a dollar amount; the application's screen for adding one is the "List type and amount" pair the form itself prints.

Fact.Name: Filer this entry belongs to
Fact.Description: SCREEN. Question: "Whose income is this?" (asked only when the return has two filers — MFJ or a return with a spouse in scope). Help text: this write-in's income is attributed to one filer, the same way a Form 1099-MISC or other document is attributed to the filer who received it — for a community-property MFJ return this attribution is the input a Form 8958 allocation would need. Asked when: adding an entry to the Schedule 1 line 8z list on a two-filer return. Unanswered posture: defaults to the primary filer, complete-safe (single-filer returns never ask this; a two-filer return with no answer still resolves rather than going Incomplete, matching the sibling form1099Misc:/form1099Miscs/*/filer shape). Validation: one of the return's filers. What the answer feeds: nothing computes from it yet; it is recorded now so a later community- property build has an attribution to key off, the way the module's own review found missing.

Fact.Name: (Writable) What type of income is this?
Fact.Description: SCREEN. Question: "What type of income is this?" Help text: A short description of the payment, matching what Schedule 1 line 8z asks you to print — for example "Substitute payments in lieu of dividends," "RTAA payments," or "Taxable grant." Do not list RTAA payments that a Form 1099-G you entered reports in box 5: that document already puts them on line 8z. Asked when: adding an entry to the Schedule 1 line 8z list. Unanswered posture: REFUSED — an amount with no type is not a complete entry (/hasIncompleteSchedule1Line8zEntries blocks submission). Validation: String, 1-100 characters, no default. What the answer feeds: printed on Schedule 1 line 8z beside this entry's amount (pdf binding drafted, not built — see the module comment above); the type is disclosure only and nothing computes from its text.

Fact.Name: (Writable) Amount
Fact.Description: SCREEN. Question: "How much was this payment?" Help text: enter the taxable amount of this Schedule 1 line 8z item, in whole dollars and cents. Asked when: adding an entry to the Schedule 1 line 8z list. Unanswered posture: REFUSED — a type with no amount is not a complete entry. Validation: Dollar, Min $0, no Max. What the answer feeds: /schedule1Line8zEntriesTotal, an addend of /schedule1TotalOtherIncome (Schedule 1 line 9) and (drafted, not built here) the printed Schedule 1 line 8z amount box beside hsa:/schedule1Line8zOtherIncome's four existing legs.

Fact.Name: Entry is complete
Fact.Description: Whether this Schedule 1 line 8z entry is complete: both the type and the amount answered.

Fact.Name: At least one Schedule 1 line 8z entry is incomplete
Fact.Description: Whether at least one Schedule 1 line 8z entry is incomplete (a type with no amount, or an amount with no type). Follows the sibling document-intake modules' Count(Not(isComplete)) > 0 shape (formW2s, unemployment, socialSecurity, interest, form1099Misc).

Fact.Name: Schedule 1 line 8z entries total
Fact.Description: Total of every complete Schedule 1 line 8z entry's amount — an addend of /schedule1TotalOtherIncome (Schedule 1 line 9), and an addend of hsa:/schedule1Line8zOtherIncome, the printed 8z amount box, so the box foots with this total. Complete-safe $0: the Switch's first arm needs /schedule1Line8zEntries Complete; the default arm is a hard $0, so a return with no entries contributes zero without reading a money box. The total also includes /unemploymentAdjacentOtherIncomeTotal for private-fund, noncovered state-employee, and union unemployment benefits.

Fact.Name: Schedule 1 line 8z, the Form 1099-G box 6 personal taxable grants
Fact.Description: The total of the box 6 taxable grants on the filer's Forms 1099-G (unemployment:/form1099Gs) that the filer says are not trade or business income, rounded once. Line 8z takes taxable income not reported elsewhere; a grant received in a trade or business is instead included in that business's other income on Schedule C or Schedule F, so it is not counted here. An addend of /schedule1TotalOtherIncome (line 9) and of hsa:/schedule1Line8zOtherIncome (the printed 8z amount box). $0 when no Form 1099-G is listed or none carries box 6; Incomplete while a document's box 6 amount waits for its business question.

Fact.Name: Schedule 1 line 8z, the Form 1099-G box 5 RTAA payments
Fact.Description: The total of box 5 (reemployment trade adjustment assistance payments) over every Form 1099-G in unemployment:/form1099Gs, cents kept per document and rounded once. The recipient instruction for box 5 sends the amount to the Other income line of Schedule 1, which for 2025 is line 8z, and Pub. 525 lists RTAA payments among the income reported there. An addend of /schedule1TotalOtherIncome (line 9) and of hsa:/schedule1Line8zOtherIncome (the printed 8z amount box), so the two foot. A document whose box 5 is unanswered contributes $0, and a negative entry, which the box's Min limit does not stop on resolution, is floored at $0. Complete-safe $0 when the Form 1099-G collection is unanswered or empty. An RTAA amount already carried by a Form 1099-G entered here is not also typed on the /schedule1Line8zEntries list; that list is for RTAA payments no entered Form 1099-G reports.

Fact.Name: Form 4797 line 35 recapture reported on Schedule 1 line 8z
Fact.Description: SCREEN SPEC. QUESTION: "How much of your Form 4797 line 35 recapture is not reported on a Schedule C or Schedule F?" HELP TEXT: "Report the recapture amount as other income on the same form or schedule on which you took the deduction. If you took the depreciation deduction on Form 2106, it goes on Schedule 1, line 8z. If the property was used both in your trade or business and to produce income, the part for producing income goes here and the business part on your Schedule C or F. A deduction taken on Schedule E or Form 4835 does not go here. Increase your basis in the property by the recapture amount." (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/p946.pdf, page 57, left column; https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i4797.pdf, page 12, right column). ASKED WHEN: form4797:/partIVLine35RecaptureToRoute is above zero. UNANSWERED: $0; when the amounts entered on every schedule do not add up to line 35, the return does not complete (form4797:/hasUnallocatedPartIVLine35Recapture). VALIDATION: Dollar, Min 0. WHAT IT FEEDS: /schedule1Line8zForm4797Line35RecaptureAllocated, hence /schedule1Line8zForm4797Line35RecaptureLeg and /schedule1TotalOtherIncome (line 9), and the Form 4797 allocation check. Not self-employment income.

Fact.Name: Form 4797 line 35 recapture allocated to Schedule 1 line 8z (complete safe)
Fact.Description: /writableSchedule1Line8zForm4797Line35RecaptureAmount when answered, else $0. The Schedule 1 term of form4797:/partIVLine35RecaptureAllocatedTotal, and what /schedule1Line8zForm4797Line35RecaptureLeg carries to line 8z, so the check and the line read one quantity.

Fact.Name: Form 4797 line 35 recapture carried to Schedule 1 line 8z
Fact.Description: /schedule1Line8zForm4797Line35RecaptureAllocated when form4797:/partIVLine35RecaptureIsAllocated is TRUE; NO default arm. Because /schedule1TotalOtherIncome is on every return's path to /totalIncome, this leg is where an unallocated line 35 recapture stops the return, whatever schedule the filer has: a return whose recapture has no destination (a Schedule E or Form 4835 deduction, or an allocation that does not add up) is Incomplete here and legible through form4797:/hasUnallocatedPartIVLine35Recapture. $0 on every return with no Part IV amount.

Fact.Name: Section 465(e) at-risk recapture income carried to Schedule 1 line 8z
Fact.Description:
The amount IRC 465(e)(1)(A) puts into gross income when the amount a filer has at risk in an activity ends the tax year below zero, summed over every Form 6198 activity on the return. form6198 already computed the per-activity figure and Exported it; before this fact existed, nothing in the dictionary read /form6198Activities at all, so a return with a below-zero amount at risk filed WITHOUT the recapture and nothing said so. The direction of that omission is a silent under-charge.
WHY LINE 8z RATHER THAN THE ACTIVITY OWN SCHEDULE, stated as the interpretation it is. No printed IRS line carries this amount. IRC 465(e)(1)(A) says the taxpayer includes it in gross income AS INCOME FROM SUCH ACTIVITY; Publication 925 says the same in the imperative, by adding it to the income from the activity for that year; the Form 6198 instructions only warn that a filer may HAVE recapture income and point at Publication 925. None of the three names a Form 1040 or Schedule 1 line. In this dictionary a Form 6198 activity carries no link to the schedule its income is reported on - the module has no cross-module dependency of any kind - so the recaptured amount is, in the words of the printed Schedule 1 instruction, taxable income not reported elsewhere, and line 8z is the residual line that sentence describes. THE REJECTED ALTERNATIVE is to route each activity amount to the Schedule C, E, F or Form 4835 it belongs to; that is the more faithful reading of the statutory phrase and it is not buildable here, because the activity-to-schedule identity does not exist in this dictionary. This placement is DECLARED, provisional.
PUBLICATION 925 SUPPORTS KEEPING IT OUT OF THE ACTIVITY NETTING: it says not to use the recapture income to reduce any net loss from the activity for the tax year, and to treat the recaptured amount as a deduction for the activity in the NEXT year - which is the separate fact form6198:/form6198Activities/*/activityDeductionAllocableToNextYear, not this one.
EVERY ACTIVITY, NOT ONLY THE ONES THAT FILE THE FORM. The Form 6198 instructions for line 3 carry the caution that a current-year PROFIT on line 5 does not rule out recapture income, so this sums /form6198Activities/*/section465eRecaptureIncome over the WHOLE collection rather than over /form6198ActivitiesToPrint. Case form6198/s478-at-risk-recapture-profitable-activity-also-recaptures is that return.
COMPLETE-SAFE FIRST, BY CONSTRUCTION. The first case answers a hard $0 whenever the activity collection is not Complete, which is every return that lists no at-risk activity, so a bare CollectionSum over an unanswered collection can never make this Incomplete and Schedule 1 line 9, total income and AGI are byte-identical on every such return. Case income/s478-form6198-activities-absent-line-8z-complete-zero pins the key-ABSENT arm. A LISTED activity whose statutory cap is unanswered leaves the per-activity figure Incomplete and this total with it, which is the deliberate refusal this fact makes instead of the silent under-charge; case form6198/s478-at-risk-recapture-cap-unanswered-blocks-line-8z measures it down to /totalIncome.
ON THE PRINTED 8z AMOUNT BOX. The Schedule 1 line 8z field binds hsa:/schedule1Line8zOtherIncome, which adds this leg (as it adds /schedule1Line8zForm4797Line35RecaptureLeg and /schedule1Line8zEntriesTotal), so the printed write-in and line 9 foot.

Fact.Name: Knockout: section 465(e) at-risk recapture income on the return
Fact.Description: SCREEN. Your amount at risk in an activity fell below zero this year, so part of your earlier losses from it must be added back to income. That recaptured income is income FROM THE ACTIVITY, and whether it is self-employment income, passive income or qualified business income depends on the schedule the activity is reported on, which this return cannot yet link to your Form 6198. This return cannot be filed here. True when /schedule1Line8zAtRiskRecaptureIncome is Complete and above $0; Complete false otherwise, including while a listed activity is still unanswered. DUAL-WIRED: BlockSubmissionOnTrue plus membership in flow:/flowIsKnockedOut.

Fact.Name: Schedule B line 5, the "Form 8814" row label
Fact.Description: The payer-name cell of the last printed Schedule B line 5 row: "Form 8814" when an attached Form 8814 carries line 9 qualified dividends above $0 and fewer than fifteen Form 1099-DIV payers fill the rows above it; not Complete otherwise, so the cell prints the fifteenth payer or stays blank. Printed only; the amount is already in /ordinaryDividends (line 6).

Fact.Name: Schedule B line 5, the "Form 8814" row amount
Fact.Description: The amount cell beside /scheduleBLine5Form8814RowLabel: the Form 8814 line 9 total in whole dollars, on the same population; not Complete otherwise, so the cell prints the fifteenth payer's amount or stays blank. Printed only.

Fact.Name: Form 1099-PATR box 1 patronage dividends that are not taxable
Fact.Description: SCREEN. QUESTION TEXT: "How much of the patronage dividends in box 1 of your Forms 1099-PATR was paid on property you bought for personal use, or on capital assets or depreciable property used in your business?" HELP TEXT: those dividends are not taxable (Form 1099-PATR box 1 instruction); for business capital assets or depreciable property, reduce the asset's basis by this amount. ASKED WHEN: the return records a Form 1099-PATR and does not claim Schedule F. UNANSWERED: $0, so the whole box 1 amount is treated as taxable (the conservative direction). VALIDATION: dollars, not less than $0, and not more than the box 1 total (a larger answer takes off nothing beyond the Form 1099-PATR total). FEEDS: /form1099PatrNontaxablePatronageDividendsOrZero and through it /schedule1Line8zCooperativeDistributionsWithoutScheduleF.

Fact.Name: Form 1099-PATR nontaxable patronage dividends, $0 when unanswered
Fact.Description: /writableForm1099PatrNontaxablePatronageDividends floored at $0, or $0 when unanswered. Subtracted in /schedule1Line8zCooperativeDistributionsWithoutScheduleF.

Fact.Name: Form 1099-PATR distributions carried to Schedule 1 line 8z on a return without Schedule F
Fact.Description: The Form 1099-PATR boxes 1, 2, 3 and 5 total (scheduleF:/form1099PatrsCooperativeDistributions) on a return that does not claim Schedule F farm income (scheduleF:/claimsScheduleFFarmIncome false), and $0 on a return that does. The Form 1099-PATR recipient instructions tell an individual to report those boxes as ordinary income unless nontaxable; on a farm return they are Schedule F lines 3a and 3b, and on any other return no printed line names them, so they are taxable income not reported elsewhere, which is Schedule 1 line 8z. The box 4 backup withholding reaches Form 1040 line 25b, and this leg carries the income beside it. Complete $0 on every return that records no Form 1099-PATR. Less the part reported on Schedule C line 6 (scheduleC:/scheduleCForm1099PatrDistributionsTotal, amounts received in a nonfarm business) and the box 1 patronage dividends on personal-use purchases or on capital or depreciable business assets, which are not taxable (/form1099PatrNontaxablePatronageDividendsOrZero), floored at $0. ON THE PRINTED 8z AMOUNT BOX: the Schedule 1 line 8z field binds hsa:/schedule1Line8zOtherIncome, which adds this leg, so the printed write-in and line 9 foot.

Fact.Name: Recovery of an earlier year's casualty or theft loss deduction carried to Schedule 1 line 8z
Fact.Description:
The part of this year's casualty or theft reimbursements that recovers a loss deducted on an earlier year's return and reduced tax there, included in income as other income on Schedule 1 line 8z. It is form4684:/priorYearCasualtyDeductionRecoveryIncome, which is $0 on every return with no casualty events and on every event whose recovery cannot be measured (that return is refused on Form 4684 instead). Positive, integer cents.
ON THE PRINTED 8z AMOUNT BOX. The Schedule 1 line 8z field binds hsa:/schedule1Line8zOtherIncome, and that fact adds this leg, so the printed write-in and line 9 foot by construction (the same arrangement as /schedule1Line8zForm4797Line35RecaptureLeg).

Fact.Name: Total other income
Fact.Description:
Total other income reported on line 9 of the 1040 Schedule 1 (the total of lines 8a through 8z). Alaska PFD (line 8g, inherited) + taxable HSA distributions — TWO legs, the top-level scalar route and the /hsaDistributions collection route, which ADD rather than select (see the comment on the second dependency below) + W-2G gambling winnings + non-W-2G gambling (8b), jury duty pay (8h) and prizes/awards (8i) + the Form 2555 foreign earned income exclusion (line 8d; complete-safe 0) + wages earned while incarcerated (line 8u; complete-safe 0, and $0 on every return that does not answer the /writableIncarceratedWagesOutsideReportedIncome router TRUE) + the Form 4797 line 35 recapture allocated to line 8z (/schedule1Line8zForm4797Line35RecaptureLeg; $0 on every return with no Part IV amount, Incomplete when line 35 is not fully allocated).
TWO ADDENDS CAN BE NEGATIVE, and they are the reason this sum can be negative too. Schedule 1 prints lines 8a and 8d in parentheses. For 8d the instructions say to enter the Form 2555 line-45 amount "as a negative number", because it "will be subtracted from the other amounts of income listed on lines 8a through 8c and lines 8e through 8z"; for 8a they say the same of the NOL deduction, which "will be subtracted from the other amounts of income listed on lines 8b through 8z". So both form2555:/schedule1Line8dForeignEarnedIncomeExclusion and /schedule1Line8aNetOperatingLossDeduction arrive already negated and this Add is still literally "Add lines 8a through 8z". A reader who negates either again double-counts it in the wrong direction.
KNOWN CONSEQUENCE, DISCLOSED RATHER THAN FIXED HERE. /hasOtherIncome below tests this chain with GreaterThan 0, so a return whose only Schedule 1 Part I entry is a parenthesised negative has /otherIncome negative, /hasOtherIncome false, and does not reach /requiresSchedule1 true while Schedule 1 genuinely carries an entry. THIS IS REACHABLE ONLY BECAUSE THE LINE 8a ADDEND EXISTS: the 8d arm is inert because form2555:/knockoutFilesForm2555 refuses every return whose Form 2555 gate is true and the line 8d leg is $0 on every other return, but the 8a arm has no knockout and its intake is answerable on any return. The tax math is unaffected; the schedule-required flag is the wrong part. Narrowing /hasOtherIncome still belongs to the unit that retires that knockout, and that unit should note a NotEqual-0 test is not a complete fix either: a return with +5,000 of gambling and a 5,000 NOL totals zero on line 9 and still reads as no-Schedule-1. Schedule 1 line 8s is parenthesised the same way and is a third signed addend of this sum through /schedule1Line8sNontaxableMedicaidWaiverBackOutOrZero, so it widens the same reachable case rather than being the exception the sentence above used to name.
THIRTEEN PRINTED BOXES ARE IN THE ADD: 8c, 8j, 8k, 8l, 8m, 8n, 8o, 8p, 8q, 8r, 8s, 8t and 8v, each through its own complete safe OrZero wrapper, plus a THIRD line 8e leg, hsa:/form8853Line26TaxableLtcPayments (Form 8853 Section C, taxable long term care payments). Before that edit each of those boxes had a shipping intake that printed on the schedule and footed nowhere. Every new leg is $0 on every committed scenario, so this sum did not move.
/schedule1Line8zEntriesTotal sits beside form1099Misc:/form1099MiscOtherIncome as a second line 8z leg: a generic per-entry type+amount write-in for taxable income with no other route, discharging four otherwise-omitted findings (Form 1099-MISC box 8 substitute payments, Form 1099-G box 5 RTAA payments, Form 1099-G box 6 taxable grants, and the Form 6251 line 2b "or line 8z" recovery leg). $0 and byte-identical on every committed scenario, because the collection is new and none of them carries an entry.
Plus, since the OUT-forms integration, the Form 8621 ordinary-income legs — QEF inclusions, section 1296 ordinary gains and losses and the section 1291 current-year and pre-PFIC allocations — through form8621:/form8621OrdinaryIncome, an outer addend beside the rounded lines 8a–8z sum; $0 on every return with no Form 8621.

Fact.Name: Schedule 1 lines 1, 7 and 9 subtotal (a PART of Schedule 1 line 10)
Fact.Description:
The Schedule 1 Part I subtotal of line 1 taxable state and local income tax recoveries, line 7 unemployment compensation and line 9 other income (the 8a through 8z roll up).
THIS IS NOT SCHEDULE 1 LINE 10 AND IT IS NOT FORM 1040 LINE 8. Schedule 1 line 10 is "Combine lines 1 through 7 and 9", which also picks up line 2a alimony received, line 3 business income, line 4 other gains, line 5 rental and royalty and K-1 income and line 6 farm income. Those five legs are DIRECT addends of /totalIncome rather than terms of this fact, so this fact is a proper part of the printed line. The whole printed line is /schedule1Line10AdditionalIncome below, which adds this subtotal and the same five legs.
WHY THIS FACT WAS NOT SIMPLY GROWN INTO THE WHOLE LINE. Four facts read it as this partial and would double count the five legs the moment it absorbed them, because each of the four already reads those legs directly beside it: /totalIncome (Form 1040 line 9), /totalIncomeUpperBoundForIraMagi (the section 219(g) bound below), socialSecurity:/socialSecurityBenefitsWkshtLine3 (the Form 1040 line 8 proxy in the section 86 provisional income base) and scheduleE:/section8582Magi (the Form 8582 line 6 MAGI). The bound is the one that cannot be repaired by editing all four: it must never read scheduleE:/scheduleETotalIncome at all (scripts/lint_ira_magi_bound.py check 1, and the classification in scripts/ira_magi_bound_addends.tsv records why), so a line 10 complete version of this fact could not be an addend of the bound at all. OPERATOR RULING: the Export STAYS - downstream/state consumers may read this path, and renaming or dropping an exported path is a breaking change owned by the application/states campaign, not this one.

Fact.Name: Schedule 1 line 10 additional income (Form 1040 line 8)
Fact.Description:
Schedule 1 line 10, "Combine lines 1 through 7 and 9", which Form 1040 line 8 carries onto page 1 of the return.
WHY THIS FACT EXISTS SEPARATELY FROM /otherIncome: /otherIncome sums only Schedule 1 lines 1, 7 and 9, while the other five Part I legs (line 2a alimony received, line 3 business income, line 4 other gains, line 5 rental and royalty and K-1 income, line 6 farm income) reach Form 1040 line 9 as DIRECT addends of /totalIncome instead of through /otherIncome. A fact that read only /otherIncome for both Schedule 1 line 10 and Form 1040 line 8 would compute the right tax but print wrong: a return with a Schedule C profit would print that profit on Schedule 1 line 3 while Schedule 1's own line 10 total omitted it, and Form 1040 line 8 would be smaller than its own line 9 arithmetic implies.
WHAT THIS FACT IS. The whole printed line: the /otherIncome subtotal plus the same five legs, in the SAME identities /totalIncome reads, so Form 1040 foots BY CONSTRUCTION - line 9 is "Add lines 1z, 2b, 3b, 4b, 5b, 6b, 7a, and 8" and this fact is exactly /totalIncome minus those seven other addends.
NOTHING IN THE GRAPH READS THIS FACT AND NOTHING SHOULD. It is a print only total; its consumer is the printed form register, once the two register cells are re-pointed (dictionary/pdf/2025/IRS1040S1/en/configuration.yml field f1_38, Schedule 1 line 10, and dictionary/pdf/2025/IRS1040/en/configuration.yml field f1_72, Form 1040 line 8, both of which name /otherIncome today). It carries an Export for that reason. THIS IS WHY THERE IS NO DOUBLE COUNT: the coordinated pair the carry map asked for - the printed total gains the legs AND the return level total drops them - would be needed only if /totalIncome read this fact, and it does not. /totalIncome, /totalIncomeUpperBoundForIraMagi, socialSecurity:/socialSecurityBenefitsWkshtLine3 and scheduleE:/section8582Magi all keep reading /otherIncome plus their own direct legs, unchanged, so every committed scenario and every committed node fixture is byte identical.
THE SCHEDULE C LEG IS THE NONEXCLUDED FIGURE, scheduleC:/scheduleCNetProfitSubjectToUsTax, and not scheduleC:/scheduleCNetProfit. The two diverge only for a bona fide resident of Puerto Rico or a section 931 possession, and /totalIncome's own Description records the modelling decision that Schedule 1 line 3 carries the reduced figure while Schedule C line 31 keeps the combined one (section 933(1) takes the excluded income out of gross income, so it cannot be inside Form 1040 line 9). Choosing the combined figure here would print a Schedule 1 line 10 that no longer equals the line 8 that Form 1040 line 9 was built from, which is the very defect this fact exists to close. The printed line 3 register cell (IRS1040S1 field f1_07) still names the combined figure and must move with this fact for Schedule 1 to foot down its own column; that re-point is reported to the lead.
ROUNDED ONCE, like every printed dollar line on the schedule. /totalIncome rounds its own thirteen addend sum once, so on a return whose legs carry cents this printed line and the line 8 implied by Form 1040's own subtraction can differ by at most the rounding of the legs, which is the ordinary printed form residual and not a modelling difference.

Fact.Name: Total income
Fact.Description:
Total income to report on line 9 of Form 1040.
⚠ THE SCHEDULE 1 LINE-3 ADDEND IS THE NONEXCLUDED SCHEDULE C NET PROFIT. It reads scheduleC:/scheduleCNetProfitSubjectToUsTax — the combined line 31 LESS the section 931/933 excluded part — rather than scheduleC:/scheduleCNetProfit itself. Publication 1321 states the direction in its opening instruction: "The income you receive from Puerto Rico sources (except income received as a civilian or military employee of the U.S. government) is not subject to U.S. income tax" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/p1321.pdf, page 1 — the sentence opens with "The income" at the end of line 27), and section 933(1) is the statute behind it — that income "shall not be included in gross income and shall be exempt from taxation under this subtitle". WHY THIS ADDEND MOVES HERE AND NOT WITH THE SE-TAX/QBI APPORTIONMENT. That apportionment moved the half of self-employment tax deducted on Schedule 1 line 15 and both QBI derivations onto the nonexcluded basis while THIS line still carried the combined figure, so a filer who named an exclusion was taxed on it AND lost the deductions allocable to it — compounding taxpayer-adverse, on a population that COMPUTES (the narrowed ctcOdc:/knockoutPossessionOrPuertoRicoIncomeExclusion resolves false for a return whose exclusion is fully answered). That defect is what this addend discharges, where line 9 falls from 101,000 to 41,000 on the same fixture that apportionment used. THE OTHER CONSUMERS OF /scheduleCNetProfit MOVE OR STAY ON THEIR OWN AUTHORITY, never by following this one — the per-consumer discipline this repo follows, and the full table is on scheduleC:/scheduleCNetProfitSubjectToUsTax. The three that moved with this fact are /totalIncomeUpperBoundForIraMagi (the dominance bound below, which must mirror this addend set or stop dominating), socialSecurity:/socialSecurityBenefitsWkshtLine3 (the Form 1040 line-8 proxy, whose own section 86(b)(2) add-backs then restore the exclusion exactly once) and scheduleE:/section8582Magi (which follows plain AGI). The two that did NOT are scheduleSE:/selfEmploymentEarnedIncome (section 1402(a)(6) computes net earnings from self-employment "without regard to section 933") and scheduleE:/rentalSection179IncomeLimit (no vendored source answers it either way). WHAT THE PRINTED RETURN NOW SHOWS, stated because nothing adjudicates it: Schedule C line 31 keeps the combined figure (it is the mef export and its own instruction is "Subtract line 30 from line 29", pure arithmetic on that business's receipts and expenses), while Schedule 1 line 3 carries less, with no printed reconciliation line between them. That is a MODELLING DECISION, not a transcription — Publication 1321's model is that a bona fide resident does not file a Schedule C for the excluded business at all, so the IRS never has to reconcile the two. Collecting the exclusion per item is this dictionary's shape. The residual is a DISCLOSURE gap on the printed form, with no tax effect; the full statement is on scheduleC:/scheduleCNetProfit.
⚠ THE CREDIT-MAGI INTERLOCK, WHICH IS WHY MOVING THIS LINE IS SAFE FOR CREDITS AND WHY IT FIXES A SECOND DOUBLE COUNT. Publication 1321 carries a caution that reads at first like the opposite of this unit: "Excluded Puerto Rico source income must be included in gross income when calculating income limits for certain credits. It is important to remember that credits which apply to your excluded Puerto Rico income are not allowed on your Federal income tax return" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/p1321.pdf, page 7). IT IS NOT CONTRARY AUTHORITY; IT IS THE ARCHITECTURE. The income comes out HERE, at gross income, and each credit's own MAGI puts it back through add-backs on seven surfaces — so it is included in the income limits exactly where the caution asks and nowhere else. MEASURED, NOT ARGUED, on this unit's witness. ctcOdc:/dependentCreditMagi (section 24(b)(1)) and scheduleA:/saltMagi both fall from 158,174 to 98,174 — which is AGI 38,174 PLUS the 60,000 exclusion, i.e. counted ONCE. They fell because while this line carried the COMBINED line 31 they counted it TWICE: once through AGI and once through their own add-back. That over-stated every one of those MAGIs, made their phaseouts too large and their credits too SMALL — taxpayer-ADVERSE — and this unit corrects it across all seven surfaces at once. The same correction on socialSecurity:/socialSecurityBenefitsWkshtLine3 and taxCalculations:/magiForIraDeduction is written up on those facts. ⚠⚠ AND IT CREATES ONE RESIDUAL, IN THE OTHER DIRECTION, ON THE SURFACE THAT HAS NO ADD-BACK. elderlyAndDisabled:/edcMagi is Schedule R line 16 — PLAIN AGI less the exemption-table amount — so it falls from 88,174 to 28,174 and the section 22 credit gets LARGER. TAXPAYER-FAVOURABLE, which is this repo's worst class, and it is stated here as well as on that fact because this line is what moved. It is NOT patched, and the reason is invariant #3 rather than doubt: section 22 is not vendored, Schedule R prints no add-back line, and this repo's discipline is that each MAGI surface is wired against ITS OWN statute rather than against a generic caution. form8960:/niitMagi falls the same way and is CORRECT there — section 1411(d) names section 911 alone, and the NIIT is a tax rather than a credit income limit, so the caution does not reach it. Both are pinned by the witness so neither can move unnoticed. California TY2025 reads this fact through its stateSystems export (Schedule CA (540), Schedule CA (540NR)).

Fact.Name: Form 1040 line 9 DISREGARDING SECTION 137 (i8839 line 25 worksheet, lines 1 + 2 + 3)
Fact.Description:
/totalIncome's thirteen addends with ONE substitution and ONE addition: /employerIncomeSubtotal is replaced by /employerIncomeSubtotalDisregardingSection137 (line 1z without the two Form 1040 line 1f legs), and form8839:/adoptionLine23TotalEmployerBenefits is added in full. Not a printed line; no MeF or PDF export.
THIS IS THE i8839 LINE 25 WORKSHEET, lines 1 through 4, read as facts. Worksheet line 1 is "the amount you would enter on line 1z ... if you could exclude the total amount on Form 8839, line 23"; line 2 is "the amount from Form 8839, line 23"; line 3 is "the total of lines 2b, 3b, 4b, 5b, 6b, and 7a from Form 1040 ... and the amount from Schedule 1 (Form 1040), line 10"; line 4 adds the three. That enumeration is exactly Form 1040 line 9 with 1z swapped and line 23 added, which is why this fact is /totalIncome's addend list rather than a re-derivation of it. The worksheet's line 5 subtraction and its Form 2555 / Form 4563 / Puerto Rico footer live on form8839:/adoptionExclusionMagi, the fact that reads this one.
AND IT IS ALSO THE SECTION 86 AND SECTION 219(g) BASE. Those two MAGIs are defined "without regard to ... section 137", so they want line 1z carrying the FULL benefit rather than the section 137 remainder. Their consumers read /employerIncomeSubtotalDisregardingSection137 directly (socialSecurity:/socialSecurityBenefitsWkshtLine3 and /totalIncomeUpperBoundForIraMagi) because each rebuilds its own total from line-level addends; this fact exists for the one consumer that needs the whole of line 9.
THE THIRTEEN ADDENDS ARE MIRRORED, NOT REFERENCED, and that is a maintenance debt stated rather than hidden: a new /totalIncome addend must be added here too, exactly as it must be mirrored into /totalIncomeUpperBoundForIraMagi. There is no lint pinning this set today; the node fixture income/adoption-line1f-unanswered-complete-safe pins the identity /totalIncomeDisregardingSection137 == /totalIncome + line 23 on a return with no adoption benefits, which catches a dropped addend as a value divergence.
BYTE-IDENTICAL CONSEQUENCE: on every committed return line 23 is $0 and both line 1f legs are $0, so this fact equals /totalIncome.

Fact.Name: Upper bound on Form 1040 line 4b (taxable IRA distributions), route-independent
Fact.Description: An upper bound on /taxableIraDistributions built ONLY from intake writables, so it never reads the Worksheet 1-1 route's output. Dominates every branch of /taxableIraDistributions above: the scalar fully-taxable branch (the writable itself, added exactly — the other terms are non-negative), the Form 8606 partial-taxability branch (form8606:/form8606TaxableAmountUpperBound + form8606:/spouseForm8606TaxableAmountUpperBound dominate lines 15c + 18 term by term), and the complete-safe 0 branch. The scalar and 8606 intakes are mutually exclusive by knockout, so SUMMING them here is merely loose, never unsound. Complete-safe: 0 when no IRA intake is in use.

Fact.Name: Upper bound on Form 1040 line 6b (taxable social security), route-independent
Fact.Description:
An upper bound on /taxableSocialSecurityBenefits that never reads the Worksheet 1-1 route's output. §86(a)(2)(B) caps the includible amount at 85% of the benefits received UNCONDITIONALLY — the Social Security Benefits Worksheet's own line 18 is a LesserOf against exactly this product — so 85% x SSA-1099 box 5 (= /socialSecurityBenefits, Form 1040 line 6a) dominates line 6b without touching the worksheet's MAGI-dependent base-amount arithmetic (which reads /totalIncome and would close the cycle). The GreaterOf-0 mirrors line 6b's own negative-benefits-after-repayment branch (which returns 0, not a negative), and the Round mirrors line 6b's Round so that monotonicity survives rounding: Round is monotone non-decreasing and 0.85 x benefits >= LesserOf(line 16, 0.85 x benefits), so this dominates after rounding too. Complete-safe: 0 when no SSA-1099 is reported.
STILL A BOUND WITH THE PUB. 590-A APPENDIX B ROUTE. Form 1040 line 6b is a two-arm Switch: the ordinary Social Security Benefits Worksheet, and Pub. 590-A Appendix B Worksheet 3 for a filer who meets Appendix B's four conditions. BOTH arms end on a LesserOf against 85% of gross benefits — the ordinary worksheet at its line 18 and Worksheet 3 at its line 19 against line 18 (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/p590a.pdf, page 56) — because both are the same §86(a)(2) lesser-of. So this product dominates either arm and the bound is unchanged in strength. It also does not gain an edge: Worksheet 3 is DOWNSTREAM of the IRA deduction, and this bound reads only /socialSecurityBenefits, so it still touches nothing the Worksheet 1-1 route produces. scripts/lint_ira_magi_bound.py was run by name after the fill and both of its checks still report OK.

Fact.Name: Upper bound on Form 1040 line 9 (total income) for the §219(g) MAGI bound
Fact.Description: /totalIncome's THIRTEEN addends with the three that are downstream of the Worksheet 1-1 route replaced or omitted (see the block comment above). The thirteenth is scheduleF:/scheduleFNetProfitOrLoss (Schedule 1 line 6, farm net profit or loss), classified `clean` — read directly and exactly, because Schedule F reads only its own writables. TWO OPEN OBLIGATIONS, named here rather than left silent: scripts/ira_magi_bound_addends.tsv does not yet carry this addend's classification row, so CHECK 2 of scripts/lint_ira_magi_bound.py (a GATE_FULL step) is RED until the classification row lands; and the tsv's SECOND OBLIGATION — mirroring any new /totalIncome addend into socialSecurity:/socialSecurityBenefitsWkshtLine3, so that /totalIncome == Round(line 3 + line 6b) stays an identity — is also undischarged. Until the mirror lands, a §219(g) MAGI computed for a return with farm income is missing that income stream, which makes the IRA deduction too LARGE and UNDER-taxes; no committed scenario answers a Schedule F intake, so nothing is wrong today. VALID ONLY when scheduleE:/scheduleEActivityPresent is false — that is the one state in which omitting the /scheduleETotalIncome addend is exact rather than an under-estimate, and it is why the only consumer of this fact, iraDeduction:/iraDeductionProvablyNotReducedByIncomeLimits, conjoins the refusal gate with the comparison rather than reading this fact alone. The addend set is pinned mechanically by scripts/lint_ira_magi_bound.py against scripts/ira_magi_bound_addends.tsv. Rounding mirrors /totalIncome's single Round over the sum, so the two are comparable dollar for dollar.

Fact.Name: Earned income including all combat pay
Fact.Description:
Earned income plus all combat pay.
This value is reported on line 18a of schedule 8812, used to calculate ACTC. Includes net self-employment earned income; both EITC and ACTC count self-employment earnings as earned income.
⚠ THE LAST SENTENCE ABOVE IS TOO SIMPLE ON ITS OWN. This fact reads scheduleSE:/selfEmploymentEarnedIncomeSubjectToUsTax, not scheduleSE:/selfEmploymentEarnedIncome. Both credits count self-employment earnings, but they count DIFFERENT amounts for a filer with a section 931 or 933 exclusion, and the difference is statutory on both sides: section 24(d)(1)(B)(i) takes only earned income "which is taken into account in computing taxable income", while section 32(c)(2)(A)(ii) reaches section 1402(a), whose paragraphs (6) and (9) put both exclusions back in. The whole argument, with the printed instruction and worksheet lines, is on the fact this now reads. THIS PATH IS THE SCHEDULE 8812 SIDE OF THAT SPLIT and it keeps the MeF export and the line-18a name, so the transmitted and printed line 18a move with the credit rather than against it. The EITC side is /earnedIncomeWithAllCombatPayIncludingExcludedTerritory below, which is this fact's former body, extracted unchanged. THE COMBAT-PAY ADDEND IS NOT AN EXCEPTION TO THE SAME RULE, it is its proof: section 112 pay is excluded from gross income too, and section 24(d)(1)'s flush sentence has to say so expressly - "any amount excluded from gross income by reason of section 112 shall be treated as earned income which is taken into account in computing taxable income for the taxable year". formW2s:/allCombatPay is that sentence. Sections 931 and 933 have no such sentence. WORLD-1: additive. No committed scenario answers either exclusion entry, so scheduleC:/scheduleCExcludedTerritoryNetProfit is $0 everywhere, scheduleSE:/selfEmploymentTaxDeduction takes its un-apportioned arm, and the two self-employment addends are equal, which pins them and this fact to the same 92,935.
⚠ A FOURTH ADDEND is the STATUTORY EMPLOYEE ADD-BACK, /statutoryEmployeeWagesInEarnedIncome. The dictionary routes a statutory employee's box 1 to the linked Schedule C's line 1, which takes it out of the first addend; this worksheet prints its own line for it, at Earned Income Worksheet line 2a. The line-2b half of the same worksheet ("Do not include on this line any statutory employee income") is landed in the SAME unit on the third addend, scheduleSE:/selfEmploymentEarnedIncomeSubjectToUsTax, which now subtracts scheduleC:/statutoryEmployeeScheduleCNetProfit. Both halves or neither: 2a without 2b counts the statutory business twice, by its line 1 AND its line 31, in the taxpayer favourable direction. THE FOOT, which is the test of the whole arrangement: this fact is worksheet lines 1a + 1b + 2a + 2b(+2e), addend for addend. Complete safe $0 on every committed return; no committed line 18a moves.

Fact.Name: Earned income including all combat pay and any excluded territory self-employment income
Fact.Description:
/earnedIncomeWithAllCombatPay's own body, extracted UNCHANGED so the Schedule 8812 line-18a figure has a section 32 twin to stand against. It reads scheduleSE:/selfEmploymentEarnedIncome, which section 1402(a)(6) and (9) compute WITHOUT regard to sections 933 and 931 respectively.
ITS ONE CONSUMER IS eitc:/hasEarnedIncome, and that is the whole reason it exists. That gate asks whether the filer had earned income FOR THE EITC, so it must not follow the section 24(d)(1)(B)(i) "taken into account in computing taxable income" filter that /earnedIncomeWithAllCombatPay now applies. Pointing it here rather than leaving it on the re-bodied path is what stops a section 931/933 exclusion from silently switching off an EITC gate on a Schedule 8812 authority, running in the taxpayer-ADVERSE direction.
NOT AN EXPORT SURFACE. Schedule 8812 line 18a is /earnedIncomeWithAllCombatPay, which keeps the mef flag and the PDF consumer; this fact is a building block beside it. The same two-path shape scheduleSE:/fullSelfEmploymentTaxDeduction takes beside scheduleSE:/selfEmploymentTaxDeduction, for the same reason and in the same unit family.
EQUAL TO /earnedIncomeWithAllCombatPay ON EVERY RETURN THAT EXCLUDES NOTHING - i.e. every committed return - and the equality is structural rather than arithmetical: the two self-employment addends differ only through scheduleC:/scheduleCExcludedTerritoryNetProfit, which is Complete $0 by its own double guard wherever it is unanswered. DIRECTION IF IT IS EVER READ BY A SCHEDULE 8812 CONSUMER BY MISTAKE: line 18a too large, additional child tax credit too large, taxpayer-FAVOURABLE. That is the defect this pair was split to fix; do not add an ACTC consumer here.
⚠ A FOURTH ADDEND is the STATUTORY EMPLOYEE ADD-BACK, /statutoryEmployeeWagesInEarnedIncome, on EIC Worksheet B Part 3's authority rather than Schedule 8812's, because this is the section 32 arm. The pair above stays EQUAL ON EVERY RETURN THAT EXCLUDES NOTHING: both take the same addend, from the same fact. Complete safe $0 on every committed return.

Fact.Name: Primary filer's ministerial W-2 salary also reported on Schedule SE, for Form 2441 earned income
Fact.Description: The amount Form 2441's earned income item 1(b) subtracts from Form 1040 line 1z for this filer: ministerial salary that is in W-2 box 1 and is ALSO reported on Schedule SE line 2. Item 2 then adds the Schedule SE line 3 amount (net of the line 15 deduction) back, so without this subtraction the salary would count twice. It mirrors scheduleSE:/primaryFilerScheduleSeMinisterW2SalaryIncluded from that module's exported writables: the entered salary, floored at $0, when it is answered and the filer does NOT hold an approved Form 4361; $0 otherwise, including when the salary is unanswered, because an exempt minister's salary never reaches Schedule SE and so is not "also reported" there. Church employee income (Schedule SE line 5a) is NOT subtracted here.

Fact.Name: Primary filer's Form 2441 earned income items 1 and 3, net of the item 1(b) clergy subtraction
Fact.Description: /primaryFilerEarnedIncomeBaseWithStatutoryEmployeeWages minus /cdccPrimaryFilerClergyWagesAlsoOnScheduleSe: the wage term every Form 2441 earned income chain (lines 4 and 5, lines 18 and 19, and the deemed-income actual figures) reads. The subtraction never exceeds a positive base, so an entered ministerial salary above the filer's wages cannot drive the term below $0, and the term equals the base exactly on every return with no ministerial salary on Schedule SE.

Item 2 then adds the Schedule SE line 3 amount (net of the line 15 deduction) back, so without this subtraction the salary would count twice. It mirrors scheduleSE:/secondaryFilerScheduleSeMinisterW2SalaryIncluded from that module's exported writables: the entered salary, floored at $0, when it is answered and the filer does NOT hold an approved Form 4361; $0 otherwise, including when the salary is unanswered, because an exempt minister's salary never reaches Schedule SE and so is not "also reported" there. On a return that is not married filing jointly it is $0, because line 5 then copies line 4 and the spouse has no line of her own. Church employee income (Schedule SE line 5a) is NOT subtracted here.
