Fact.Name: Primary filer's ACTUAL Form 2441 credit-side earned income, before any floor
Fact.Description:
The three-term sum that Form 2441 line 4 is built from — this filer's employer income subtotal, his combat pay election for the CREDIT side, and his own self-employment earned income NET OF LOSS — with NO floor of any kind applied.
WHY IT IS A NAMED FACT RATHER THAN AN INLINE Add, and the answer is that TWO different consumers need the same sum floored at two different points. /cdccPrimaryEarnedIncomeWithCombatPayForCredits floors it against the section 21(d)(2) deemed amount and $0; /cdccEarnedIncomePrimaryFilerLine4 must floor it against the same two AFTER adding the taxable dependent care benefits, because Form 2441 line 4's earned income is Form 1040 line 1z (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i2441.pdf, page 4) and line 1z carries line 1e, the taxable benefits Part III leaves in income. THE PRE-FLOOR SUM CANNOT BE RECOVERED FROM THE FLOORED FACT: max(a+b, d) is not a function of max(a, d) and b — with a=0, d=10, b=5 it gives 10, while a=10, d=10, b=5 gives 15 from identical inputs to the claimed function. So the extraction is forced, not stylistic.
THE SUM IS UNFLOORED ON PURPOSE AND A FLOORED VERSION WOULD BE A DIFFERENT, WRONG FIX. Form 2441's CAUTION box says "You must reduce your earned income by any loss from self-employment" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i2441.pdf, page 4), and a component floored at $0 cannot reduce anything; that is why the $0 floor sits on the line rather than on the self-employment component. With a the actual sum, b the taxable benefits and d the deemed amount, the statutory order is max(a+b, d, 0). A floored extraction would compute max(max(a,0)+b, d, 0) instead, and the two differ on exactly the population where a is NEGATIVE and b is positive — it would have replaced one over-statement with a smaller one and called it a fix. tests/nodes/ty2025/form2441/cdcc-credit-deemed-se-loss-with-benefits-and-months is drawn to be that case and separates all three readings: 5,000 as shipped before this unit, 4,000 under the floored draft, 1,000 under the statute.
VALUE-NEUTRAL BY CONSTRUCTION. Both arms of /cdccPrimaryEarnedIncomeWithCombatPayForCredits now read this fact under their existing GreaterOf, so that fact is byte-identical to what it computed before — which matters because cdcc:/flowShowCdccQualifyingPersonsLoop reads it DIRECTLY and must keep seeing the income section 21(d)(2) deems this filer to have.
TYPE/SIGN/ROUNDING: Dollar, integer cents, SIGNED — this fact may legitimately be negative, which is the whole reason it exists. Not Round-wrapped: neither consumer's arms were, and rounding here would move the rounding boundary of both. STATUTORY EMPLOYEE ADD-BACK. The wage term is now /primaryFilerEarnedIncomeBaseWithStatutoryEmployeeWages rather than the raw /primaryFilerEmployerIncomeSubtotalBase. Round 7 took a routed statutory employee's box 1 OUT of that base, because the printed instruction puts it on the linked Schedule C's line 1; Form 2441's Earned Income list prints its own item for it, item 3, "If you are filing Schedule C (Form 1040) as a statutory employee, the amount shown on line 1 of the schedule" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i2441.pdf, page 4). LINE 1, not line 31: the line 31 reaches this sum through the self-employment term, which is already $0 on a statutory business. Complete safe and equal to the base on every committed return. CLERGY SUBTRACTION: the wage term is read through the NetOfClergyWages fact, which takes earned income item 1(b)'s ministerial salary also reported on Schedule SE out of line 1z, so that salary is counted once (through the Schedule SE term) rather than twice.

Fact.Name: Secondary filer's ACTUAL Form 2441 credit-side earned income, before any floor
Fact.Description: The exact twin of /cdccPrimaryActualEarnedIncomeForCreditsUnfloored, which carries the full reading of why the sum is named, why it is unfloored, and why the pre-floor value cannot be recovered from the floored fact. Not repeated here. Complete-safe 0 on a non-MFJ return in each of its three terms, exactly as the floored fact it feeds. STATUTORY EMPLOYEE ADD-BACK. The wage term is now /secondaryFilerEarnedIncomeBaseWithStatutoryEmployeeWages rather than the raw /secondaryFilerEmployerIncomeSubtotalBase. Round 7 took a routed statutory employee's box 1 OUT of that base, because the printed instruction puts it on the linked Schedule C's line 1; Form 2441's Earned Income list prints its own item for it, item 3, "If you are filing Schedule C (Form 1040) as a statutory employee, the amount shown on line 1 of the schedule" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i2441.pdf, page 4). LINE 1, not line 31: the line 31 reaches this sum through the self-employment term, which is already $0 on a statutory business. Complete safe and equal to the base on every committed return. CLERGY SUBTRACTION: the wage term is read through the NetOfClergyWages fact, which takes earned income item 1(b)'s ministerial salary also reported on Schedule SE out of line 1z, so that salary is counted once (through the Schedule SE term) rather than twice.

Fact.Name: Primary filer's CDCC earned income for the credit, Form 2441 line 4
Fact.Description:
The primary filer's own earned income as Form 2441 line 4 defines it.
TWO ARMS, AND THE SECOND IS THE OLD BODY VERBATIM. Arm 1 substitutes the section 21(d)(2) DEEMED earned income for a filer who was a full-time student or was incapable of self-care: "These rules for a spouse who was a student or disabled also apply to you if you were a student or disabled. For each month or part of a month you were a student or disabled, your earned income is considered to be at least $250 ($500 if you had two or more qualifying persons at any time during 2025). Enter that amount on line 4. If you also worked during that month, enter the higher of $250 (or $500) or your actual earned income for that month" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i2441.pdf, page 4). Arm 2 is the wage + combat-pay + self-employment sum floored at $0, character for character as it stood, so every return that does not answer the months question keeps its exact pre-fill value.
ARM 1 IS A JOINT-RETURN RULE, and the i2441 sentence quoted above does not say so. IRC section 21(d)(2) is written entirely in SPOUSE terms — "In the case of a spouse who is a student or a qualifying individual described in subsection (b)(1)(C) ... such spouse shall be deemed ... to have earned income of not less than" — and its flush text ("In the case of any husband and wife, this paragraph shall apply with respect to only one spouse for any one month") presupposes a married couple. Pub. 503 supplies the missing condition in as many words: "If you are filing a joint return, this rule also applies to you. You can be treated as having earned income for any month you are a full-time student or not able to care for yourself" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/p503.pdf, page 4). An unmarried filer has no spouse for the rule to operate on, and section 21(d)(1)(A) makes their earned-income limitation simply their own earned income. So arm 1 carries an isFilingStatusMFJ conjunct. WITHOUT IT the defect was REACHABLE, unlike every other deviation on this fact: cdcc:/knockoutStudentOrDisabled refuses the MFJ population that reaches these arms, but it does not fire for a Single or head-of-household filer, so an ungated arm 1 would have put a deemed floor on a FILABLE return — and /cdccEarnedIncomeLine5 copies line 4 for every non-MFJ status, so BOTH terms of the line-6 minimum would have carried it. Witnessed by tests/nodes/ty2025/form2441/cdcc-credit-deemed-non-mfj-denied, a head-of-household student whose deemed product resolves to 3,000 and whose line 4 still reads the actual 1,200.
THE CREDIT SIDE OF WHAT FRONTIER PACK 1 DID TO PART III, AND IT LANDS WITH ITS SIBLING. Form 2441 keeps two earned-income pairs: lines 18/19 size the dependent-care-benefit EXCLUSION and lines 4/5 size the CREDIT. Pack 1 deemed income on the Part III pair only and contracted this one. The instruction states the rule once for both spouses ("If filing jointly, figure your and your spouse's earned income separately. Enter your earned income on line 4 and your spouse's earned income on line 5", https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i2441.pdf, page 4) and line 6 takes the SMALLEST of lines 3, 4 and 5, so deeming on one chain and not the other would compute a minimum from two different rules. /cdccSecondaryEarnedIncomeWithCombatPayForCredits changes in the same commit for that reason.
THE ARM-1 GUARD IS THE IsComplete IDIOM, NOT A Placeholder, and it is the Part III twin's guard unchanged: a single IsComplete over /primaryFilerIncomeForMonthsDisabledOrInSchool covers BOTH of that product's operands, because the second one (/monthlyIncomeIfDisabledOrInSchool) is a Switch with no True fallback. The months > 0 conjunct keeps dormancy STRUCTURAL rather than an arithmetic coincidence.
DIRECTION OF WHAT THIS CORRECTS: before it, a student or disabled filer's line 4 read their actual earned income where the statute deems a floor, so line 6 — and the credit with it — was UNDER-stated. Taxpayer-adverse, never taxpayer-favourable. TYPE/SIGN/ROUNDING is unchanged: Dollar, integer cents, NON-NEGATIVE (the GreaterOf against $0 stays on both arms), and NEITHER arm is Round-wrapped — arm 2 never was, and wrapping arm 1 alone would make the two arms disagree about rounding for no reason the form states.
NOT UNFILABLE — THIS PARAGRAPH WAS FALSE AND IS CORRECTED. It used to read "cdcc:/knockoutStudentOrDisabled still refuses this population outright, so arm 1 is correct-but-unreachable on a filed return". That refusal's credits gate is GreaterThan(cdcc:/cdccQualifyingExpenseCap, cdcc:/lowerOfCdccEarnedIncomeMfj), and arm 1 deeming for the WHOLE YEAR lands EXACTLY on that cap — 12 x $250 = $3,000 with one qualifying person, 12 x $500 = $6,000 with two or more — so the strict comparison goes false and the refusal evaporates on precisely the returns arm 1 moves furthest. Arm 1 IS reachable on a filed return, and it was reachable the moment the credit-side fill landed. WHAT THAT EXPOSED, and what now contains it: with both spouses deemed, the two chains deem INDEPENDENTLY and nothing implements section 21(d)(2)'s flush text ("In the case of any husband and wife, this paragraph shall apply with respect to only one spouse for any one month", 26 U.S.C. 21, https://uscode.house.gov/view.xhtml?req=granuleid:USC-2024-title26-section21&num=0&edition=2024). A joint return with two qualifying children, both spouses students for 12 months and no actual earned income took a $1,200 credit where the best legal six-months-each split allows $600. cdcc:/knockoutBothSpousesDeemedStudentOrDisabled now refuses exactly that population, and carries the full derivation. The SINGLE-deemed-spouse shape is unaffected and still files — it always could, and this fill is what makes its lines 4 and 5 right.
THE COUPLING WITH cdcc:/knockoutStudentOrDisabled STANDS for what that refusal does still cover (a deemed amount BELOW the expense cap), so Part II and Part III agreeing remains the reason this fill landed with its sibling.

Fact.Name: Secondary filer's CDCC earned income for the credit, Form 2441 line 5
Fact.Description:
The secondary filer's own earned income as Form 2441 line 5 defines it.
TWO ARMS, AND THE SECOND IS THE OLD BODY VERBATIM — the exact twin of /cdccPrimaryEarnedIncomeWithCombatPayForCredits, which carries the full reading of the section 21(d)(2) deemed substitution, of the IsComplete guard, of the two provisional interpretations and of why the pair lands in ONE commit. Not repeated here. The spouse form of the rule is the one the FORM's own line 5 points at: "If married filing jointly, enter your spouse's earned income (if you or your spouse was a student or was disabled, see the instructions)" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f2441.pdf, page 1), and the instruction it sends the reader to is "For each month or part of a month your spouse was a student or was disabled, they are considered to have worked and earned income. Their earned income for each month is considered to be at least $250 ($500 if you had two or more qualifying persons at any time during 2025). Enter that amount on line 5. If your spouse also worked during that month, use the higher of $250 (or $500) or their actual earned income for that month" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i2441.pdf, page 4).
THIS IS THE LINE WHERE THE RULE ACTUALLY BITES, and it is not line 4's lesser sibling. Form 2441 line 6 takes the SMALLEST of lines 3, 4 and 5, so the population section 21(d)(2) exists for — one spouse working, the other a full-time student or incapable of self-care with little or no earned income — is exactly the population whose CREDIT is sized by THIS line. Deeming her income up is what unlocks the credit; deeming his up normally changes nothing. The same asymmetry the Part III twin records at line 20.
TYPE/SIGN/ROUNDING: Dollar, integer cents, NON-NEGATIVE, and neither arm is Round-wrapped — see the line-4 twin.

Fact.Name: CDCC Earned Income elections for primary filer
Fact.Description:
Earned income as defined for Child and Dependent Care Credit. Reported on Form 2441 line 4.
TWO ARMS, AND THE SECOND IS THE OLD BODY VERBATIM. Arm 1 applies the section 21(d)(2) deemed floor to the WHOLE of this line, which is what the printed rule says and what this fact did not do until now.
WHAT WAS WRONG AND HOW FAR IT REACHED. Form 2441 line 4's earned income is "The amount shown on Form 1040, 1040-SR, or 1040-NR, line 1z" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i2441.pdf, page 4), and line 1z carries line 1e — the taxable dependent care benefits Part III leaves in income. This fact adds that term one level ABOVE /cdccPrimaryEarnedIncomeWithCombatPayForCredits, which is where the deemed floor sat, so the graph computed max(wages + combat + SE, deemed) + taxable benefits where section 21(d)(2)'s "earned income of not less than $250" floors the whole. The two forms agree except when the student or disabled filer PERSONALLY received box-10 benefits, and there the line was OVER-stated — taxpayer-favourable, the one direction this repo treats most seriously. It was obligation (e) on cdcc:/knockoutStudentOrDisabled and is discharged here.
THE FIX IS AN ADDITIONAL FLOOR, NOT A MOVED ONE, and that is the trap this arm avoids. /cdccPrimaryEarnedIncomeWithCombatPayForCredits KEEPS its own deemed floor and is byte-identical to what it computed before, because cdcc:/flowShowCdccQualifyingPersonsLoop reads that fact DIRECTLY and a floor moved one level up would leave the gate that asks whether this population qualifies unable to see the income section 21(d)(2) deems them to have. So the unfloored three-term sum is extracted into /cdccPrimaryActualEarnedIncomeForCreditsUnfloored, both facts read it, and the $0 sits differently on the two arms here — ABOVE the benefits add on arm 1, below it on the preserved arm 2. That is deliberate and is the "arm 2 is the old body verbatim" discipline the whole cluster follows.
AND THE EXTRACTED SUM IS UNFLOORED, WHICH IS THE OTHER HALF OF THE FIX. With a the actual sum, b the taxable benefits and d the deemed amount, the statutory order is max(a+b, d, 0); a draft that floored the extraction would compute max(max(a,0)+b, d, 0) and the two differ whenever a is NEGATIVE and b is positive — Form 2441's CAUTION box requires the self-employment loss to reduce earned income, and a floored component cannot reduce anything. tests/nodes/ty2025/form2441/cdcc-credit-deemed-se-loss-with-benefits-and-months is drawn to separate all three: the 5,000 this line used to read, 4,000 under the floored draft, 1,000 under the statute, and 200 of over-claimed credit measured on that one return.
THE ARM-1 GUARD IS THIS CLUSTER'S, unchanged in shape and with the same limb conjunct all four deemed arms now carry: All(isFilingStatusMFJ, IsComplete of the deemed product, months > 0, /cdccPrimaryFilerIsStudentOrQualifyingIndividual). Arm 2 is byte-unchanged, so every return that does not answer the months question keeps its exact pre-fix value — which on the 704-store corpus is every return, none of which answers it.
TYPE/SIGN/ROUNDING is unchanged: Dollar, integer cents; both arms stay Round-wrapped, and the Round sits OUTSIDE the GreaterOf on arm 1 rather than inside it. That ordering is value-neutral, not a coin flip: Round is monotone non-decreasing and the deemed operand is a whole-dollar product, so Round(max(x, d, 0)) equals max(Round(x), d, 0). The outer position matches the Part III twins. California TY2025 reads this fact through its stateSystems export (FTB 3506).

THE MIRROR OF /cdccEarnedIncomePrimaryFilerLine4, which carries the full reading of the section 21(d)(2) floor spanning the whole line-1z amount, of why the floor is ADDITIONAL rather than moved, of why the extracted sum is unfloored, and of the Round ordering. Fact.Name: Primary filer earned income as defined for CDCC line 18
Fact.Description:
Earned income as defined for Child and Dependent Care Credit pay minus taxable dependent care benefits. Form 2441, line 18.
TWO ARMS, AND THE SECOND IS THE OLD BODY VERBATIM. Arm 1 substitutes the section 21(d)(2) DEEMED earned income for a filer who was a full-time student or was incapable of self-care: "For each month or part of a month you were a student or disabled, your earned income is considered to be at least $250 ($500 if you had two or more qualifying persons at any time during 2025) ... If you also worked during that month, enter the higher of $250 (or $500) or your actual earned income for that month" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i2441.pdf, page 4, under the heading "If You or Your Spouse Was a Student or Disabled" at line 242), and Part III inherits that rule by its own pointer — "If your spouse was a full-time student or disabled in 2025, see the instructions for lines 4 and 5, earlier" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i2441.pdf, page 5), which IRC section 129(b)(2) is the statutory form of. Arm 2 is the wage + combat-pay + self-employment sum floored at $0, character for character as it stood, so every return that does not answer the months question keeps its exact pre-fill value.
THE ARM-1 GUARD IS THE IsComplete IDIOM, NOT A Placeholder. /primaryFilerIncomeForMonthsDisabledOrInSchool is the product of filers:/primaryFiler/cdccMonthsDisabledOrInSchool and /monthlyIncomeIfDisabledOrInSchool, and that second operand is a Switch with NO True fallback (it is Incomplete when cdcc:/cdccCountOfQualifyingPersons is neither 1 nor more than 1), so a single IsComplete over the product covers both inputs at once. The months > 0 conjunct is kept so that dormancy is STRUCTURAL rather than an arithmetic coincidence: no corpus scenario answers the months writable, so arm 1 is unreachable across the whole corpus and this fill must land as an additions-only delta.
A THIRD CONJUNCT IS isFilingStatusMFJ. IRC section 129(b)(2) applies section 21(d)(2) only "in determining the earned income of a SPOUSE who is a student or incapable of caring for himself" (26 U.S.C. 129, https://uscode.house.gov/view.xhtml?req=granuleid:USC-2024-title26-section129&num=0&edition=2024), and section 129(b)(1)(A) gives an employee who is NOT married simply "the earned income of such employee" with no deemed rule available; i2441's own Part III routing agrees — its line-19 instruction offers the lines 4 and 5 pointer only on the "No, I am not considered unmarried" branch (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i2441.pdf, page 5 — the Line 19 heading, the "considered unmarried" test, and BOTH branches; the span this used to cite, 353-359, began inside the MFS routing and stopped mid-answer). Without the conjunct a Single or head-of-household student who answered the months writable took a deemed floor here, and /cdccEarnedIncomeLine19 copies this line for every non-MFJ status. The full statutory reading is on /cdccPrimaryEarnedIncomeWithCombatPayForCredits.
THIS FACT IS THE CONSUMER THE DEEMED-INCOME PAIR NEVER HAD. /primaryFilerIncomeForMonthsDisabledOrInSchool previously shipped with zero consumers; the scope-out token its Description carries said the rule was "commented-out and unimplemented", and it was neither — it was unconsumed.
WHAT THIS FILL DID NOT REACH WHEN IT LANDED, and what has changed since. (a) The CREDIT side is a DIFFERENT pair of facts: /cdccPrimaryEarnedIncomeWithCombatPayForCredits and /cdccSecondaryEarnedIncomeWithCombatPayForCredits are Form 2441 lines 4 and 5 and they feed /cdccLowerOfEarnedIncomeAndExpenses and the credit. THEY NOW CARRY THE SAME TWO-ARM RULE , so Parts I/II and Part III no longer read different rules — the sentence this replaces said they get "NO deemed substitution", which was true only until that fill. (b) The refusal cdcc:/knockoutStudentOrDisabled fires for PART of the MFJ population only: it does not fire for every MFJ return, so arm 1 remains filable there. That refusal's credits gate is a STRICT GreaterThan against cdcc:/cdccQualifyingExpenseCap, and full-year deeming lands exactly ON the cap ($3,000 with one qualifying person, $6,000 with two or more), so it evaporates on the returns arm 1 moves furthest. Arm 1 is reachable on a filed return. The both-spouses-deemed shape that exposed — two chains deeming independently against section 21(d)(2)'s one-spouse-per-month flush text — is now refused by cdcc:/knockoutBothSpousesDeemedStudentOrDisabled, which carries the derivation and the measured $1,200-against-$600 divergence. /knockoutStudentOrDisabled also does NOT fire for a non-MFJ filer, which is why the joint-return conjunct above is a correctness fix rather than a tidy-up. TYPE/SIGN/ROUNDING is unchanged: Dollar, integer cents, non-negative, whole dollars. STATUTORY EMPLOYEE ADD-BACK. The wage term is now /primaryFilerEarnedIncomeBaseWithStatutoryEmployeeWages rather than the raw /primaryFilerEmployerIncomeSubtotalBase. Round 7 took a routed statutory employee's box 1 OUT of that base, because the printed instruction puts it on the linked Schedule C's line 1; Form 2441's Earned Income list prints its own item for it, item 3, "If you are filing Schedule C (Form 1040) as a statutory employee, the amount shown on line 1 of the schedule" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i2441.pdf, page 4). LINE 1, not line 31: the line 31 reaches this sum through the self-employment term, which is already $0 on a statutory business. Complete safe and equal to the base on every committed return.

Fact.Name: Secondary filer earned income as defined for CDCC
Fact.Description:
Earned income as defined for Child and Dependent Care Credit minus dependent care benefits. This value is reported on part III, line 19 of form 2441 if MFJ, used to calculate CDCC. It includes the secondary filer's self-employment earned income, scheduleSE:/secondaryFilerSelfEmploymentEarnedIncome, her own computed line 3 less her own line 13 (retiring the two scope-notes this fact used to carry, oos-income-earned-income-schedule-se and oos-income-earned-income-schedule-c, which said that figure was left out "rather than guessing at a self-employment earned-income figure").
TWO ARMS, AND THE SECOND IS THE OLD BODY VERBATIM — the exact twin of /cdccEarnedIncomePrimaryFilerLine18, which carries the full reading of the section 21(d)(2) deemed substitution, of the IsComplete guard, of the annual-versus-monthly interpretation and of what the fill does not reach. The two land in ONE unit because the instruction states the rule once for both spouses ("If filing jointly, figure your and your spouse's earned income separately. Enter your earned income on line 18 and your spouse's earned income on line 19", https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i2441.pdf, page 5): substituting deemed income on one chain and not the other would print a Form 2441 whose two Part III lines follow different rules.
THIS IS THE LINE WHERE THE RULE ACTUALLY BITES, and it is not the lesser sibling of line 18. Form 2441 line 20 takes the SMALLER of the two Part III lines, so the population section 21(d)(2) exists for — one spouse working, the other a full-time student or incapable of self-care with little or no earned income — is exactly the population whose exclusion cap is set by THIS line. Deeming her income up is what unlocks the exclusion; deeming his up normally changes nothing.
THE DIRECTION IS NOT SIMPLY TAXPAYER-FAVOURABLE, AND IT IS REGION-DEPENDENT. A larger exclusion is a smaller AGI, but the benefits this line excludes are ALSO earned income for the EIC and the additional child tax credit (Form 2441 line 26 is Form 1040 line 1e, inside line 1z), so the same dollars leave /eitcEarnedIncomeBase. Which way the refund then moves depends on WHERE on the EIC curve the return sits: in the PHASE-IN a smaller earned income is a smaller EIC; in the PHASE-OUT it is a LARGER one; and on the PLATEAU between them the EIC does not move at all. The general claim is therefore a direction only once the region is named — and the ACTC leg has no such ambiguity, since Schedule 8812 line 20 is a flat 15% of earned income over $2,500 and always moves with it.
THIS FIXTURE IS ON THE PLATEAU, which is the correction the pair's own numbers force. tests/nodes/ty2025/form2441/cdcc-deemed-income-student-spouse and its actual-arm twin move /eitcEarnedIncomeBase 8,000 -> 7,700, and with his elected combat pay the EIC lookup reads 12,700 against 13,000. BOTH land at the published maximum for one qualifying child, 4,328 (2025 EIC Table rows "12,700-12,750" and "13,000-13,050", https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040gi.pdf, page 51), so the EIC leg is INERT here — by a single $50 row, since the row below prints 4,310. The whole of the $45 by which /overpayment falls (5,963 -> 5,918) is the ACTC: 15% of (12,700 - 2,500) = 1,530 against 15% of (13,000 - 2,500) = 1,575. Both arms' assert files pin /eitcEarnedIncomeBase, /earnedIncomeCredit, /earnedIncomeWithAllCombatPay and /additionalCtc, so this paragraph is falsifiable rather than narrative: pinning one arm would pin a value, pinning both pins the DELTA, which is what the claim is about. STATUTORY EMPLOYEE ADD-BACK. The wage term is now /secondaryFilerEarnedIncomeBaseWithStatutoryEmployeeWages rather than the raw /secondaryFilerEmployerIncomeSubtotalBase. Round 7 took a routed statutory employee's box 1 OUT of that base, because the printed instruction puts it on the linked Schedule C's line 1; Form 2441's Earned Income list prints its own item for it, item 3, "If you are filing Schedule C (Form 1040) as a statutory employee, the amount shown on line 1 of the schedule" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i2441.pdf, page 4). LINE 1, not line 31: the line 31 reaches this sum through the self-employment term, which is already $0 on a statutory business. Complete safe and equal to the base on every committed return.

Fact.Name: The section 21(d)(2) deemed monthly rate - $250, or $500 by the qualifying-person count
Fact.Description:
The rate to use per month as income for a taxpayer or spouse who was disabled or a student. This is dependent on if they have one or more than one qualifying person for CDCC.
The rate is EXPORTED because the section 21(d)(2) intake screens must show the filer WHICH rate applies to them: "did you earn more than the deemed amount in any qualifying month" is unanswerable without the amount. cdcc:/cdccCountOfQualifyingPersons is exported too, so a consumer could select $250 against $500 for itself — but that would be re-deriving IRC section 21(c)'s dollar-limit test outside this dictionary. Exporting the rate lets the screen READ the number this dictionary already computed.

Fact.Name: Primary filer's section 21(d)(2) figure — exact where the filer can answer, deemed product otherwise
Fact.Description:
The operand the four Form 2441 deemed arms read. It is the EXACT month-by-month figure when the filer has answered the stage-3 screening pair, and the pre-stage deemed product (/primaryFilerIncomeForMonthsDisabledOrInSchool) otherwise.
THE EXACT ARM, AND WHY IT IS EXACT RATHER THAN CLOSER. Printed line 4 is the sum over QUALIFYING months of max(rate, that month's actual) plus the sum over the remaining months of actual earned income. When filers:/filers/*/cdccEarnedOverDeemedRateInAnyQualifyingMonth is FALSE, every qualifying month's actual is at or below the rate, so the first sum is exactly the deemed product; and the second sum is the year's earned income less what was earned during those months, which filers:/filers/*/cdccEarnedIncomeDuringQualifyingMonths supplies. So this arm is deemedProduct + (annualUnfloored - earnedDuringQualifyingMonths), with no attribution assumed and nothing rounded.
THIS CLOSES OBLIGATION (b), the annual-versus-monthly under-statement this module has carried as a disclosed taxpayer-ADVERSE deviation. The pre-stage shape is GreaterOf(annual, deemedProduct), which on the contract's own witness — six qualifying months at $250 with $1,200 earned in the OTHER six — returns 1,500 where the printed rule gives 6 x 250 + 1,200 = 2,700. That 1,200 gap was measured, disclosed, and accepted as irreducible. It is neither irreducible nor accepted any more.
WHY THE ARMS NEED NO RESTRUCTURING, which is what keeps this stage small. Each arm is already GreaterOf(actualUnfloored, thisOperand, $0), and on the exact arm this figure DOMINATES both other operands: it is at least the annual actual (because the money earned during qualifying months is at most the deemed product when the boolean is false), and it is at least the deemed product (because earnings during those months are at most the year's earnings). Verified numerically before authoring. So the GreaterOf still selects correctly, section 21(d)(2)'s "not less than" floor is preserved by that same GreaterOf, and every arm inherits the exact figure by reading one changed operand.
THE GUARD IS TOTAL. All(IsComplete(boolean), Not(boolean), IsComplete(earnedDuring)) — IsComplete always returns a Complete boolean, so this Switch can never manufacture a Placeholder on its When. A TRUE boolean takes the fallback deliberately: that filer's figure is NOT computable from these inputs, needs the per-month amounts, and is the only population cdcc:/knockoutStudentOrDisabled still has to guard after this stage.
TYPE/SIGN/ROUNDING: Dollar, integer cents; no rounding. Not floored here — the arms' own GreaterOf against $0 owns the floor, exactly as before. The exact arms require the reported student/disabled month set to match the allocated deemed-month set; otherwise the existing approximate operand and refusal remain in force.

The derivation, the proof that the exact figure dominates both other GreaterOf operands, and the reason a TRUE screening boolean takes the fallback are stated on the primary twin and are not repeated here.

WHY THIS FACT IS THE RETIREMENT CONDITION. cdcc:/knockoutStudentOrDisabled was never about students or disability; it was about a computation the dictionary could not do correctly. Every earlier phrasing framed the bar as populations to exclude. The honest phrasing is the negation of THIS fact — refuse exactly where the figure is inexact, file everywhere else.
TOTAL BY CONSTRUCTION. Every term is an IsComplete or a Not over one, and IsComplete always returns a Complete boolean, so this fact is never Incomplete and never a Placeholder. That property is what lets the refusal use it without changing the completeness of anything it guards. The exact arms require the reported student/disabled month set to match the allocated deemed-month set; otherwise the existing approximate operand and refusal remain in force.

Round 7 took a routed statutory employee's box 1 OUT of that base, because the printed instruction puts it on the linked Schedule C's line 1; Form 2441's Earned Income list prints its own item for it, item 3, "If you are filing Schedule C (Form 1040) as a statutory employee, the amount shown on line 1 of the schedule" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i2441.pdf, page 4). LINE 1, not line 31: the line 31 reaches this sum through the self-employment term, which is already $0 on a statutory business. Complete safe and equal to the base on every committed return. The exact arms require the reported student/disabled month set to match the allocated deemed-month set; otherwise the existing approximate operand and refusal remain in force.

Fact.Name: Primary filer's section 21(d)(2) qualifying months, per limb
Fact.Description:
The months on which this filer is deemed to have earned income, computed from the PER-LIMB partition when it is answered and falling back to the conflated count when it is not.
THE ARITHMETIC, AND WHY THE ABODE GATE SITS ON ONE TERM ONLY. Section 21(d)(2) deems each month the filer "is a full-time student at an educational institution, or is such a qualifying individual", and "such a qualifying individual" is section 21(b)(1)(C) — which requires incapacity for self-care AND sharing the taxpayer's abode for more than half the year. The disjunction is therefore asymmetric: qualifying student months deem unconditionally, incapacity months deem only behind the abode test. So this fact is qualifyingStudentMonths + (abode ? admissibleUnableAndNotStudentMonths plus the overlap months when the student count is below five : 0). The gate is filers:/filers/*/cdccQualifyingPerson, which is exactly that (b)(1)(C) test and is the same gate /cdccPrimaryFilerIsStudentOrQualifyingIndividual already uses for this filer. A five-month student already counts the overlap in the student term, so the overlap term is zero and is not read. A sub-five-month student is not a section 21 student; their overlap months count only as disabled months, behind the same abode gate. Thus the three intake counts preserve the statutory disjunction without losing or double-counting overlap.
THE FALLBACK IS WHAT MAKES THIS ADDITIVE, and it is the CD3 idiom one level up. The guard is All(IsComplete(studentMonths), IsComplete(unableAndNotStudentMonths)), and IsComplete always returns a Complete boolean, so the Switch can never manufacture a Placeholder on its When. When the partition is unanswered, this fact resolves to filers:/primaryFiler/cdccMonthsDisabledOrInSchool unchanged. When it is answered, the student term uses cdccQualifyingStudentMonths and the abode-qualified disabled term uses the admissible disabled-only count plus the overlap only when the five-month student test fails. The overlap count is intentionally not in the outer completeness gate: it is required only on that sub-five-month, qualifying-person branch with at least one answered student month. A zero student-month count has no possible overlap and contributes zero without reading it. If unanswered or inadmissible when required, the nested count is Incomplete. A valid student or a filer who fails the abode test never reads the overlap count. Behind the abode gate, the student and disabled-only counts must also be individually admissible and sum to at most 12; the overlap count must be admissible and no greater than the student count when its branch applies.
WHAT THIS DOES NOT DECIDE: the one-spouse-per-month rule. This fact is the filer's OWN qualifying months; the flush-text split is applied by /primaryFilerDeemedMonthsAfterOverlapAllocation below, which reads this fact. Feeding the allocation rather than bypassing it is deliberate — the overlap machinery must see the per-limb count too, or a both-spouses return would allocate against the wrong totals.
TYPE/SIGN/ROUNDING: Int, months; no rounding.

Fact.Name: Secondary filer's section 21(d)(2) qualifying months, per limb
Fact.Description:
The secondary filer's twin of /primaryFilerCdccQualifyingMonths, same shape and same fallback: qualifyingStudentMonths + (abode ? admissibleUnableAndNotStudentMonths plus the overlap months when the five-month student test fails : 0) when the per-limb partition is answered, and filers:/secondaryFiler/cdccMonthsDisabledOrInSchool when it is not. The full derivation, the reason the abode gate rides on the incapacity term alone, and the partition property that makes the Add safe are stated on the primary twin and are not repeated here.
TYPE/SIGN/ROUNDING: Int, months; no rounding.

Fact.Name: Primary filer's deemable months after the section 21(d)(2) one-spouse-per-month split
Fact.Description:
The primary filer's own student-or-disabled months, less the months they SHARED with the secondary filer, plus the share of those shared months the return allocates back to them. Section 21(d)(2)'s flush text is "In the case of any husband and wife, this paragraph shall apply with respect to only one spouse for any one month" (26 U.S.C. 21, https://uscode.house.gov/view.xhtml?req=granuleid:USC-2024-title26-section21&num=0&edition=2024), restated as "If, in the same month, both you and your spouse were either students or disabled, only one of you can be treated as having earned income in that month under these rules" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i2441.pdf, page 4).
P - V + A, where P is filers:/primaryFiler/cdccMonthsDisabledOrInSchool, V is cdcc:/cdccMonthsBothSpousesStudentOrDisabled and A is cdcc:/cdccOverlappedMonthsAllocatedToPrimaryFiler. The twin subtracts A from the secondary filer's own count, so the two allocated counts sum to P + S - V — the size of the UNION of the two spouses' months — and no month is deemed twice. That identity is what the flush text asks for, and it holds for every A the validity gate admits.
WHY THIS FACT EXISTS RATHER THAN FOUR EDITS. Form 2441 lines 4, 5, 18 and 19 all reach the deemed amount through /primaryFilerIncomeForMonthsDisabledOrInSchool and its secondary twin, so changing the MONTHS operand of those two products applies one split to all four arms by construction. The same split on all four arms is therefore structural here rather than a property four separate bodies have to keep agreeing about.
THE FIFTH READER IS LINE B, AND THE SPLIT REACHES IT THROUGH THE SAME PRODUCTS — BUT NOT "FOR FREE", WHICH IS WHAT THIS PARAGRAPH FIRST CLAIMED. cdcc:/cdccEnteredDeemedIncomeForStudentOrDisabled decides whether the box is checked by asking whether each filed line is at or below that filer's deemed product, on the reading that under the shared arm-1 guard the line is never BELOW the product, so "not above it" is exactly "the deemed operand is what got entered". That reading rested on a premise this unit breaks: before it, the arm-1 guard (months above zero) implied the product was POSITIVE. It no longer does. A spouse whose allocated months are zero — exactly the case V = P with A = 0, all their student months shared and all given away — has a product of 0.00 while the guard still fires on their RAW count, so the test degenerates to "the line is zero" and would check the box for a filer who entered no deemed dollar. THE SHAPE IS UNREACHABLE ON A FILED RETURN rather than guarded: it needs that filer's actual earned income to be zero as well, which puts /lowerOfCdccEarnedIncomeMfj at zero, makes the strict GreaterThan in cdcc:/showSpecialEarnedIncomeKnockoutFlowInCredits true, and hands the return to cdcc:/knockoutStudentOrDisabled — the same bound cdcc:/knockoutBothSpousesDeemedStudentOrDisabled records, with the same residue (its shape (ii), both made-less questions left unanswered). Line B moves no dollar in any event, so the honest statement is a disclosure that could be over-checked on a return that cannot file, not a value defect. A SECOND BREACH OF THE SAME PREMISE IS CLOSED HERE TOO, recorded because this paragraph is where the premise is stated. Adding the section 21(d)(2) limb conjunct to all four arms (income:/cdccPrimaryFilerIsStudentOrQualifyingIndividual and its twin, obligation (f)) made the arms' guard STRICTLER than line B's copy of it, so a return with months answered but NEITHER limb took arm 2 — where the actual line may genuinely sit below the product — and that over-check was reachable rather than merely unfiled. cdcc:/cdccEnteredDeemedIncomeForStudentOrDisabled took the same conjunct in the same commit, which is what keeps the two guards agreeing; the witness is tests/nodes/ty2025/form2441/cdcc-deemed-months-without-student-status-refused. THE ZERO-MONTH SHAPE THIS PARAGRAPH DESCRIBES IS UNTOUCHED by that fix and remains as stated.
NON-NEGATIVE BY THE GATE, NOT BY A FLOOR. On the allocated arm the gate has already proven A at most V and V at most P, so P - V + A is at least zero and at most P; a GreaterOf against zero would be dead weight and would hide a gate defect rather than catch one.
COMPLETE EXACTLY WHERE THE RAW COUNT IS, which is the property the whole unit rests on. The fallback arm is a bare Dependency on filers:/primaryFiler/cdccMonthsDisabledOrInSchool, so when the overlap questions are unanswered — every scenario in the corpus, and every node-test fixture authored before this unit — this fact resolves to the raw count and the product, the four arms and their ~26 downstream consumers see byte-identical values. The gate itself is false-and-Complete corpus-wide (its four IsCompletes come first), so the Switch never goes Incomplete on the When. WHAT THE FALLBACK IS AND IS NOT. It is NOT a silent legalisation of the unrestricted both-deemed computation: a return with both months above zero and no proven release is refused by cdcc:/knockoutBothSpousesDeemedStudentOrDisabled, so the fallback is reachable on a FILED return only where there is nothing to allocate — one spouse with zero months, a proven-disjoint split, or a non-MFJ return whose arms are gated off anyway. An incoherent answer set (P = 0 with V = 3, say) also lands here, and the raw count is the right answer there for the same reason: with P = 0 no month is shared and none can be reallocated.
TYPE/SIGN/ROUNDING: Int, months; no rounding.

Fact.Name: Secondary filer's deemable months after the section 21(d)(2) one-spouse-per-month split
Fact.Description:
The secondary filer's own student-or-disabled months less the share of the SHARED months the return allocated to the primary filer: S - A. The full reading of the split, of why it sits on the two deemed products rather than on the four arms, of the non-negativity argument and of the fallback is on /primaryFilerDeemedMonthsAfterOverlapAllocation and is not repeated.
WHY IT IS S - A AND NOT S - V + (V - A), which is the same number written the way the twin is written. The secondary filer keeps her non-shared months (S - V) and takes the shared months the primary filer did not (V - A); the V cancels. One Subtract instead of a Subtract inside an Add, and one fewer place for the two facts to drift apart. The identity the flush text needs is still the pair's: the two allocated counts sum to P + S - V.
THIS IS THE CHAIN THE RULE USUALLY TURNS ON, the same asymmetry the deemed arms record. Form 2441 line 6 takes the SMALLEST of lines 3, 4 and 5 and line 20 the smallest of 17, 18 and 19, so on the population section 21(d)(2) exists for — one spouse working, the other a full-time student or incapable of self-care — the allocation moves the filed number through THIS side. Which is also why the allocation cannot be derived: see cdcc:/cdccOverlappedMonthsAllocatedToPrimaryFiler for the two worked returns whose optimal allocations sit at opposite ends of the range.
TYPE/SIGN/ROUNDING: Int, months; no rounding.

Total income assigned to primary filer for months they were disabled or in school. Used for CDCC. NO LONGER A DEAD END, AND NOW WITH TWO CONSUMERS: /cdccEarnedIncomePrimaryFilerLine18 (Form 2441 line 18, the exclusion side) and /cdccPrimaryEarnedIncomeWithCombatPayForCredits (Form 2441 line 4, the credit side) each read this fact on their section 21(d)(2) arm. WHAT IS STILL TRUE: it resolves in NO corpus scenario, because filers:/primaryFiler/cdccMonthsDisabledOrInSchool is never set, so the Multiply is Incomplete everywhere and both consuming arms are unreachable across the corpus. THE MONTHS OPERAND IS NO LONGER THAT WRITABLE DIRECTLY: it is /primaryFilerDeemedMonthsAfterOverlapAllocation, which applies section 21(d)(2)'s one-spouse-per-month split when the return has proven one and falls back to the raw writable otherwise — so the Incompleteness claim above is unchanged, and so is every resolved value in the corpus. Putting the split HERE is what gives all four deemed arms and Form 2441 line B the same allocation by construction. THAT GROUND IS SPENT: the coupled retirement IS shipped behaviour now — the refusal was rebodied to fire only where the section 21(d)(2) figure is inexact. The row's disposition is re-stated rather than left to be inferred: what this fact anchors is no longer a deferral waiting on a contract, it is the deemed PRODUCT term inside a computation that is now exact wherever the filer answers — see /{primary,secondary}FilerCdccDeemedOrExactFigure and its ForBenefits twins, which read this fact as their months-times-rate term. What remains genuinely out of scope on this rule is narrower and is disclosed on its own facts: the line 1b Conservation Reserve Program subtraction, the Part II optional methods, and the per-filer attribution of a return-level Schedule F. NOTE that both consuming arms are additionally gated on isFilingStatusMFJ — section 21(d)(2) is a spouse rule — so this product is inert on every non-MFJ return even if the months writable is answered.

Total income assigned to secondary filer for months they were disabled or in school. Used for CDCC. NO LONGER A DEAD END, AND NOW WITH TWO CONSUMERS: /cdccEarnedIncomeSecondaryFilerPartIII (Form 2441 line 19) and /cdccSecondaryEarnedIncomeWithCombatPayForCredits (Form 2441 line 5) each read this fact on their section 21(d)(2) arm — and this is the chain the rule usually turns on, since Form 2441 line 20 takes the SMALLER of the two Part III lines and line 6 the SMALLEST of lines 3, 4 and 5. STILL TRUE: it resolves in NO corpus scenario, because filers:/secondaryFiler/cdccMonthsDisabledOrInSchool is never set. ITS MONTHS OPERAND IS NOW /secondaryFilerDeemedMonthsAfterOverlapAllocation, the section 21(d)(2) split with a fallback to that same writable — see the primary-filer twin for the full reading and for why the Incompleteness claim is unchanged. Both consuming arms are additionally gated on isFilingStatusMFJ.

Fact.Name: Primary filer is the section 21(d)(2) limb — a student, or a (b)(1)(C) qualifying individual
Fact.Description:
WHICH FILERS SECTION 21(d)(2) ACTUALLY REACHES, read off the statute's own words rather than off the months writable. The deemed-income rule applies "In the case of a spouse who is a student or a qualifying individual described in subsection (b)(1)(C)" (26 U.S.C. 21, https://uscode.house.gov/view.xhtml?req=granuleid:USC-2024-title26-section21&num=0&edition=2024), and (b)(1)(C) is "the spouse of the taxpayer, if the spouse is physically or mentally incapable of caring for himself or herself and who has the same principal place of abode as the taxpayer for more than one-half of such taxable year" (26 U.S.C. 21, https://uscode.house.gov/view.xhtml?req=granuleid:USC-2024-title26-section21&num=0&edition=2024). Until this fact landed, the four deemed arms tested only All(MFJ, IsComplete of the deemed product, months > 0) and so deemed income on nothing but an Int — that is obligation (f) on cdcc:/knockoutStudentOrDisabled, and this fact is its fix.
THE TWO LIMBS ARE SEPARATE WRITABLES EVEN THOUGH THE MONTHS ARE NOT. filers:/filers/*/cdccMonthsDisabledOrInSchool is ONE Int that conflates student months with disabled months, and that conflation is real; but /filers/*/isStudent and /filers/*/isDisabled are two independent Booleans, so the LIMB is decidable per filer even where the MONTH is not. That is what makes an honest partial possible where the obligation text said none was.
THE ABODE CONDITION SITS ON THE DISABLED LIMB ONLY, AND THAT ASYMMETRY IS PRINTED, not inferred. Pub. 503 lists the rule as two numbered items — "1. A full-time student, or" and "2. Physically or mentally not able to care for themselves." — and attaches "(Your spouse must also live with you for more than half the year.)" to item 2 and NOT to item 1 (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/p503.pdf, page 4). The student arm requires the exported isStudentOrDisabled status, the explicit isStudent answer, and the five-month test; the latter two keep this arm student-only because isStudentOrDisabled also includes disabled filers. The disabled arm is filers:/filers/*/cdccQualifyingPerson, which IS the (b)(1)(C) predicate already: All(IsComplete(isDisabled), isDisabled, treatAsMFJ, Any(lived together all year, the more-than-six-months option)).
FOUR POPULATIONS, THREE CLOSED AND ONE NAMED. Student and not disabled: isStudent true and the five-month test passes, so the arm deems. Disabled and not a student: the abode test now binds. Neither: the arm no longer deems on an Int alone. BOTH a student and disabled: isStudent carries the Any when the five-month test passes, so student months still deem even where abode fails — THE RESIDUAL, named rather than closed. Turning it into a new refusal is a different unit's decision, deliberately not taken here. THE RESIDUAL IS CONTAINED AND WITNESSED, and the ground for leaving it open is no longer the one first written here. That ground read "closing it needs the months writable split by limb, which is a SERVICE-side intake shape (invariant #7)"; the BUILD-FIRST directive converts exactly that class, so the deciding facts were said to be instead "that an honest split redefines filers:/filers/*/cdccMonthsDisabledOrInSchool, declared in filers.xml, and that a second months writable beside the shipping conflated Int is two intakes for one question". THAT SECOND GROUND IS SPENT TOO: the filers.xml grant's boundary half is now named, and the deciding fact is now a SOURCE fact rather than a graph fact: NO PRINTED INSTRUMENT ASKS A PER-LIMB MONTHS FIGURE. Form 2441 collects no months figure at all; the instructions ask one count for "each month or part of a month your spouse was a student or was disabled" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i2441.pdf, page 4); the statute deems per month "during which such spouse is a full-time student ... or is such a qualifying individual" (26 U.S.C. 21, https://uscode.house.gov/view.xhtml?req=granuleid:USC-2024-title26-section21&num=0&edition=2024); and Pub. 503's Jim and Sharon example unrolls the printed algorithm as ONE count times the rate, 11 times $250 = $2,750 (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/p503.pdf, page 12). Pub. 503 is also the instrument that enumerates the two limbs as items 1 and 2 and still asks a single count over their disjunction (lines 262-267), which is the sharpest form of the point: the printed RULE is per-limb, carrying the abode parenthetical on item 2 alone, and the printed DATUM is one number. So this residual is IRREDUCIBLE FROM ANSWERED INPUTS, not merely unbuilt, and it is a disclosed deviation on the present printed intake rather than a closable gap. The derivation, the reason a naive per-limb pair of counts cannot reconstruct this Int's meaning, and the two things that would reopen the question are on filers:/filers/*/cdccMonthsDisabledOrInSchool itself. The witness is tests/nodes/ty2025/form2441/cdcc-deemed-both-limbs-abode-failed-residual, which is the abode-unapplied fixture with this fact's isStudent operand alone flipped true: the conjunct goes true, all six months deem, and cdcc:/knockoutStudentOrDisabled and flow:/flowIsKnockedOut are asserted true on the same return, so the exposure is contained rather than merely named. The same fixture's transcript carries, not asserted, the two month attributions that bracket the shipped figure in OPPOSITE directions — one where the annual form over-states by 300 (this residual) and one where the printed month-by-month rule would give 1,200 more (obligation (b)) — which is why neither is reachable from a single conflated Int.
COMPLETE-SAFE BY CONSTRUCTION, and this was the harder half. The student and disabled predicates can be Incomplete: isStudent is a bare Writable that three of the 704 corpus stores do not answer, isStudentOrDisabled may be Incomplete when neither limb resolves, and cdccQualifyingPerson is NOT complete-safe either — its leading IsComplete covers isDisabled ALONE, so a return that answers isDisabled true, is MFJ, answers filers:/livedTogetherAllYearWithSpouse false and leaves /spouseLivedTogetherMonths unanswered takes the inner Any Incomplete and the whole fact with it. That is exactly the population this conjunct exists to catch, so a bare Any over the two would go Incomplete and take the shipping line with it. Each arm is therefore wrapped All(IsComplete(x), x) for both external status predicates. All short-circuits on FALSE (AllOperator returns Complete(false) the moment any operand is Complete(false), whatever the others' completeness), so an Incomplete operand yields a definite false rather than propagating. The five-month predicate is itself complete-safe. The disabled-arm idiom is filers:/filers/*/cdccQualifyingPerson's own.
WHICH MFJ PREDICATE, said rather than left to a reader: the deemed arms keep testing filingStatus:/isFilingStatusMFJ, and cdccQualifyingPerson tests filingStatus:/treatAsMFJ. The two are not the same predicate and this unit did NOT unify them — the arms' own joint-return conjunct is unchanged, and the treatAsMFJ term reaches these arms only as an internal term of the (b)(1)(C) predicate, where it is that predicate's own reading.
SYMMETRIC ON BOTH CHAINS. Section 21(b)(1)(C)'s condition is a RELATION between the spouses ("the same principal place of abode as the taxpayer"): if they do not share an abode for more than half the year, neither is the other's (b)(1)(C) individual, and filers:/filers/*/cdccQualifyingPerson already reads it symmetrically with an SME note saying so. THE ASYMMETRIC READING IS NAMED AND NOT HIDDEN: Pub. 503 restates the abode condition on the SPOUSE limb and omits it from "If you are filing a joint return, this rule also applies to you" (lines 270-273), which can be read as making it vacuous on the taxpayer's own chain. Both readings are defensible; this fact takes the symmetric one and tests/nodes/ty2025/form2441/cdcc-deemed-disabled-spouse-abode-unapplied is its witness.
TYPE/SIGN/ROUNDING: Boolean; no rounding. Complete on every return.

Fact.Name: Secondary filer is the section 21(d)(2) limb — a student, or a (b)(1)(C) qualifying individual
Fact.Description: The exact twin of /cdccPrimaryFilerIsStudentOrQualifyingIndividual, which carries the full reading of section 21(d)(2)'s limb clause, of the printed Pub. 503 asymmetry, of the four populations and the named both-limbs residual, of the completeness idiom and of the treatAsMFJ-versus-isFilingStatusMFJ note. Not repeated here. This is the chain the rule usually turns on, since Form 2441 line 6 takes the SMALLEST of lines 3, 4 and 5 and the deeming spouse is normally the lower-earning one.

Fact.Name: 2025 gross income from all sources, including excluded territory income
Fact.Description:
The DENOMINATOR of the Publication 570 chapter 4 apportionment fraction: "Gross income from all sources (including excluded territory income)". Attested, because it is NOT DERIVABLE from anything this graph holds — the same finding /writableGrossIncomeFromAllSourcesFromPriorTaxYear records for the 2024 twin of this very quantity ("a SEPARATE attestation ... and not derivable from it"), reached there for the Form 2210 farmer/fisher test and reached again here independently.
WHY income:/totalIncome CANNOT STAND IN, stated because it is the obvious shortcut and it is wrong in a way no test on the committed corpus can catch. /totalIncome is Form 1040 line 9, TOTAL income, and gross income is neither of the two things line 9 mixes: capital LOSSES net into line 9 and gross income is never reduced by a loss; Schedule C, F and E enter line 9 as NET figures where gross income is receipts (this dictionary computes the gross figures separately - scheduleC:/scheduleCGrossIncome, scheduleF:/scheduleFGrossIncome, scheduleE:/rentalProperties/*/grossIncome - and line 9 reads none of them). The same attested figure also serves the Form 2210 farmer/fisher test: estimatedPayments /farmerFishermanTwoThirdsArmCurrentYear reads /grossIncomeFromAllSourcesCurrentYear, which is this writable floored at $0, so neither reader substitutes /totalIncome. Here the fraction MULTIPLIES the standard deduction, so a denominator that is too small would make the ratio too small and the deduction too LOW - taxpayer-adverse, and wrong for every filer in the population this exists to serve.
UNANSWERED IS SAFE AND IS TODAY'S BEHAVIOUR: /standardDeduction's guard resolves to the full deduction whenever this is Incomplete, so no return that never answers it moves. Min 0.
⚠ THE PUBLICATIONS' FRACTION IS A SIMPLIFICATION, AND THE CONTROLLING RULE IS ELSEWHERE. Found after a search for how this apportionment is handled in practice; it reframes every open question about the apportionment rather than answering one of them. 26 CFR section 1.933-1(c) disallows deductions "properly allocable to, or chargeable against, the amounts so excluded from gross income" and then says the allocation is governed by the rules of section 1.861-8 — the general allocation-and-apportionment regulation — NOT by a gross-income ratio. Publications 570 and 1321 print that ratio as a worked simplification for the common case; the regulation is the authority behind it. WHY THAT MATTERS HERE AND IS NOT PEDANTRY: the two questions this unit deliberately refused to guess — whether a charitable CARRYOVER takes the current year's fraction, and whether the state INCOME tax component of Schedule A line 5d is apportioned, fully disallowed or untouched — are exactly the questions section 1.861-8 exists to answer, by classifying each deduction as definitely related to a class of income or not. The publications are silent on both because their example does not reach them. So those are ANSWERABLE questions against a source this repo has not vendored, rather than genuine gaps in the authority, and that is a materially better position than "nothing printed settles it". BOTH REGULATIONS ARE VENDORED: 26 CFR 1.933-1, https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-26/section-1.933-1, whose paragraph (c) carries the disallowance and the cross-reference at lines 13-19 of the two-column extraction — "there will not be allowed as a deduction from gross income any items of expenses or losses or other deductions (except the deduction under section 151 ...), or any credit, properly allocable to, or chargeable against, the amounts so excluded from gross income. For purposes of the preceding sentence, the rules of section 1.861-8 will apply" — and 26 CFR 1.861-8, https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-26/section-1.861-8, whose own heading is at line 60 and whose "Deductions not definitely related" rule opens at lines 204-213. Both are the official GPO annual CFR edition revised as of April 1 2025, same flow as cfr26-1-469-2. There was no obstacle to vendoring them; they simply had not been fetched. NOTHING IN THIS UNIT CITES THEM FOR A COMPUTATION, and this paragraph is careful not to overclaim what having them settles. Section 1.861-8's machinery is written for the SOURCE-OF-INCOME and foreign-tax-credit context and is largely corporate — its state income tax treatment runs through unitary-business apportionment and a four-step methodology aimed at a consolidated return. Reading that onto an individual section 933 filer's Schedule A line 5d is itself an interpretation, not a lookup. So the honest position is: the questions this unit refused to guess now have a NAMED and VENDORED place to be answered, which is better than "nothing printed settles it" and weaker than "the answer is in hand". The current fraction remains what it always was — the publications' simplification, faithfully implemented, with its limits named.
TYPE/SIGN/ROUNDING: Dollar, integer cents, NON-NEGATIVE. interpretation:provisional.

Fact.Name: Gross income subject to U.S. income tax (Pub. 570 apportionment numerator)
Fact.Description:
The NUMERATOR of the Publication 570 chapter 4 fraction, "Gross income subject to U.S. income tax" = /writableGrossIncomeFromAllSources MINUS the section 933 and section 931 exclusions, floored at zero.
DERIVED RATHER THAN ATTESTED, and the publication's own worked example is why: it runs the fraction at 96,000 / 120,000 with 24,000 of excluded territory income, so the numerator IS the denominator less the exclusions and asking for it twice would invite the two answers to disagree (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/p570.pdf, page 34, the worked standard-deduction and Schedule A example). That is the one asymmetry with the 2024 twin in estimatedPayments, where BOTH figures are attested because that test's numerator is farming/fishing income - a different quantity, not a subtraction of this one.
INCOMPLETE WHEN THE DENOMINATOR IS UNANSWERED, deliberately: there is no honest $0 tail for a numerator whose whole meaning is a share of an unknown total, and a $0 tail would prorate every unanswered return's standard deduction to ZERO. The consumer guards with IsComplete instead - standardDeduction:/standardDeduction - which is the completeness-contagion idiom this dictionary uses everywhere else.
TYPE/SIGN/ROUNDING: Dollar, integer cents, NON-NEGATIVE (floored).

Fact.Name: Answered yes to the digital assets question
Fact.Description: True when the filer received a digital asset or sold, exchanged or otherwise disposed of one during the tax year. The printed question joins its two limbs with or, so the Yes box is the disjunction of the two intake facts rather than either one alone.

Fact.Name: Activity not engaged in for profit income (Schedule 1 line 8j)
Fact.Description: Amount reported for Schedule 1 line 8j, activity not engaged in for profit income.

Fact.Name: Form 1040 line 7b, the child's capital gain included in line 7a
Fact.Description: The amount printed in the entry space beside the Form 1040 line 7b "Includes child's capital gain or (loss)" box: "enter the amount from Form 8814, line 10, in the entry space" — form8814:/form8814TotalLine10CapitalGainDistributions, the child capital gain distributions the election includes on the parent's return, summed over the attached Forms 8814 (one printed space, however many forms). DERIVED from the shipping Form 8814 lines 6-12; it replaced the writable /writableChildCapitalGainIncludedInLine7a, whose Description said "No minimum of zero applies: the printed line says capital gain or loss and the figure may be negative" — true of the printed label, never of Form 8814 line 10, which is a product of floored amounts and cannot be negative, so the derived figure is never negative either. Whole dollars, complete-safe $0 on every return with no election. Printed whenever line 10 is nonzero, whichever route line 10 takes to line 7a (the direct route or through Schedule D line 13); the box beside it, /line7aIncludesChildCapitalGain, states why that reading was taken.

Fact.Name: Form 1040 line 3c box 1, the child's qualified dividends are included in line 3a
Fact.Description: Form 1040 line 3c box 1: "If you are including your child's qualified dividends in the total on line 3a, check box 1 on line 3c." True exactly when Form 8814 line 9 is nonzero across the attached Forms 8814 — form8814:/form8814TotalLine9QualifiedDividends greater than $0 — because line 9 IS the child's qualified dividends the election includes on line 3a, and it is the only Form 8814 figure that reaches line 3a. DERIVED from the shipping Form 8814 lines 6-12; it replaced the writable /writableChildDividendsIncludedInLine3a, whose "No Form 1099-DIV can carry this answer ... so it is a writable intake rather than a derived fact" was true until Form 8814 itself was modelled. Complete-safe False on every return with no election.

Fact.Name: Form 1040 line 3c box 2, the child's ordinary dividends are included in line 3b
Fact.Description: Form 1040 line 3c box 2: "If you are including your child's ordinary dividends in the total on line 3b, check box 2 on line 3c." IDENTICALLY TRUE WITH BOX 1, and this is a correction of what the writable it replaced said. /writableChildDividendsIncludedInLine3b described itself as "a separate answer from the line 3a box, because a child's ordinary dividends and qualified dividends land on different printed lines and either may be present without the other". On the form as printed that cannot happen: the ONE Form 8814 figure that reaches the parent's dividend lines is line 9, and the Line 9 instruction sends it to "lines 3a and 3b" — the child's non-qualified ordinary dividends never touch line 3b at all, they are inside line 12 and go to Schedule 1 line 8z. So the two boxes are checked together or not at all, and this fact is a direct alias of /childDividendsIncludedInLine3a rather than a second predicate that could drift from it (one quantity, one fact; two printed boxes). DERIVED.

Fact.Name: Form 1040 line 7b, line 7a includes the child's capital gain or (loss)
Fact.Description:
Form 1040 line 7b, the RIGHT box: "Includes child's capital gain or (loss)". True exactly when Form 8814 line 10 is nonzero across the attached Forms 8814 (form8814:/form8814TotalLine10CapitalGainDistributions greater than $0), and then /childCapitalGainIncludedInLine7a prints the amount beside it. DERIVED; it replaced the writable /writableLine7aIncludesChildCapitalGain.
INTERPRETATION, PROVISIONAL: the box is checked on EITHER route line 10 takes to line 7a. The Line 7b instruction conditions it only on "including your child's capital gain or (loss) in the total on line 7a", and line 7a includes line 10 whether it arrives directly (Schedule D not required) or through Schedule D line 13 and line 16. The narrower reading — check it only on the direct route, because the Schedule D route carries its own "Form 8814" note on the dotted line next to line 13 — was considered and not taken: the instruction does not say it, and a box checked once too often is a disclosure while a box left unchecked is an omission. Complete-safe False on every return with no election.

Fact.Name: Form 1040 line 1h, the type of other earned income

Fact.Name: Schedule 1 unnumbered 1099-K entry space, amount reported in error or for personal items sold at a loss

No information return in this dictionary carries the split between a correct 1099-K amount and an erroneous or personal-loss one, so the figure is attested by the filer. A minimum of zero applies because the printed space asks for an amount that was reported to the filer, which cannot be negative.

The filer's own entry for this printed line.
