Fact.Name: Schedule 1 line 14: moving expenses for members of the Armed Forces (filer entry)
Fact.Description:
Schedule 1 (Form 1040) line 14: the Form 3903 moving expense deduction a member of the Armed Forces on active duty who moves under military orders to a permanent change of station may claim as an adjustment to income.
QUESTION TEXT: "What is your Form 3903 moving expense deduction (line 5)?"
HELP TEXT: Form 3903 nets your actual, unreimbursed transportation, storage and travel costs (its lines 1 and 2) against any Form W-2 box 12 code P reimbursement (its line 4). Enter the result of Form 3903 line 5 here ONLY when your expenses were MORE than your code P reimbursement — "Subtract line 4 from line 3. Enter the result here and on Schedule 1 (Form 1040), line 14. This is your moving expense deduction." (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f3903.pdf txt lines 33-34, the form's printed line 5; the same rule in the instructions is https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i3903.pdf txt lines 148-150, the RIGHT column of a two-column extraction). If your code P reimbursement was equal to or more than your expenses, you have no deduction here — see the excess-reimbursement question instead (Form 1040 line 1h, /writableForm1040Line1hArmedForcesMovingExpenseExcessReimbursement).
ASKED WHEN: on a return where the filer indicates they have Form 3903 moving expenses to claim (typically alongside a positive Form W-2 box 12 code P amount, formW2s:/formW2s/*/armedForcesMovingExpenses, though a filer with unreimbursed costs and no code P entry may still have a deduction). Form 3903 IS now modeled (dictionary/ty2025/form3903.xml), so this hand entry is the FALLBACK only: /schedule1Line14ArmedForcesMovingExpensesOrZero prefers form3903:/form3903Line5DeductibleMovingExpenses whenever the Form 3903 attestation and lines 1, 2 and 4 are answered, and reads this writable only when they are not. The application asks this question only on a return that is not completing Form 3903 itself.
VALIDATION: Dollar, Min $0. No maximum.
UNANSWERED POSTURE: blank on the return; NOTHING IS REFUSED. /schedule1Line14ArmedForcesMovingExpensesOrZero is this writable's complete-safe wrapper, $0 when unanswered.
WHAT THE ANSWER FEEDS: /schedule1Line14ArmedForcesMovingExpensesOrZero → Schedule 1 line 26 → taxCalculations:/adjustmentsExcludingStudentLoanAndIra → /adjustmentsToIncome → /agi.

Fact.Name: Schedule 1 line 12, certain business expenses of reservists, performing artists and fee basis government officials, complete safe
Fact.Description: The complete safe wrapper of /writableSchedule1Line12ReservistPerformingArtistExpenses: the filer's Schedule 1 line 12 entry when it was answered, and $0 otherwise. It is read by taxCalculations:/adjustmentsExcludingStudentLoanAndIra, the Schedule 1 line 26 build up, which feeds /adjustmentsToIncome, /allowableAdjustmentsToIncome and /agi. The intake is a bare Writable, so a raw Dependency on it would make that subtotal, AGI and every MAGI built on AGI Incomplete on every return that did not answer this one optional line; this wrapper is the same complete safe Switch idiom the line 13 HSA and line 23 Archer MSA terms of that same Add already use. $0 on every committed scenario, because no committed scenario answers the intake, so the subtotal and AGI are byte identical. California TY2025 reads this fact through its stateSystems export (Schedule CA (540), Schedule CA (540NR)).

Fact.Name: Schedule 1 line 14, moving expenses for members of the Armed Forces, complete safe
Fact.Description: The complete safe wrapper of /writableSchedule1Line14ArmedForcesMovingExpenses: the filer's Schedule 1 line 14 entry when it was answered, and $0 otherwise. It is read by taxCalculations:/adjustmentsExcludingStudentLoanAndIra, the Schedule 1 line 26 build up, which feeds /adjustmentsToIncome, /allowableAdjustmentsToIncome and /agi. The intake is a bare Writable, so a raw Dependency on it would make that subtotal, AGI and every MAGI built on AGI Incomplete on every return that did not answer this one optional line; this wrapper is the same complete safe Switch idiom the line 13 HSA and line 23 Archer MSA terms of that same Add already use. When Form 3903 is answered it governs: its line 5 when the return files the form, and $0 when it does not (the permanent change of station certification answered No, or no expense or reimbursement), so a self-attested hand entry never reaches line 14 on a return whose Form 3903 says there is no deduction. The hand entry is read only on a return that does not answer Form 3903. California TY2025 reads this fact through its stateSystems export (Schedule CA (540), Schedule CA (540NR)).

Fact.Name: Form 1040 line 1h: excess Armed Forces moving expense reimbursement (filer entry)
Fact.Description:
Form 1040 line 1h: the part of a Form W-2 box 12 code P (Armed Forces moving expense) reimbursement that was MORE than the filer's actual moving expenses. Form 3903's own arithmetic nets the two: line 3 is the filer's actual transportation, storage and travel costs; line 4 is the box 12 code P reimbursement; when line 4 is at least as large as line 3, the excess (line 4 minus line 3) is not a deduction — it is gross income Form 3903 itself routes here rather than to Schedule 1 line 14, because it corresponds to no deductible moving expense and so is never a "qualified moving expense reimbursement" excluded by IRC 132(g) in the first place.
QUESTION TEXT: "Was your Form W-2 box 12 code P moving expense reimbursement more than your actual moving expenses? If so, enter the excess here."
HELP TEXT: "If line 3 is less than line 4, subtract line 3 from line 4 and include the result on Form 1040, 1040-SR, or 1040-NR, line 1h." (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f3903.pdf txt lines 30-31, the form's printed line 5; the whole of that printed line is txt lines 28-34). "Generally, if the total reimbursements or allowances that you receive from the government because of the move are more than your actual moving expenses, the government must include the excess in your wages on Form W-2. However, if any reimbursements or allowances … exceed the cost of moving and the excess isn't included in your wages on Form W-2, the excess still must be included in gross income on Form 1040, 1040-SR, or 1040-NR, line 1h." (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i3903.pdf, General Instructions: txt lines 69-71, the LEFT column of a two-column extraction, continuing at txt lines 4-10, the RIGHT column of the same page). Enter $0, or leave this blank, if your actual moving expenses were at least as much as your box 12 code P amount — use the Schedule 1 line 14 deduction question instead in that case.
ASKED WHEN: MUST BE ASKED on any return where a Form W-2 carries a positive box 12 code P amount (formW2s:/formW2s/*/armedForcesMovingExpenses). That is the whole gate, and it is deliberately a condition the return can see: the netting the answer reports is Form 3903's, which a return may leave uncompleted, so the interview cannot know in advance which of the two Form 3903 outcomes applies and must put the question to the filer whenever the box is answered. Ask it on the same screen as the sibling Schedule 1 line 14 deduction question (income:/writableSchedule1Line14ArmedForcesMovingExpenses), because Form 3903 line 5 is a strict either/or and the filer answers exactly one of the two: expenses more than the reimbursement is the deduction, the reimbursement at least as much as expenses is this income leg. There is no fact-graph gate on the question itself (matching the sibling writable's own shape); the obligation is an application screen-flow one.
VALIDATION: Dollar, Min $0. No maximum — the excess is not capped by anything on this return. ONE MORE CHECK THE APPLICATION SHOULD MAKE BEFORE SUBMIT, because the engine does not: Form 3903 line 5 is a strict either/or, so a positive answer here and a positive answer to income:/writableSchedule1Line14ArmedForcesMovingExpenses cannot both be right on the same return. WHEN FORM 3903 IS COMPLETED IN THE GRAPH the either/or is now ENFORCED, not merely asked of the application: both wrappers read the single Form 3903 netting (form3903:/form3903Line1hExcessReimbursement here, form3903:/form3903Line5DeductibleMovingExpenses on Schedule 1 line 14), and exactly one of those two is positive because they are GreaterOf(line3-line4,0) and GreaterOf(line4-line3,0) over the same two amounts. These hand entries are then the FALLBACK only, read on a return that does not complete Form 3903 itself; on such a return the two writables remain independent, ungated and self-attested, so the application should still refuse or warn on a return that answers both.
UNANSWERED POSTURE: blank on the return; NOTHING IS REFUSED. /form1040Line1hArmedForcesMovingExpenseExcessReimbursementOrZero is this writable's complete-safe wrapper, $0 when unanswered — the same posture as every other Form 1040 line 1h leg and the sibling Schedule 1 line 14 writable. UNANSWERED MEANS "no excess", and the printed instruction is what makes that the right default rather than an adverse one: where a reimbursement does exceed actual moving expenses, "the government must include the excess in your wages on Form W-2" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i3903.pdf, General Instructions), and Form 3903's own line 4 asks only for the amount "that is not included in box 1 of your Form W-2 (wages)" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f3903.pdf txt lines 24-26). So the ordinary excess is already inside box 1 and reaches Form 1040 line 1a and line 1z without this question being asked at all. This line exists for the residual case the instructions name next — the excess that "isn't included in your wages on Form W-2" and "still must be included in gross income on Form 1040, 1040-SR, or 1040-NR, line 1h" — which is a payer reporting error, not the ordinary code P return. A filer who leaves this blank when that residual case applies understates income by the excess; that risk is why the ASKED WHEN above is a must-ask on every positive code P amount.
WHAT THE ANSWER FEEDS: /form1040Line1hArmedForcesMovingExpenseExcessReimbursementOrZero, which is an addend of THREE facts, once each: (1) /otherEarnedIncome, which IS printed Form 1040 line 1h, so the answer appears on the printed form beside the disability-pension and IRC 402(g) excess-deferral legs and lines 1a through 1h foot to line 1z; (2) /employerIncomeSubtotal, printed Form 1040 line 1z, → /totalIncome → /agi and every MAGI this dictionary builds ON AGI; (3) /employerIncomeSubtotalDisregardingSection137, the parallel line 1z the two MAGIs that are NOT built on AGI read instead — the IRC 86 taxable-social-security modified AGI (socialSecurity), the IRC 219(g) IRA-deduction phaseout MAGI, and scheduleE. Those two are built on the parallel subtotal rather than on AGI to keep the dependency graph acyclic, so they see this leg only because it is wired there too; that fact and /employerIncomeSubtotal are the same quantity modulo the two line 1f adoption legs and must move together. It is NOT double counted anywhere: /employerIncomeSubtotal and /employerIncomeSubtotalDisregardingSection137 are built from the two PER-FILER bases, which read /primaryFilerOtherEarnedIncome and /secondaryFilerOtherEarnedIncome and never the /otherEarnedIncome total, so each subtotal carries the leg exactly once through its own direct dependency.
It also reaches /employerIncomeSubtotalWithoutCommunityPropertyAllocation on its non-allocation arm, so the EIC, additional child tax credit and standard-deduction earned income include it on every return except a community-property allocation return, whose earned-income arm sums the primary filer's base alone and so does not take this return-level leg. PER FILER: Form 2441 lines 4 and 5 and the IRA compensation of each spouse need the leg per filer ("figure your and your spouse's earned income separately", i2441 lines 252-255). /primaryFilerArmedForcesMovingExcessReimbursementShare and its secondary twin carry it into /primaryFilerEarnedIncomeBaseWithStatutoryEmployeeWages and its twin: the whole excess to the primary filer on a return that is not joint, and on a joint return to the spouse named by /writableForm1040Line1hArmedForcesMovingExcessRecipient.

Fact.Name: Form 1040 line 1h, excess Armed Forces moving expense reimbursement, complete safe
Fact.Description: The complete-safe wrapper of /writableForm1040Line1hArmedForcesMovingExpenseExcessReimbursement: the filer's answer when it was answered, and $0 otherwise. Read by exactly three facts, once each: /otherEarnedIncome (printed Form 1040 line 1h), /employerIncomeSubtotal (printed line 1z, the AGI chain) and /employerIncomeSubtotalDisregardingSection137 (the parallel line 1z the IRC 86 taxable social security MAGI, the IRC 219(g) IRA-deduction phaseout MAGI and scheduleE read instead of AGI). The two subtotals are built from the per-filer bases and never from /otherEarnedIncome, so nothing is counted twice. The intake is a bare Writable, so a raw Dependency on it would make line 1h, line 1z, AGI and every figure built from them Incomplete on every return that did not answer this one optional line; this wrapper is the same complete-safe Switch idiom the sibling /schedule1Line14ArmedForcesMovingExpensesOrZero and the line-13 HSA and line-23 Archer MSA terms of /adjustmentsExcludingStudentLoanAndIra already use. $0 on every scenario in scenarios/, none of which answers the intake, so line 1h, line 1z and AGI are byte identical there.

Fact.Name: Whose Form W-2 box 12 code P moving reimbursement the line 1h excess came from
Fact.Description: SCREEN. QUESTION TEXT: "Whose moving expense reimbursement (Form W-2 box 12 code P) was more than the moving expenses?" (a filer on this joint return). HELP TEXT: the excess of an Armed Forces moving reimbursement over the moving expenses is the earned income of the service member who received it; Form 2441 figures each spouse's earned income separately ("If filing jointly, figure your and your spouse's earned income separately", 2025 Instructions for Form 2441, Lines 4 and 5), and each spouse's IRA compensation is that spouse's own. ASKED WHEN: the return is married filing jointly and Form 1040 line 1h carries an excess Armed Forces moving reimbursement (/form1040Line1hArmedForcesMovingExpenseExcessReimbursementOrZero above $0). UNANSWERED: on that population each spouse's share of the excess (/primaryFilerArmedForcesMovingExcessReimbursementShare, /secondaryFilerArmedForcesMovingExcessReimbursementShare) is Incomplete, so Form 2441 lines 4 and 5 and both IRA compensations stay undecided; nothing is defaulted and line 1z, AGI and the EIC figure are unaffected (they take the excess whole). VALIDATION: one of the return's filers. FEEDS: the two share facts.

Fact.Name: Primary filer's share of the Form 1040 line 1h excess Armed Forces moving reimbursement
Fact.Description: The part of /form1040Line1hArmedForcesMovingExpenseExcessReimbursementOrZero that is the primary filer's earned income: all of it on a return that is not joint; on a joint return, all of it when /writableForm1040Line1hArmedForcesMovingExcessRecipient names the primary filer and $0 when it names the spouse; $0 on a joint return with no excess. Incomplete on a joint return with an excess whose recipient is unanswered. Read by /primaryFilerEarnedIncomeBaseWithStatutoryEmployeeWages (Form 2441 line 4 and the primary filer's IRA compensation).

Fact.Name: Secondary filer's share of the Form 1040 line 1h excess Armed Forces moving reimbursement
Fact.Description: The spouse twin of /primaryFilerArmedForcesMovingExcessReimbursementShare: $0 on a return that is not joint; on a joint return, all of the excess when /writableForm1040Line1hArmedForcesMovingExcessRecipient names the spouse and $0 when it names the primary filer; $0 with no excess; Incomplete on a joint return with an excess whose recipient is unanswered. Read by /secondaryFilerEarnedIncomeBaseWithStatutoryEmployeeWages (Form 2441 line 5 and the spouse's IRA compensation).

Fact.Name: Section 461(l) excess business loss adjustment (Schedule 1 line 8p)
Fact.Description: User response: the excess business loss adjustment from Form 461 line 16, reported on Schedule 1 line 8p. It is an add-back: the part of a business loss that section 461(l) disallows for the year is restored to income here. On a return whose only trade or business items are Schedules C, Form 461 is computed (scheduleC:/scheduleCForm461ExcessBusinessLoss) and this intake is not asked or read; on any other return (a Schedule E rental, a Schedule K-1 or a Schedule F as well) Form 461 lines 3 through 8 are not computed, so the figure is attested. A minimum of zero applies because the add-back is entered as a positive amount and line 8p is not a preprinted parentheses field. The 2025 Instructions for Form 1040 give the line its content (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040gi.pdf, the Schedule 1 line 8 block that begins at line 6595).

Fact.Name: Pension or annuity from a nonqualified deferred compensation plan or a nongovernmental section 457 plan (Schedule 1 line 8t)

Fact.Name: Digital assets received as ordinary income not reported elsewhere (Schedule 1 line 8v)
Fact.Description:
User response: ordinary income received in connection with digital assets that is not reported elsewhere on the return, reported on Schedule 1 line 8v. The instructions name forks, staking and mining as examples and exclude wages reported on line 1a, capital gain or loss reported on Form 8949 and Schedule D, and a gift or inheritance of digital assets. The income module already carries /receivedDigitalAssets and /disposedDigitalAssets, but those are the yes or no answers to the Form 1040 digital asset question and carry no amount, so neither reaches this printed line. A minimum of zero applies because line 8v is an income addend. The 2025 Instructions for Form 1040 give the line its content (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040gi.pdf, the Schedule 1 line 8 block that begins at line 6595).
This intake is also a FILING GATE: /knockoutDigitalAssetYesWithNothingReported refuses a return whose filer answered YES to limb (a) of the Form 1040 digital-asset question and left this intake unanswered, so the screen below is now the only way that filer reaches a filable return.
QUESTION TEXT, as it should be asked: "How much ordinary income did you receive in connection with digital assets in 2025 that is not already reported somewhere else on this return?"
HELP TEXT, paraphrasing the governing instruction with its cite: the 2025 Instructions for Form 1040 send here only the residue. "If you received ordinary income in connection with digital assets that isn't reported elsewhere on your return, see the instructions for Schedule 1, line 8v" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040gi.pdf, page 16). Everything reported elsewhere stays elsewhere: "If you received any digital asset as compensation for services or disposed of any digital asset that you held for sale to customers in a trade or business, you must report the income as you would report other income of the same type (for example, W-2 wages on Form 1040 or 1040-SR, line 1a, or inventory or services on Schedule C)" (lines 905-910). Typical amounts that DO belong here are mining, staking, hard-fork and reward or award receipts that no Form W-2 and no business return already carries.
ENTER ZERO IF ALL OF IT IS ALREADY REPORTED ELSEWHERE, and this sentence is the whole reason the screen exists in this shape. A filer paid in crypto as WAGES answers this screen $0, files, and the amount stays on line 1a where the instructions put it; the Schedule C receipt case is the same. ZERO IS AN ANSWER AND BLANK IS NOT: $0 satisfies the guard and files, blank refuses. A separate Boolean meaning "it is all reported elsewhere" was deliberately NOT minted, because it would re-derive a quantity this intake already carries (one quantity, one fact).
ASKED WHEN: /receivedDigitalAssets is answered TRUE. It is never asked of a filer who answered no or left the Form 1040 question blank, and a filer who answered only limb (b), the disposal limb, is not asked it either: that limb is gated by /writableNoUnenteredDigitalAssetDispositions instead.
UNANSWERED POSTURE: REFUSED for a received-yes filer (the residue named above), and IGNORED for everyone else. The printed cell IRS1040S1 f1_34 is bound to this intake directly, so an unanswered one leaves Schedule 1 line 8v BLANK on the printed form, which is right; the complete safe wrapper /schedule1Line8vIncomeOrZero supplies the hard $0 that Schedule 1 line 9 adds, so the total never goes Incomplete.
VALIDATION: Dollar, Min $0 (line 8v is an income addend and the printed line takes no negative), no Max.
WHAT THE ANSWER FEEDS: /schedule1Line8vIncomeOrZero, and through it /schedule1TotalOtherIncome (Schedule 1 line 9), /otherIncome and /schedule1Line10AdditionalIncome (Schedule 1 line 10), which prints at Form 1040 line 8 (IRS1040 f1_72) and reaches /totalIncome; and the printed Schedule 1 line 8v cell itself.

Fact.Name: Schedule 1 line 8e, the Form 8853 Section C long term care leg, complete safe
Fact.Description:
The complete safe wrapper of hsa:/form8853Line26TaxableLtcPayments, the printed Form 8853 line 26 taxable long term care payments: that amount when Section C resolves, and $0 otherwise. Form 8853 line 26 says "Also include this amount in the total on Schedule 1 (Form 1040), line 8e", and this wrapper is how /schedule1TotalOtherIncome honours that instruction, as a THIRD leg of the printed line 8e beside the Archer line 8 and Medicare Advantage line 12 legs.
THE WRAPPER IS NOT DECORATIVE. hsa:/form8853Line26TaxableLtcPayments is floored at $0 by a printed GreaterOf, but the subtraction under that floor reads Section C intakes that a return without a long term care insurance contract never answers, so the fact itself is Incomplete on such a return. A raw Dependency on it turns /schedule1TotalOtherIncome, /otherIncome, /totalIncome and everything downstream of them Incomplete on any return without a long term care insurance contract. The wrapper restores the complete safe posture every other leg of line 9 already has, and it carries $0 on every committed scenario because no committed scenario answers Section C, so the line 9 total is byte identical.
THIS DOES NOT END THE SECTION C DEFERRAL, which is recorded on hsa:/form8853Line26TaxableLtcPayments. Two obligations remain and both live outside the income module: hsa:/schedule1Line8eForm8853Income, the printed line 8e figure, needs the same third term so the printed cell and this total agree; and the IRS8853 render gate hsa:/archerMsaOnThisReturn needs a Section C arm, or the form still does not render for the policyholder who owes it.

Fact.Description: The secondary filer's twin of /primaryFilerW2sWithBox12CodeHAnswered.

Fact.Name: Form W-2 box 12 code H total for the return, the amount Schedule 1 line 24f is owed from
Fact.Description: The section 501(c)(18)(D) elective deferrals reported in box 12 with code H on the W-2s of the filers on this return: the primary filer's, plus the spouse's on a joint return only. Each amount is floored at $0 and the total is rounded to whole dollars, the unit line 24f is entered in. The W-2 instructions say the employee deducts this amount on Form 1040, and Pub. 525 puts that deduction on Schedule 1 line 24f subject to the IRC 219(b)(3) limit (the lesser of $7,000 or 25 percent of section 415(c)(3) compensation (W-2 box 1 of the code-H W-2s, IN-337)). Complete safe $0 on a return with no answered code H amount.

Fact.Name: The section 501(c)(18) deduction allowed for Schedule 1 line 24f
Fact.Description: The section 219(b)(3) allowed deduction for the return's section 501(c)(18)(D) contributions: iraDeduction:/primaryFiler501c18AllowedDeduction plus, on a joint return, iraDeduction:/secondaryFiler501c18AllowedDeduction, rounded to whole dollars as the code H total is. Each is the lesser of that filer's code H contributions, $7,000 and 25 percent of that filer's compensation (IRC 219(b)(3), 26 U.S.C. 219, https://uscode.house.gov/view.xhtml?req=granuleid:USC-2024-title26-section219&num=0&edition=2024; TAX-INTERPRETATIONS IN-301). /knockoutW2Box12CodeHNotDeductedOnSchedule1Line24f compares the line 24f entry with it (obligation IRA-024, reconciliation finding).

Fact.Name: Knockout: a Form W-2 box 12 code H deferral is not deducted on Schedule 1 line 24f
Fact.Description: SCREEN. Your Form W-2 shows an amount in box 12 with code H: elective deferrals to a section 501(c)(18)(D) pension plan. That amount is included in your box 1 wages, and you deduct it on Schedule 1 (Form 1040) line 24f, up to the lesser of $7,000 or 25 percent of your compensation. The line 24f amount on this return differs by $1 or more from the deduction this return figures from your W-2s under that limit, so this return cannot tell which figure is right. Enter the amount figured, or correct the W-2 or compensation entries. This return cannot be filed here until they agree. True when the code H total is above $0 and line 24f differs by $1 or more from /schedule1Line24fAllowedSection501c18Deduction, the section 219(b)(3) allowed amount (IRC 219(b)(3), 26 U.S.C. 219, https://uscode.house.gov/view.xhtml?req=granuleid:USC-2024-title26-section219&num=0&edition=2024: the lesser of the code H contributions, $7,000 and 25 percent of section 415(c)(3) compensation (W-2 box 1 of the code-H W-2s, IN-337); TAX-INTERPRETATIONS IN-301). An entry equal to the allowed amount files even when the code H total is larger, because the part above the limit is not deductible. The $1 tolerance is FACT-SKILL-1 2.4b (filer-entered against computed amounts; https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040gi.pdf, page 23). A reasoned refusal rather than a silent cap: line 24f is the filer's statement of the deduction claimed, and capping would file a figure the filer did not give (a project posture, not a tax rule). Complete false on every return with no code H amount. DUAL-WIRED: BlockSubmissionOnTrue plus membership in flow:/flowIsKnockedOut.

Fact.Name: Schedule 1 line 24f, contributions to section 501(c)(18)(D) pension plans, complete safe
Fact.Description: The complete safe wrapper of /writableSchedule1Line24fSection501c18DPensionContributions: the filer's entry when it was answered, $0 otherwise. The intake is a bare Writable, so an unanswered one is Incomplete and would carry that incompleteness into the Schedule 1 line 25 subtotal through the Add, leaving the printed line blank on every return that did not answer all twelve. Fact.Name: Required to file FinCEN Form 114 (FBAR)
Fact.Description: Schedule B line 7a, second question. Whether the filer, having a financial interest in or signature authority over a foreign financial account, is required to file FinCEN Form 114, the Report of Foreign Bank and Financial Accounts. Filer supplied rather than derived: the aggregate-value test behind it lives in 31 U.S.C. 5314 and its regulations, not in the Internal Revenue Code this dictionary computes from, so the graph records the answer instead of deriving it. Unanswered leaves both printed boxes of the question blank and changes no tax value.

Fact.Name: Schedule B line 7b, foreign account countries, first writing line
Fact.Description: Schedule B line 7b, the first of the two printed writing lines listing the names of the foreign countries where the filer's financial accounts are located. A faithful record field: it plays no part in any computation, and unanswered leaves the printed box blank. Not the same quantity as filers:/foreignCountryName, which is the filer's own mailing-address country. NO SCREEN ASKS THIS YET: the printed obligation is "If you are required to file FinCEN Form 114, list the name(s) of the foreign country or countries in the space provided on line 7b" (2025 Instructions for Schedule B, https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040sb.pdf, page 3), and since unit J1 narrowed the Part III knockout a below-threshold 7a-yes return FILES rather than being refused, so it prints this box blank until the application ships the screen (asked when income:/hasForeignAccounts is yes). Unanswered is a blank disclosure line on a filed return, NOT a refusal arm: gating the knockout on this writable being answered would re-refuse the whole freed population.

Fact.Name: Schedule B line 7b, foreign account countries, second writing line
Fact.Description: Schedule B line 7b, the second of the two printed writing lines listing the countries where the filer's financial accounts are located. Its own intake rather than an overflow of the first line, following the Form 2555 line 9 and line 15a precedent: the filler has no wrapped-text group, so a single String mapped to both boxes would print the whole answer twice. Plays no part in any computation and unanswered leaves the printed box blank.

Fact.Name: Form 1099-A tax treatment unavailable
Fact.Description: You entered a Form 1099-A, Acquisition or Abandonment of Secured Property. This return cannot yet figure the gain or loss on a lender's acquisition of your property or the canceled-debt income an abandonment can produce, so it cannot be filed here. Any entered Form 1099-A refuses, including one with unanswered boxes; a return with no Form 1099-A (an absent or empty list) is not refused. The form's own Instructions for Borrower say you may have reportable income or loss because of the acquisition or abandonment, measured against your adjusted basis and the debt canceled or the sale proceeds.

Fact.Name: Form 1099-K documents
Fact.Description: Source documents received on Form 1099-K, one item per received document. The collection records the printed document; its box 4 backup withholding is summed into /form1099KFederalIncomeTaxWithheld, a term of Form 1040 line 25b, and no other box reaches a federal line. Its items are available for state returns and document transcription.

Unanswered is complete-safe: nothing reads this fact. No federal line; carried for state returns and source-document identification. The printed source is https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-prior/f1099k--2024.pdf, page 2.

Fact.Name: This Form 1099-K's box 4 federal income tax withheld, or zero
Fact.Description: Box 4, Federal income tax withheld, on this Form 1099-K with cents intact, when box 4 is answered and the copy is not marked VOID; zero when box 4 is unanswered, when VOID is answered checked, and for a negative answer (the Min $0 limit on the writable is not enforced when a fact resolves, so the floor is here). No per-document rounding: /form1099KFederalIncomeTaxWithheld sums these and Form 1040 line 25b rounds its total once.

Fact.Name: Total Form 1099-K box 4 federal income tax withheld
Fact.Description: Sum of box 4 backup withholding over every Form 1099-K on the return, with cents intact: an addend of the Form 1040 line 25b total, taxCalculations:/form1099Withholding, which rounds once. A VOID copy adds nothing. No filer filter, as the Form 1099-NEC and Form 1099-DA totals: the return credits the withholding shown on every statement it lists, whichever spouse is the payee. An absent or empty list contributes zero.
